"A Christ-centered Courtship" er en serie taler om gudfryktig frieri preket av Paul Hershberger. Han preket disse talene flere ganger på forskjellige steder gjennom de siste ti årene. Nylig fikk vi dem transkribert og forkortet for klarhet ved lesing. Etter å ha trykt alle seks artiklene i The Heartbeat of the Remnant, vil vi gi dem ut i et hefte. Dette er den første artikkelen av seks.

Innledning

Min kone og jeg hadde privilegiet å ha et frieri uten anger eller skyld. Vi ble velsignet med foreldre som veiledet oss på rett vei og ga oss muligheter som de ikke hadde.

Hvis du ikke har det vitnesbyrdet eller minnet, vær så snill ikke å gå inn i en skyldfølelse. Men min bønn for deg er at du får et brennende ansvar og en visjon i ditt hjerte om å gi det videre til dine barn. Det kan være din belønning.

Et Kristus-sentrert frieri er en tidsperiode mellom et singelliv og et ekteskapsliv. Beslutningene du tar i denne perioden vil påvirke dere for resten av livet. Med Guds velsignelse over livet ditt kan du ende opp uten anger eller skyld.

Fem mål for denne serien om et Kristus-sentrert frieri.

Mål nr. 1. Å vende fedrenes hjerter til deres barn.

Mål nr. 2. Å vende barnas hjerter til deres fedre.

Mål nr. 3. At foreldre skulle få et ansvar for å lede hver av sine barn inn i Guds fullkomne vilje for deres liv.

Mål nr. 4. At unge mennesker skulle få et ansvar for å søke Gud, finne oppfyllelse og hensikt i å vandre med Gud, og at dere skulle søke modenhet i deres manerer og i deres karakter.

Mål nr. 5. At unge menn og unge kvinner skulle reise seg til å bli gudfryktige fedre og gudfryktige mødre med en visjon om å reise opp en ny gudfryktig generasjon, og at evangeliet om Jesus Kristus kan fortsette.

Guds plan for mann og kvinne

Forkynneren 12:1 says, “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them.” Min hensikt er at hver og en av dere skal huske deres Skaper i deres ungdoms dager. Vend ditt hjerte, ditt fokus og ditt liv for å søke etter din Skaper, den Allmektige Gud i himmelen.

Hva mener han med «while the evil days come not» og «the years draw nigh»? Det betyr å søke Herren når du er ung. Ta energien fra din ungdom og søk etter Gud. Unge mennesker, dere er unge og fulle av ideer, visjoner, planer og drømmer. Jeg tviler på at det er noen av dere som bare liker å sitte i en lenestol, legge opp føttene og bare drømme om hvor forferdelig livet kommer til å bli. Vi gjør ikke det, gjør vi? Men hvis vi ikke vandrer med Gud og følger Guds plan, vil harde ting komme over oss. Når harde ting kommer i livet, har vi ingen plass å vende oss til. Vi drømmer om at livet skal gå godt. Beslutningene og handlingene i vår ungdom påvirker oss for resten av livet. Den gode nyheten er at de kan påvirke oss positivt. Den dårlige nyheten er at de kan påvirke oss negativt. Det avhenger av hvilke beslutninger og valg vi tar. Men unge mennesker, dere er unge, og dere har muligheten til å velge.

La oss gå til begynnelsen i 1 Mosebok.

“And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him. And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field, and every fowl of the air; and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them: and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof. And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him. And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man. And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (1 Mosebok 2:18-24).

“And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth” (1 Mosebok 1:26-28).

“And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him” (1 Mosebok 2:18). «I will make him an help that is meet for him.» Gud sa at Han ville gjøre det.

“So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them” (1 Mosebok 1:27). Gud skapte. Gud skapte oss mann og kvinne. Det krever mye blind tro å tro at vi evolverte perfekt som mann og kvinne. Skapelsen av mann og kvinne er Guds plan. Det er ett av de levende bevisene på Skapelsen. Gud gjorde det. Gud skapte. Det er Guds plan. Gud er Forfatteren. Og Guds plan bringer velsignelse.

Jeg vil gjerne se på ti forskjellige aspekter av denne velsignelsen i Guds plan.

1) Gud fører Eva til Adam.

“And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man. And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man” (1 Mosebok 2:22-23).

Gud fikk Adam til å falle i en dyp søvn. Så skapte Gud Eva og førte henne til Adam. Adam våknet og skjønte: «Denne er for meg!» Han hadde sett alle dyrene gå forbi mens han gav dem navn. Nå gir Gud ham noen som er for ham. Han skjønte også: «Hun ble tatt ut av min side.» Hun er nær hans hjerte. «Dette er ben av mine ben og kjød av mitt kjød.» Det er ikke en hund; det er ikke en giraff, eller en ape. Denne som Gud førte til ham er lik ham. Guds plan har en velsignelse.

Adam og Eva hadde aldri hatt en ledsager før. Adam og Eva hadde aldri latt hjertets følelser gå foran. Noe skjedde i Adams og Evas hjerter. Adam var en «en-kvinne-mann», og Eva var en «en-mann-kvinne». De ga aldri sine hjertes lidenskaper til noen andre. Gud har den planen for oss også. Guds plan bringer velsignelser.

2) Å forlate og holde seg nær i enhet for livet.

“Therefore Bshall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (1 Mosebok 2:24).

Denne verset sier, «Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother,» men Adam og Eva hadde ikke en far og mor. Det Gud sier er at det ikke fungerer med sammenbinding med mindre det er et forlatelse. Også i Markus 10:7 leser vi, «For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife.» Dette er Guds plan, og Guds plan bringer velsignelse.

Å forlate betyr å legge igjen, å forlate. «For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother» er å forlate foreldrene, legge dem bak seg. La oss tenke på en ung mann som har et virkelig godt hjemmeliv. Han er velsignet og har alt han trenger. Likevel, når Gud bringer hans Eva inn i hans liv, reiser noe seg inne i ham, og han sier: «Jeg drar!» Men dette er Guds plan. Og Guds plan bringer velsignelse.

Det er ikke bare å forlate sin far og mor; han klistrer seg også til sin kone. Cleave betyr «å lime seg til, å feste seg». Vi kjenner godt til limte treplater. Alle slags solide møbler er laget av plater limt sammen. Og hvis de er limt riktig, kommer de ikke fra hverandre i leddene. Hvis du river dem fra hverandre, må du rive treet i stykker. Guds lim er på samme måte, hvor det limer to mennesker sammen. Den eneste måten å rive dem fra hverandre på er ved splintring og riving, og Gud velsigner ikke det. Men å forlate og klamre seg til, bli sammen og være limt sammen, det er Guds plan, og det bringer velsignelse.

3) De skal være ett kjød.

“Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (1 Mosebok 2:24). To single personer som blir ett ektepar, blir en enhet for Gud, og blir en familie for Gud. De blir ett kjød, der Gud ser dem sammen som ett.

“And they twain shall be one flesh: so then they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder” (Markus 10:8-9). Guds plan for mann og kvinne er at Han bringer Eva til Adam. Så skal det skje at de forlater og klamrer seg til hverandre. Han får dem til å bli ett kjød. Å dra dem fra hverandre er ingen velsignelse i det hele tatt, men fører til angst, smerte, fødselssmerter og skade. Det finnes ingen velsignelse i separasjon. Men Guds plan bringer velsignelse.

4) Ikke et ulikt åk.

“Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness” (2 Korinterbrev 6:14-15). “The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband liveth; but if her husband be dead, she is at liberty to be married to whom she will; only in the Lord” (1 Korinterbrev 7:39).

Guds plan er at ekteskapet er en lik tore. Gud vil ikke bringe en Eva til en Adam i et ekteskap som er en ulik åk. La oss tenke på å forlate og klamre seg, bli limt sammen, og to som blir ett. I ekteskapet er disse to nå ett for Gud. Forestill deg å være i et dårlig ekteskap som dette—en familie som prøver å fungere sammen. Det vil ikke være noen velsignelse.

Men et likt åk bringer velsignelse! Gud ønsker at vi skal være forenet i ett kjød, ett hjerte og ett sinn. Han vil se oss forenet i hjerte, sinn og kjød—hele vesenet, være ett. Guds plan bringer velsignelse.

5) Gud planla at vi skulle få barn.

“And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth” (1 Mosebok 1:28). Tenk på gleden og miraklet hver gang et nytt barn blir født inn i et kristent hjem. Gud planla det slik. Og hvis Gud brakte Adam hans Eva, og de forlater og klamrer seg til hverandre, blir de ett kjød, ett hjerte, ett sinn. Hvis de er likt åkede og Gud velsigner dem med barn, blir det et gledelig tilfluktssted hvor Gud kan bo. “And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth” (1 Mosebok 9:1). “And you, be ye fruitful, and multiply; bring forth abundantly in the earth, and multiply therein” (1 Mosebok 9:7). Guds plan bringer velsignelse.

6) Ledelsesorden.

“But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God” (1 Korinterbrev 11:3). Det er Gud, så Kristus, mannen og kvinnen. Gud etablerte en rangordning for lederskap, og denne rangordningen er en velsignelse. Det er Guds plan, og det er en velsignelse.

“Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honor thy father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise; That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth” (Efeserne 6:1-3). Barn, adlyd deres foreldre i Herren er en del av denne rangordningen. Dette er ikke vanskelig å forstå, er det vel? Et hjem som følger Guds plan er rett og slett en velsignet situasjon. Unge mennesker lærer å være under myndighet. Gjør det til deres høyeste prioritet. Jo raskere dere lærer å være under myndighet, jo bedre forberedt vil dere være for ansvarene i livet.

Jeg husker at jeg så på ekteskapet og hadde ambisjoner om å undervise barn og oppdra en gudfryktig familie. Jeg lyttet til «The Godly Home»-serien og trodde jeg var klar til å gå i gang. Men så kom dagen da det var min tur og mitt ansvar, og plutselig ønsket hjertet mitt å visne. Ansvar føles ikke som å drømme om det. DU trenger å gjøre noe! DU er ansvarlig. DU må få det til. Og, forresten, ikke bare få det til; du må få det til på en kristuslik måte. Du må få det til på en måte slik at Herrens Ånds unction kan komme over din familie. Jo bedre vi lærer å være under myndighet, jo bedre forberedt blir vi for disse ansvarene. Jo mer vi innser at vi trenger Gud, desto bedre er vi. La oss gjøre det til en høy prioritet å lære å være under myndighet som barn og som unge. “My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments: For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee” (Ordspråkene 3:1-2).

Gud vil gi sin velsignelse dersom vi forblir i denne rangordningen. Jo mer du lærer å være under myndighet, jo mer vil du bli velsignet når du etablerer ditt hjem. Guds plan har velsignelser.

7) Et gudfryktig ekteskap.

Efeserne 5:21,22,24 says, “Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God. Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. . . Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.”

Først se på vers 21, «submitting yourselves one to another.» Det må skje en sammensmelting i et gudfryktig hjem. Denne sammensmeltingen bør skje i gudsfrykt. Hvis vi underordner oss hverandre i gudsfrykt, kommer vi til å adlyde Gud fordi vi ønsker Hans velsignelser.

Efeserne 5: 22, 24 “Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. . . Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.” Unge damer, dere kan regne med det: underordning under far tilsvarer underordning under en ektemann. Dere kan øve mens dere er single. Dette vil hjelpe å bygge karakter i livet deres. Å være en opprørsk og egenrådig kvinne vil ikke bringe Guds velsignelse.

Det fortsetter i Efeserne 5:25,28,29. “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it . . . So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church.” Unge menn, dette sier at ektemenn skal elske sine koner. Så hvem tror dere Gud satte i livet deres for å forberede dere til å elske deres kone? Moren deres! Vil dere lære å elske deres kone? Lær å ha et godt forhold til moren, elsk moren og bry dere om henne. Vil du øve på å elske din fremtidige kone? Gå foran og elsk din mor.

Vers 33, “Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.” Guds plan bringer velsignelser.

8) Å være arvinger sammen av livets nåde.

1 Peter 3:7 “Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honor unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.” Som ektemenn gir vi ære til konen. Hun er det svakere kar, og den som bar barna! Hun har gått gjennom mange traumatiske forandringer i livet. Hun er den som blir utslitt og blir trøtt før mannen.

Og han sier, “Husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge.”

Unge menn, lær å forstå moren din og søstrene dine. Det vil hjelpe deg etter at du gifter deg. Ikke konkluder med at—ah, det er bare kvinner. Nei, du vil ha Guds velsignelse. Lær å kjenne og forstå dem.

“Being heirs together of the grace of life.” Gud vil at vi skal være arvinger sammen av livets nåde. Hvis vi ikke er arvinger sammen av livets nåde, kan vi være arvinger adskilt av livets nåde? Jeg tror ikke det. Han sier at vi skal være arvinger sammen slik at våre bønner ikke blir hindret. Så hvis vi er arvinger adskilt, kan vi si at våre bønner vil bli hindret? Ja, våre bønner vil bli hindret. La oss gi ære til konen som til det svakere kar. Hver eneste ounce du kan vinne på dette området vil bare velsigne deg senere. Det er verdt det. Guds plan bringer velsignelse.

9) Et velsignet og trygt hjem.

Dette kommer delvis fra 1 Peter 3:7, men også fra Salme 144:12 “That our sons may be as plants grown up in their youth; that our daughters may be as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace.” Guds nåde hviler over et trygt hjem hvor det er enhet. Hvor far forstår mor, hvor far bryr seg om mor. Far tjener og er der for å hjelpe og veilede. Han er der for å gi retning med et barmhjertig hjerte. Guds plan for mann og kvinne—Guds plan bringer velsignelser.

10) Som Kristus og kirken.

“Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing. Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish. So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church” (Efeserne 5:24-29).

“Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave Himself for it.” Gud ser etter menn som er villige til å gi sine liv. Single unge menn, er dere villige til å svare kallet og gi deres liv? Dette er et høyt kall fra Gud. Det er Guds plan.

Unge menn, er dere villige til å legge ned livet, agendaen og de uavhengige ting dere liker å gjøre? Er dere villige til å være tålmodige, milde og forståelsesfulle? Er dere villige til å miste søvn og fortsette selv når dere er trøtte? Er dere villige til å holde dere rolige og ikke reagere i stressede omstendigheter? Er dere villige til å lede og veilede en kone og barn, evige sjeler, gjennom dette livet?

Men min bønn er at dere vil melde dere frivillig og si, «Jeg er villig til å anvende meg på Guds Ord, Guds vilje, Guds plan, og jeg vil gi mitt liv. Jeg er villig til å legge det på alteret.» Jesus ga sitt liv for oss, og Han sammenligner ekteskapet med kirken og seg selv.

Det er også behov for mødre som er underdanige og overgitt under autoritet. Mødre som ikke følger kvinnesakskampen i vår tid, men snarere er fornøyde med å være hjemmeholdere.

Unge damer, er dere villige til å verve dere? Vil dere gi deres hjerte for å bli ledet og veiledet? Er dere villige til å følge og med glede underordne dere deres autoritet? Er dere villige til å tjene og bli brukt opp for familien deres? Er dere villige til å tjene og bli brukt opp for DIN familie? Hvis du gifter deg en dag, vil det være DIN familie du skal tjene og bli brukt opp for. Er du villig til å bære smerte og ubehag? Er du villig til å være en hjelpmeet, gi deg selv for hans byrde og visjon?

Men når vi ser på Guds plan og velsignelser, ønsker dere Guds velsignelse, unge mennesker! Men det betyr at dere må ta valg deretter. Reis dere og ta beslutninger som fører til modenhet. Modenhet kommer med prosessen å søke etter Gud. Forplikt dere i deres hjerte til å åpne dere for Guds velsignelser og prinsipper. Jeg oppmuntrer dere til å vandre med Gud, å ha et forhold til Jesus Kristus, og å gjøre det i ydmykhet.

Søk etter kristuslik karakter, og gjør det med hensikt. Det er så lett for oss å bare leve livet slik det skjer. Men hvis vi tar beslutninger med hensikt, vil det føre oss et sted! De beslutningene betyr noe. Gjør ting i henhold til Guds plan.

Gud har en plan for mann og kvinne, og han har en plan for deg.

Eight-year-old Jamin wasn’t very smart. Or at least that’s what his older brother told him. Almost daily, brother Kenny found ways to remind Jamin of his shortcomings and laugh at his blunders.

“Jamin, you will never be smart”, Kenny said. Deep inside Jamin felt resigned to a life of muddled trip-ups. Would he always be clumsy? Would he always say things wrong? That’s what Kenny said.

Jamin believed Kenny’s lectures with wide-eyed belief. Kenny was three years older than him, so he must be right. Very well, then Jamin would be simple. Kenny would be smart. Life was not fair. Dad and Mom disliked Kenny’s proud talk and punished him whenever they walked in on one of his speeches. But Kenny had a way of avoiding earshot. So he continued mocking Jamin.

Grandma Otto watched these trials from her rocker on the porch. She was a quiet old lady.

“Jamin, do you know where Kenny is?” Mom asked with a smile. “It’s almost supper time.”

“He went to check his coyote traps. I’ll go find him.”

There was a chill in the air as he tramped up over the lawn, and the sun was growing old as he crossed the border of the woods. The fleeting shadows scurried over the hills. The chill deepened as he stumped further in. He breathed the rich air and followed Kenny’s trail. Eventually, the trail would end up in a meadow, but Jamin hoped he would find Kenny before he had to go that far. The various traps had been checked already, so Jamin knew Kenny had come this way. Jamin trudged on resolutely. His golden head caught the tired beams that fled from the sun as they flickered through the trees. And soon those too had faded leaving behind the musky smell of the woods. The fall webworms had been at work, and their web curtains shuttered from branches overhead.

At length, as the trees subdued and thinned, and the meadow appeared Jamin knew this was the end of his brother’s trap route. If Kenny wasn’t here, he wouldn’t know where else to look.

But Kenny was there. As Jamin clumped into the meadow, he could see a frustrated heap to his right. The heap’s voice had a familiar ring. The heap’s face was lit in pain. The heap was Kenny. “Are you alright? What happened?” Jamin felt strange, seeing Kenny scrunched in the dirt. Kenny was smart. “Did you step in a trap?”

“Yes, Jamin. I..I wasn’t looking where I was going. Help me. Please.”

Jamin bent and found an ankle firmly held in the jaws of a steel trap. Darkness stained the ground around Kenny. Quickly, Jamin’s strong arms pried open the jaws. Kenny reeled free. “Can you walk?”

“Yes. I think so. If you support me, I can hobble along.”

“Dad and Mom will be worried. We’ve missed supper.”

Sure enough, as the brothers hobbled back through the woods, they heard the long calling of their father. Jamin called back, and he was by their side in a moment, seeing the ankle and scooping up Kenny like a hurt sheep. The odd little band hurried home, and the screen door banged shut as Dad swept across the porch. Jamin went to the wash house and scrubbed his hands. He headed for the front door.

“Jamin.” It was Grandma. The porch light showed her in her old rocker. A heavy comforter lay on her shoulders.

“Yes, Grandma?”

“Do you think you are not very smart?”

“That’s what Kenny says.” Jamin squirmed.

“You were strong enough to open the trap, and Kenny wasn’t. You were brave enough to find him in the dark. Lots of young boys wouldn’t be.” Jamin was silent. Grandma Otto rocked some more, then smiled. “God made you the way you are for a reason, Jamin. He made Kenny the way he is for a reason. He has a plan for you, and a place only you can fill, you know.”

Jamin turned and walked into the warm kitchen. He was smiling.

Восьмилетний Джамин вовсе не был очень умным. По крайней мере так говорил ему его старший брат. Почти каждый день Кенни находил способ напомнить Джамину о его недостатках и посмеяться над его промахами.

«Джамин, ты никогда не будешь умным», — говорил Кенни. В глубине души Джамин смирился с мыслью о жизни, полной запутанных неудач. Всегда ли он будет неуклюжим? Всегда ли он будет говорить не то? Так говорил Кенни.

Джамин с широко раскрытыми глазами верил лекциям Кенни. Кенни был на три года старше, значит, он должен быть прав. Ладно, тогда Джамин будет простаком. Кенни будет умным. Жизнь была несправедлива. Папа и мама не одобряли гордых речей Кенни и наказывали его всякий раз, когда они заходили и слышали его разговоры. Но Кенни умел уходить от их слуха. Так он продолжал насмехаться над Джамином.

Бабушка Отто наблюдала за этими испытаниями из своего кресла-качалки на веранде. Она была тихой старушкой.

«Джамин, ты знаешь, где Кенни?» — спросила мама с улыбкой. — «Уже почти время ужина».

«Он пошёл проверить капканы на койотов. Я пойду его найду».

По газону он шёл вразвалку, в воздухе стояла прохлада, и солнце уже садилось, когда он перешёл границу леса. Мимолётные тени сползали по холмам. Прохлада становилась глубже по мере того, как он продвигался дальше. Он вдыхал богатый запах леса и следовал по следам Кенни. В конце концов тропа должна была вывести на луг, но Джамин надеялся найти Кенни раньше, чем придётся идти так далеко. Разные капканы уже были проверены, так что Джамин знал, что Кенни прошёл этой дорогой. Джамин твёрдо шёл вперёд. Его золотистая голова ловила уставшие лучи заходящего солнца, мерцающие сквозь деревья. И вскоре и они угасли, оставив после себя мускусный запах леса. Паутинные гусеницы осеннего сезона работали, и их паутинки нависали над ветвями, словно занавеси.

Наконец, когда деревья разрежались и становились ниже, и показался луг, Джамин понял, что это конец маршрута Кенни по проверке капканов. Если Кенни не окажется здесь, он не знал, куда ещё искать.

Но Кенни был там. Когда Джамин ввалился на луг, он увидел справа от себя скомканную фигуру. Голос этой фигуры имел знакомое звучание. Лицо было исказено болью. Это был Кенни. «С тобой всё в порядке? Что случилось?» — почувствовал Джамин странное волнение, увидев Кенни, свернувшегося в грязи. Кенни был умным. «Ты попал в капкан?»

«Да, Джамин. Я... я не смотрел под ноги. Помоги мне. Пожалуйста».

Джамин нагнулся и нашёл лодыжку, крепко зажатую в стальных зубах капкана. Тьма окрашивала землю вокруг Кенни. Быстро Джамин сильными руками разжал челюсти. Кенни вырвался. «Ты можешь идти?»

«Да. Думаю, да. Если ты меня поддержишь, я смогу прихрамывать».

«Папа и мама будут волноваться. Мы опоздаем к ужину».

Как ни странно, когда братья шли обратно через лес, они услышали громкий зов отца. Джамин ответил, и отец был у них в тот же миг, увидел лодыжку и подхватил Кенни, как раненую овцу. Эти двое поспешили домой, и сетчатая дверь с грохотом захлопнулась, когда отец пронёсся по веранде. Джамин пошёл в умывальню и тщательно вымыл руки. Затем направился к входной двери.

«Джамин». Это была бабушка. Свет на веранде освещал её в старом кресле-качалке. На её плечах лежал тяжёлый плед.

«Да, бабушка?»

«Ты думаешь, что ты не очень умный?»

«Так говорит Кенни» — Джамин ёрзал.

«Ты были достаточно силён, чтобы открыть капкан, а Кенни — нет. Ты был достаточно храбр, чтобы найти его в темноте. Многие мальчики не смогли бы». Джамин молчал. Бабушка Отто ещё немного покачалась в кресле, затем улыбнулась. «Бог создал тебя таким не просто так, Джамин. Он создал Кенни таким по своей причине. У Него есть план для тебя и место, которое можешь занять только ты, знаешь ли».

Джамин повернулся и вошёл в тёплую кухню. Он улыбался.

I can still smell the tantalizing cacophony of odors as I clutched my father’s strong hand, weaving our way through the masses of tourists that crowded the building. The vendors at the Green Dragon Farmer’s Market in Ephrata, PA, were trying their best to entice buyers with their rows of fresh fish over ice, cheeses of every variety, deli meat and sandwiches, and piles of fresh fruit. And, oh, the candy! My young preschool mind had never seen so many delectable sweets in one place at one time.

The past two days for me were like the boy at the candy store. I had the privilege of attending Christian Aid Ministries’ first Annual Writers’ Conference. I brushed shoulders with well-known authors such as Katrina Hoover Lee, Johnny Miller, and Ruthann Stelfox. I chatted with aspiring writers and seasoned school teachers. I had the opportunity to sit under hours of inspirational and educational workshops on how to write to communicate, using realistic dialog, descriptive writing, and much more. We all had one common goal in mind. Together, we share and learn how to effectively communicate what is in our hearts, and through the power of the written word, transmit those thoughts to your hearts.

The Heartbeat of the Remnant is a means to communicate inspirational thoughts to eager readers scattered across the globe. Courageous writers step forward with pen and paper or keyboard and monitor and help spread the Good News of the Word of God with caution, correction, and edification. Yet, we need more such writers. We need young believers who bravely submit their first children’s stories. Seasoned grandfathers who bring words of admonishment to the younger generation. Mothers who share experiences and trials with other mothers who are in the throes of raising little ones. Youth encouraging fellow youth to press toward the mark of the prize of the high calling in Christ Jesus. Fathers who with a concerned eye watch the world pressing in on the Christian homes. Together, these aspiring writers will produce a periodical that will endure on the family coffee table for many years. I encourage you, fellow believers, to give it a try. Nelson Mandela, former president of South Africa wrote, “Failure is a teacher, and at the end of your life, what do you think you’ll feel worst about, failing or never trying?”

The Berean Voice has a goal to provide printed material that will help readers navigate through the varied and difficult seasons of life. All our material is available at no charge, but we are dependent on the donations of our supporters. Here is a list of books we have available:

The Power of the Love of Truth
Christian Counseling- Counterfeit?
The Heart of God
Free Indeed!
Pilgrims and Politics
Cup & Cross
The High Cost of Holistic Healing
Secrets of Successful Writing
The Catholic Connection
Psychiatry and Mood altering Medications
The Mennonite Church and Modernism

In 2017 and 2018, the Berean Voice printed a series of vaccine articles in The Heartbeat of the Remnant magazine. These articles were a sincere effort to examine various aspects of vaccine usage with an unbiased approach. We attempted to present the facts as clearly as possible and let the readers draw their own conclusions.

Since then, we have received numerous requests from our readers to publish all the vaccine articles in a booklet, which we agreed to do. But then along came 2019, bringing coronavirus with it. This monumental event upended the vaccine debate and ushered in a frenzied rush to market COVID-19 remedies, many of which were not properly tested. We put the printing on hold, unsure whether to include information on these new and unproven COVID-19 “vaccines.” As time progressed and the deadly nature of COVID-19 abated, we decided to publish the original vaccine articles in a booklet without any additional articles on the COVID-19 debate. We are pleased that the project is nearing completion and will be announced when it is released.

Blessings to all,

Edward Martin

Je peux encore sentir la cacophonie alléchante d’odeurs tandis que je serrais la main robuste de mon père, nous frayant un chemin parmi les foules de touristes qui encombraient le bâtiment. Les vendeurs du Green Dragon Farmer’s Market à Ephrata, en Pennsylvanie, faisaient de leur mieux pour attirer les acheteurs avec leurs rangées de poissons frais sur glace, des fromages de toutes sortes, de la charcuterie et des sandwiches, et des tas de fruits frais. Et, oh, les bonbons ! Mon jeune esprit de préscolaire n’avait jamais vu autant de douceurs alléchantes réunies au même endroit.

Ces deux derniers jours ont été pour moi comme pour le garçon dans la confiserie. J’ai eu le privilège d’assister à la première conférence annuelle des écrivains organisée par Christian Aid Ministries. J’ai croisé des auteurs connus tels que Katrina Hoover Lee, Johnny Miller et Ruthann Stelfox. J’ai discuté avec des aspirants écrivains et des professeurs d’école expérimentés. J’ai eu l’occasion d’assister à des heures d’ateliers inspirants et pédagogiques sur la façon d’écrire pour communiquer, en utilisant des dialogues réalistes, un écriture descriptive, et bien plus encore. Nous avions tous un objectif commun. Ensemble, nous partageons et apprenons comment communiquer efficacement ce qui est dans nos cœurs, et, par le pouvoir de l’écrit, transmettre ces pensées dans vos cœurs.

The Heartbeat of the Remnant est un moyen de communiquer des pensées inspirantes à des lecteurs avides répartis à travers le monde. Des écrivains courageux se présentent, plume et papier ou clavier et écran, et contribuent à répandre la Bonne Nouvelle de la Parole de Dieu avec prudence, correction et édification. Pourtant, nous avons besoin de davantage de tels écrivains. Nous avons besoin de jeunes croyants qui présentent courageusement leurs premières histoires pour enfants. De grands-pères expérimentés qui apportent des paroles d’avertissement à la jeune génération. De mères qui partagent expériences et épreuves avec d’autres mères en plein élevage des tout-petits. Des jeunes encourageant leurs pairs à poursuivre la course vers le prix de l’appel élevé en Jésus-Christ. Des pères qui, d’un œil inquiet, observent le monde faire pression sur les foyers chrétiens. Ensemble, ces écrivains aspirants produiront une périodique qui restera sur la table basse familiale pendant de nombreuses années. Je vous encourage, frères et sœurs en Christ, à tenter votre chance. Nelson Mandela, ancien président de l’Afrique du Sud, a écrit : « L’échec est un maître, et à la fin de votre vie, de quoi pensez-vous que vous vous sentirez le plus mal : d’avoir échoué ou de ne jamais avoir essayé ? »

Le Berean Voice a pour objectif de fournir des documents imprimés qui aideront les lecteurs à traverser les saisons variées et difficiles de la vie. Tout notre matériel est disponible gratuitement, mais nous dépendons des dons de nos soutiens. Voici une liste des livres que nous avons disponibles :

La puissance de l’amour de la vérité
Conseil chrétien : contrefaçon ?
Le cœur de Dieu
Libres en vérité !
Pèlerins et politique
Coupe et croix
Le coût élevé de la guérison holistique
Secrets de l’écriture réussie
La connexion catholique
Psychiatrie et médicaments modifiant l’humeur
L’Église mennonite et le modernisme

En 2017 et 2018, le Berean Voice a publié une série d’articles sur les vaccins dans le magazine The Heartbeat of the Remnant. Ces articles étaient un effort sincère pour examiner divers aspects de l’utilisation des vaccins avec une approche équilibrée. Nous avons tenté de présenter les faits aussi clairement que possible et de laisser les lecteurs tirer leurs propres conclusions.

Depuis lors, nous avons reçu de nombreuses demandes de la part de nos lecteurs pour publier tous les articles sur les vaccins dans un livret, ce que nous avons accepté de faire. Puis est arrivé 2019, apportant avec lui le coronavirus. Cet événement monumental a bouleversé le débat sur les vaccins et a ouvert la voie à une ruée effrénée pour commercialiser des remèdes contre la COVID-19, dont beaucoup n’étaient pas correctement testés. Nous avons mis l’impression en attente, ne sachant pas s’il fallait inclure des informations sur ces nouveaux « vaccins » contre la COVID-19 non éprouvés. Avec le temps et l’atténuation du caractère mortel de la COVID-19, nous avons décidé de publier les articles originaux sur les vaccins dans un livret sans articles supplémentaires sur le débat concernant la COVID-19. Nous sommes heureux que le projet soit presque achevé et qu’il sera annoncé lors de sa sortie.

Bénédictions à tous,

Edward Martin

Circumstantial overload might be the most difficult. We can choose not to go to a Norwex party if we need to give our schedule some space. But if a child breaks a leg in the middle of wedding preparations, we have no choice other than to make the best of the situation.

Circumstantial overload may happen slowly, as in the following story, or it may happen quickly as in the case of an accident in which a family member is injured.

Becky is in her thirties with seven children under seventeen. A few years ago, one of their chicken houses burned down. At the time, they were thankful that the chickens had left the day before and that no one was close by when the propane tank exploded.

“My husband faced the disaster like a man,” says Becky. “His calm spirit helped me relax. I felt certain that we could make the financial adjustments and life would go on as before. But I was wrong. Very wrong.”

“In time the mess was cleaned up, and Rick looked into rebuilding. The quotes were higher than expected, so he opted to do some of the work himself. He also took on a part-time job to provide more income. Our boys were old enough to help, yet they couldn’t do much without Rick’s direction.”

“I first felt the adjustment in my wallet, but I consoled myself that this was only temporary. Then the spark in Rick’s eyes was replaced with a dull stare. He became distant from us. I knew something wasn’t right, but I couldn’t put my finger on it.”

“Then he was elected to finish the last four months of secretarial duties for a brother who spent some time in Bulgaria. That night he came home and wept. ‘Doesn’t anyone understand what I’m going through? Every time I turn around, there is something to do. The boys want to go fishing, you need a new clothesline, and the chicken house needs to be finished in six months! I am not mentally capable of handling one more duty.’”

“That was the straw that broke the camel’s back,” Becky said. “I became alarmed when I heard him yawning in the middle of the night and knew that he was not sleeping.”

“It was clear to me that my perfectionist husband was overloaded. More and more Rick leaned on me. I cut back on my commitments and tried to keep my time free so that I was available to help lessen his load.”

“I felt like a lifeguard trying to keep a man from drowning while taking in a bit too much water myself. Many of the home-life responsibilities fell on my shoulders. Then I was asked to fill the position of food committee for Mrs. ‘Going-to-Bulgaria.’”

Unfortunately, circumstantial stress is often unnoticed. Worse yet, the victim can be misunderstood or misjudged. Becky said, “My darkest day came when I was accused of being selfish with my time because I declined the food committee request.”

Prolonged overload can be emotionally and mentally damaging

Intense, long-lasting pressures or troubles shouldered alone can cause severe stress. Minor stress is normal, but prolonged stress can cause depression, anxiety, heart disease, and high blood pressure. How you handle prolonged stress is important.

Sometimes this type of overload is not public knowledge. Traumatic events in our plain circles tend to receive prayer, finances, and weekly budget updates. At the same time, other saints are suffering deeply on the sidelines with little recognition or financial aid. It could be strained relationships or little bills that add up to a big sum. Betrayal and rejection cause stress beyond measure. There are no quick fixes to circumstantial stress, but little sparks of light can help you navigate the darkness.

Talk about your situation with someone you trust

Sometimes just talking about problems can help you to put issues in perspective. Hearing yourself verbalize a stressful situation somehow clears brain fog and gives a clearer path forward.

Find routine

When stress prevails, racing thoughts, forgetfulness, and inability to focus comes uninvited. Having a routine can bring some rhythm to your mental well-being. The smallest normalcy brings a moment of pleasure, and it is soothing to the soul.

Intentionally seek a breather

Lingering stress can cause agitation, moodiness, and the desire to take control. Sometimes it is hard to think beyond mental fog, but it is so important to find refreshment for your mental wellbeing. Stress hormones can speed up your heart rate and tighten your blood vessels. That temporarily raises your blood pressure. The opposite happens when you relax. Being relaxed helps you have a calmer, clearer mind which improves your concentration and decision-making.

Believe that God cares

Say it. Read the Psalms over and over. Listen to good music. Take short walks and pray aloud. Keep your eyes on Jesus. Believe “Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning” (Psalm 30:5).

If you are facing circumstantial overload, be patient and realistic. God will make a way for you. Many times, He opens doors just when we are running out of options. He will supply the needed grace for that hour. And the next hour. And the next. At times, surprising opportunities come, and prayers are answered in unexpected ways. However He chooses to work on your behalf, hold to His unchanging hand.

Regardless of the type of overload you might be encountering, turn to your Heavenly Father.

Ask Him for direction and wisdom. And say with the Psalmist, “In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust: let me never be put to confusion” (Psalm 71:1).

परिस्थितिजन्य अतिभार शायद सबसे कठिन हो सकता है। अगर हमें अपने कार्यक्रम को कुछ जगह देनी हो तो हम किसी Norwex पार्टी में न जाने का चुनाव कर सकते हैं। लेकिन अगर शादी की तैयारियों के बीच एक बच्चे की टांग टूट जाए, तो हमारे पास स्थिति का सर्वश्रेष्ठ उपयोग करने के अलावा कोई विकल्प नहीं होता।

परिस्थितिजन्य अतिभार धीरे-धीरे हो सकता है, जैसा कि निम्नलिखित कहानी में है, या अचानक भी हो सकता है, जैसे किसी दुर्घटना में परिवार के किसी सदस्य को चोट लगना।

बेकी तीस के दशक में हैं और उनके सात बच्चे सत्रह साल से कम उम्र के हैं। कुछ साल पहले, उनके चिकन हाउस में आग लग गई थी। उस समय वे आभारी थे कि मुर्गियाँ एक दिन पहले ही निकल गई थीं और प्रोपेन टैंक फटते समय कोई पास नहीं था।

“मेरे पति ने उस विपत्ति का सामना एक पुरुष की तरह किया,” बेकी कहती हैं। “उनकी शांत आत्मा ने मुझे भी शिथिल कर दिया। मुझे यकीन था कि हम आर्थिक समायोजन कर लेंगे और जीवन पहले जैसा चल पड़ेगा। लेकिन मैं गलत थी। बहुत गलत।”

“धीरे-धीरे गंदगी साफ़ कर दी गई, और रिक ने पुनर्निर्माण के बारे में सोचना शुरू किया। उद्धरण अपेक्षा से अधिक थे, इसलिए उन्होंने कुछ काम खुद करने का विकल्प चुना। उन्होंने अतिरिक्त आय के लिए अंशकालिक नौकरी भी कर ली। हमारे लड़के मदद करने के लिए बड़े थे, फिर भी वे रिक के निर्देशन के बिना ज्यादा कुछ नहीं कर सकते थे।”

“मुझे सबसे पहले अपने पर्स में समायोजन महसूस हुआ, पर मैंने खुद को सांत्वना दी कि यह केवल अस्थायी है। फिर रिक की आँखों की चमक फीकी पड़कर एक सुस्त घूरन में बदल गई। वह हमसे दूर हो गया। मुझे पता था कि कुछ सही नहीं है, पर मैं उसे पकड़ नहीं पा रही थी।”

“फिर उन्हें उस भाई के लिए सचिवीय कर्तव्यों के अंतिम चार महीने पूरा करने के लिए निर्वाचित किया गया, जो कुछ समय बुल्गारिया में रहे थे। उस रात वह घर आए और रो पड़े। ‘क्या कोई समझता नहीं कि मैं किस से गुजर रहा हूँ? हर बार मैं घुमता हूँ, कुछ न कुछ करने को होता है। लड़के मछली पकड़ने जाना चाहते हैं, तुम्हें नई कपड़ों की रस्सी चाहिए, और चिकन हाउस छह महीने में पूरा होना है! मैं मानसिक रूप से एक और कर्तव्य संभालने में सक्षम नहीं हूँ।’”

“यही वह तिनका था जिसने ऊँट की पीठ तोड़ दी,” बेकी ने कहा। “जब मैंने उन्हें आधी रात में झपकी लेते सुना और जाना कि वह सो नहीं रहे हैं तो मैं चिंतित हो गई।”

“यह मेरे लिए स्पष्ट था कि मेरे पूर्णतावादी पति पर बोझ अधिक हो गया था। रिक मुझ पर और अधिक निर्भर होने लगे। मैंने अपनी प्रतिबद्धताओं को घटाया और अपना समय खाली रखने की कोशिश की ताकि मैं उनके बोझ को कम करने में उपलब्ध रहूँ।”

“मुझे ऐसा लगा मानो मैं एक लाइफगार्ड हूँ जो डूबते हुए व्यक्ति को बचाने की कोशिश कर रही है और खुद थोड़ा-बहुत पानी ले रही हूँ। घर के बहुत से जिम्मेदारियाँ मेरी काँधों पर आ गइं। फिर मुझे 'बुल्गारिया जा रही' महिला के लिए फ़ूड कमेटी की जिम्मेदारी देने को कहा गया।”

दुर्भाग्यवश, परिस्थितिजन्य तनाव अक्सर अनदेखा रहता है। और भी बुरा, पीड़ित को गलत समझा या जज किया जा सकता है। बेकी ने कहा, “मेरा सबसे अँधेरा दिन तब आया जब मुझ पर समय के प्रति स्वार्थी होने का आरोप लगाया गया क्योंकि मैंने फ़ूड कमेटी के अनुरोध को इंकार कर दिया।”

लंबे समय तक रहने वाला अतिभार भावनात्मक और मानसिक रूप से हानिकारक हो सकता है

तेज़, दीर्घकालिक दबाव या अकेले उठाए गए कष्ट गंभीर तनाव पैदा कर सकते हैं। मामूली तनाव सामान्य है, पर लंबा तनाव अवसाद, चिंता, हृदय रोग और उच्च रक्तचाप का कारण बन सकता है। आप लंबी अवधि के तनाव को कैसे संभालते हैं यह महत्वपूर्ण है।

कभी-कभी इस प्रकार का अतिभार सार्वजनिक जानकारी में नहीं आता। हमारे दिखने वाले गोत्रों में घटी आघातकारी घटनाओं को अक्सर प्रार्थना, वित्त और साप्ताहिक बजट अपडेट मिलते हैं। उसी समय, अन्य भक्त किनारे पर गहरे कष्ट झेल रहे होते हैं और उन्हें कम पहचाना या कम आर्थिक मदद मिलती है। यह तनाउ—भरी रिश्तों या छोटी-छोटी बिलों का जमा होकर बड़े योग बन जाना—हो सकता है। धोखा और अस्वीकृति ऐसे तनाव पैदा करते हैं जो माप से परे होते हैं। परिस्थितिजन्य तनाव के कोई त्वरित हल नहीं हैं, पर छोटी-छोटी उम्मीद की किरणें आपकी अंधकार में नेविगेट करने में मदद कर सकती हैं।

किसी भरोसेमंद व्यक्ति से अपनी स्थिति के बारे में बात करें

कभी-कभी केवल समस्याओं के बारे में बात करने से ही आप मुद्दों को दृष्टिकोण में रख पाते हैं। खुद को मौखिक रूप से तनावपूर्ण स्थिति बताते हुए सुनना किसी तरह मस्तिष्क के कुहासे को साफ़ करता है और आगे का स्पष्ट मार्ग देता है।

नियमित दिनचर्या खोजें

जब तनाव हावी होता है, तब भागती सोच, भूलने की प्रवृत्ति, और ध्यान केंद्रित करने में असमर्थता अनचाहे रूप से आ जाती है। एक नियमबद्ध दिनचर्या आपके मानसिक स्वास्थ्य में कुछ लय ला सकती है। सबसे छोटी सामान्यता भी आनंद का एक क्षण लाती है, और यह आत्मा को शान्त करती है।

जानबूझकर एक विराम खोजें

लंबा तनाव उग्रता, मूडीनेस, और नियंत्रण लेने की इच्छा पैदा कर सकता है। कभी-कभी मानसिक कुहासे के परे सोचना मुश्किल हो जाता है, पर आपकी मानसिक भलाई के लिए ताज़गी पाना बहुत जरूरी है। तनाव हॉर्मोन आपके हृदय की गति तेज कर सकते हैं और आपकी रक्त वाहिकाओं को तंग कर सकते हैं। इससे अस्थायी रूप से आपका रक्तचाप बढ़ जाता है। जब आप शांत होते हैं तो इसका उल्टा होता है। शांत होना आपको शांत, स्पष्ट मन देता है जो आपकी एकाग्रता और निर्णय-क्षमता में सुधार लाता है।

विश्वास रखिये कि ईश्वर परवाह करते हैं

कहिए यह। भजनसंग्रह को बार-बार पढ़िए। अच्छी संगीत सुनिए। छोटे-छोटे पैदल चलने पर जोर-अवाज़ में प्रार्थना कीजिए। अपनी नजरें यीशु पर रखें। विश्वास कीजिए “Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning” (Psalm 30:5).

यदि आप परिस्थितिजन्य अतिभार का सामना कर रहे हैं, तो धैर्य रखें और वास्तविक बनें। ईश्वर आपके लिए मार्ग बनाएंगे। कई बार, जब हमारे विकल्प खत्म होने लगते हैं, तभी वह दरवाज़े खोल देते हैं। वह उस घड़ी के लिए आवश्यक अनुग्रह प्रदान करेंगे। और अगली घड़ी के लिए भी। और उसके बाद भी। कभी-कभी, चौंकाने वाले अवसर आते हैं, और प्रार्थनाएँ अप्रत्याशित तरीकों से सुन ली जाती हैं। जिस भी तरीके से वह आपकी ओर से काम करना चुनते हैं, उसके अचल हाथ को थामे रहिए।

आप किसी भी प्रकार के अतिभार का सामना कर रहे हों, अपने स्वर्गीय पिता की ओर मुड़िए।

उनसे मार्गदर्शन और बुद्धि माँगिए। और भजनकार की तरह कहिए, “In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust: let me never be put to confusion” (Psalm 71:1).

Circumstantial overload might be the most difficult. We can choose not to go to a Norwex party if we need to give our schedule some space. But if a child breaks a leg in the middle of wedding preparations, we have no choice other than to make the best of the situation.

Circumstantial overload may happen slowly, as in the following story, or it may happen quickly as in the case of an accident in which a family member is injured.

Becky is in her thirties with seven children under seventeen. A few years ago, one of their chicken houses burned down. At the time, they were thankful that the chickens had left the day before and that no one was close by when the propane tank exploded.

“My husband faced the disaster like a man,” says Becky. “His calm spirit helped me relax. I felt certain that we could make the financial adjustments and life would go on as before. But I was wrong. Very wrong.”

“In time the mess was cleaned up, and Rick looked into rebuilding. The quotes were higher than expected, so he opted to do some of the work himself. He also took on a part-time job to provide more income. Our boys were old enough to help, yet they couldn’t do much without Rick’s direction.”

“I first felt the adjustment in my wallet, but I consoled myself that this was only temporary. Then the spark in Rick’s eyes was replaced with a dull stare. He became distant from us. I knew something wasn’t right, but I couldn’t put my finger on it.”

“Then he was elected to finish the last four months of secretarial duties for a brother who spent some time in Bulgaria. That night he came home and wept. ‘Doesn’t anyone understand what I’m going through? Every time I turn around, there is something to do. The boys want to go fishing, you need a new clothesline, and the chicken house needs to be finished in six months! I am not mentally capable of handling one more duty.’”

“That was the straw that broke the camel’s back,” Becky said. “I became alarmed when I heard him yawning in the middle of the night and knew that he was not sleeping.”

“It was clear to me that my perfectionist husband was overloaded. More and more Rick leaned on me. I cut back on my commitments and tried to keep my time free so that I was available to help lessen his load.”

“I felt like a lifeguard trying to keep a man from drowning while taking in a bit too much water myself. Many of the home-life responsibilities fell on my shoulders. Then I was asked to fill the position of food committee for Mrs. ‘Going-to-Bulgaria.’”

Unfortunately, circumstantial stress is often unnoticed. Worse yet, the victim can be misunderstood or misjudged. Becky said, “My darkest day came when I was accused of being selfish with my time because I declined the food committee request.”

Prolonged overload can be emotionally and mentally damaging

Intense, long-lasting pressures or troubles shouldered alone can cause severe stress. Minor stress is normal, but prolonged stress can cause depression, anxiety, heart disease, and high blood pressure. How you handle prolonged stress is important.

Sometimes this type of overload is not public knowledge. Traumatic events in our plain circles tend to receive prayer, finances, and weekly budget updates. At the same time, other saints are suffering deeply on the sidelines with little recognition or financial aid. It could be strained relationships or little bills that add up to a big sum. Betrayal and rejection cause stress beyond measure. There are no quick fixes to circumstantial stress, but little sparks of light can help you navigate the darkness.

Talk about your situation with someone you trust

Sometimes just talking about problems can help you to put issues in perspective. Hearing yourself verbalize a stressful situation somehow clears brain fog and gives a clearer path forward.

Find routine

When stress prevails, racing thoughts, forgetfulness, and inability to focus comes uninvited. Having a routine can bring some rhythm to your mental well-being. The smallest normalcy brings a moment of pleasure, and it is soothing to the soul.

Intentionally seek a breather

Lingering stress can cause agitation, moodiness, and the desire to take control. Sometimes it is hard to think beyond mental fog, but it is so important to find refreshment for your mental wellbeing. Stress hormones can speed up your heart rate and tighten your blood vessels. That temporarily raises your blood pressure. The opposite happens when you relax. Being relaxed helps you have a calmer, clearer mind which improves your concentration and decision-making.

Believe that God cares

Say it. Read the Psalms over and over. Listen to good music. Take short walks and pray aloud. Keep your eyes on Jesus. Believe “Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning” (Psalm 30:5).

If you are facing circumstantial overload, be patient and realistic. God will make a way for you. Many times, He opens doors just when we are running out of options. He will supply the needed grace for that hour. And the next hour. And the next. At times, surprising opportunities come, and prayers are answered in unexpected ways. However He chooses to work on your behalf, hold to His unchanging hand.

Regardless of the type of overload you might be encountering, turn to your Heavenly Father.

Ask Him for direction and wisdom. And say with the Psalmist, “In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust: let me never be put to confusion” (Psalm 71:1).

עומס יתר הנובע מהנסיבות עשוי להיות הקשה מכול. אנחנו יכולות לבחור שלא ללכת למפגש מכירות של Norwex אם אנחנו צריכות לפנות קצת מקום בלוח הזמנים שלנו. אבל אם ילד שובר רגל בעיצומן של ההכנות לחתונה, אין לנו ברירה אלא להפיק את המיטב מהמצב.

עומס יתר הנובע מהנסיבות יכול להתפתח לאט, כמו בסיפור הבא, או להופיע במהירות, כמו במקרה של תאונה שבה נפצע בן משפחה.

בקי בשנות השלושים לחייה, ויש לה שבעה ילדים שטרם מלאו להם שבע־עשרה. לפני כמה שנים נשרף אחד הלולים שלהם. באותו זמן הם היו אסירי תודה על כך שהתרנגולות הוצאו ממנו יום קודם לכן ושאיש לא היה בקרבת מקום כשמכל הפרופאן התפוצץ.

״בעלי התמודד עם האסון כמו גבר״, אומרת בקי. ״הרוגע שלו עזר לי להירגע. הייתי בטוחה שנוכל לעשות את ההתאמות הכספיות ושהחיים יימשכו כמו קודם. אבל טעיתי. טעיתי מאוד.״

״עם הזמן פונו ההריסות, וריק בדק את האפשרות לבנות מחדש. הצעות המחיר היו גבוהות מהצפוי, ולכן הוא בחר לבצע חלק מהעבודה בעצמו. הוא גם התחיל לעבוד במשרה חלקית כדי להגדיל את ההכנסה. הבנים שלנו היו מבוגרים מספיק כדי לעזור, ובכל זאת לא יכלו לעשות הרבה בלי ההכוונה של ריק.״

״בהתחלה הרגשתי את השינוי בארנק, אבל ניחמתי את עצמי שזה זמני בלבד. ואז הניצוץ בעיניו של ריק התחלף במבט כבוי. הוא התרחק מאיתנו. ידעתי שמשהו לא בסדר, אבל לא הצלחתי לזהות מה בדיוק.״

״ואז הוא נבחר למלא את ארבעת החודשים האחרונים של תפקיד המזכיר במקום אח באמונה ששהה זמן מה בבולגריה. באותו לילה הוא חזר הביתה ובכה. ‘אף אחד לא מבין מה עובר עליי? לאן שאני פונה, יש משהו שצריך לעשות. הבנים רוצים לצאת לדוג, את צריכה חבל כביסה חדש, וצריך לסיים את הלול בתוך שישה חודשים! מבחינה נפשית אני לא מסוגל להתמודד עם עוד מטלה אחת.’״

״זה היה הקש ששבר את גב הגמל״, אמרה בקי. ״נבהלתי כששמעתי אותו מפהק באמצע הלילה וידעתי שהוא לא ישן.״

״היה לי ברור שבעלי הפרפקציוניסט נתון בעומס יתר. ריק נשען עליי יותר ויותר. צמצמתי את ההתחייבויות שלי וניסיתי להשאיר את זמני פנוי כדי שאהיה זמינה לעזור להקל עליו את העומס.״

״הרגשתי כמו מצילה שמנסה למנוע מאדם לטבוע, ובו בזמן בולעת בעצמה קצת יותר מדי מים. רבות מהמטלות הקשורות לחיי הבית נפלו על כתפיי. ואז התבקשתי למלא את התפקיד בוועדת המזון במקום גברת ‘נוסעת־לבולגריה’.״

למרבה הצער, לעיתים קרובות איש אינו מבחין במתח הנובע מהנסיבות. גרוע מכך, הסובל ממנו עלול להיתקל בחוסר הבנה או בשיפוט מוטעה. בקי אמרה: ״היום האפל ביותר שלי הגיע כשנאמר לי שאני אנוכית בכל הנוגע לזמן שלי, מפני שדחיתי את הבקשה להצטרף לוועדת המזון.״

עומס יתר מתמשך עלול לגרום נזק רגשי ונפשי

לחצים עזים ומתמשכים או צרות שנושאים לבד עלולים לגרום למתח חמור. מתח קל הוא דבר רגיל, אבל מתח מתמשך עלול לגרום לדיכאון, לחרדה, למחלות לב וללחץ דם גבוה. חשוב כיצד את מתמודדת עם מתח מתמשך.

לפעמים עומס יתר מסוג זה אינו ידוע לציבור. אירועים טראומטיים בקהילות שלנו, הדוגלות באורח חיים פשוט, זוכים בדרך כלל לתפילות, לסיוע כספי ולעדכונים שבועיים על התקציב. באותו זמן, מאמינים אחרים סובלים מאוד בשוליים, בלי שהסבל שלהם זוכה כמעט להכרה או לסיוע כספי. ייתכן שמדובר ביחסים מתוחים או בחשבונות קטנים המצטברים לסכום גדול. בגידה ודחייה גורמות למתח שאין לו שיעור. אין פתרונות מהירים למתח הנובע מהנסיבות, אבל ניצוצות אור קטנים יכולים לעזור לך למצוא את דרכך בחשכה.

דברי על מצבך עם מישהו שאת סומכת עליו

לפעמים עצם הדיבור על בעיות יכול לעזור לך לראות אותן בפרופורציה. כשאת שומעת את עצמך מתארת במילים מצב מלחיץ, הדבר מפזר איכשהו את הערפל המחשבתי ומבהיר את הדרך קדימה.

מצאי שגרה

כשהמתח משתלט, מחשבות דוהרות, שכחה וחוסר יכולת להתרכז מופיעים בלי הזמנה. שגרה יכולה להעניק קצב מסוים לרווחתך הנפשית. אפילו שמץ של שגרה רגילה מביא רגע של הנאה ומרגיע את הנפש.

חפשי במכוון רגע של הפוגה

מתח מתמשך עלול לגרום לאי־שקט, לתנודות במצב הרוח ולרצון להשתלט על המצב. לפעמים קשה לחשוב מעבר לערפל הנפשי, אבל חשוב כל כך למצוא התרעננות למען רווחתך הנפשית. הורמוני מתח יכולים להאיץ את קצב הלב ולכווץ את כלי הדם. הדבר מעלה באופן זמני את לחץ הדם. ההפך קורה כשאת נרגעת. הרגיעה עוזרת לך לחשוב בצלילות וברוגע רבים יותר, ומשפרת את הריכוז ואת קבלת ההחלטות שלך.

האמיני שאלוהים דואג לך

אמרי זאת. קראי את תהילים שוב ושוב. האזיני למוזיקה טובה. צאי להליכות קצרות והתפללי בקול. שמרי את עינייך מופנות אל ישוע. האמיני ש״הבכי עשוי להימשך לילה, אבל השמחה באה בבוקר״ (תהילים 30:5).

אם את מתמודדת עם עומס יתר הנובע מהנסיבות, היי סבלנית ומציאותית. אלוהים יפתח לך דרך. פעמים רבות הוא פותח דלתות דווקא כשהאפשרויות שלנו הולכות ואוזלות. הוא יספק את החסד הדרוש לאותה שעה. ולשעה הבאה. ולזו שאחריה. לפעמים צצות הזדמנויות מפתיעות, ותפילות נענות בדרכים בלתי צפויות. בכל דרך שבה יבחר לפעול למענך, אחזי בידו שאינה משתנה.

בלי קשר לסוג עומס היתר שאת עשויה להתמודד איתו, פני אל אביך שבשמיים.

בקשי ממנו הכוונה וחוכמה. ואמרי עם מחבר המזמור: ״בך, אדוני, אני שמה את מבטחי; אל תיתן לי לעולם לבוא לידי בושה״ (תהילים 71:1).

How unbelievable it is that God can take a wretched sinner, void of the fear of the Lord, and turn him into a blood-washed saint and preacher of the gospel! In this story, we see God’s life-changing power at work in our hymn writer’s life.

In the small cemetery of a churchyard in Olney, England, stands a granite tombstone with this inscription, written by Newton himself before his death:

John Newton, once an infidel and libertine, a servant of slaves in Africa, was, by the rich mercy of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, preserved, restored, pardoned, and appointed to preach the faith he had long labored to destroy!

This epitaph aptly describes the unusual and colorful life of this man, one of the great evangelical preachers of the eighteenth century. His testimony was, “By the grace of God, I am what I am!”

“Amazing Grace” was a hymn published in 1779, with words written in 1772 by the English poet and Anglican clergyman John Newton (1725–1807). “Amazing Grace” is probably the most beloved hymn of the last two centuries. This hymn is estimated to be performed 10 million times annually. It has appeared on over 11,000 albums and translated into about 60 languages. It was referenced in Harriet Beecher Stowe’s anti-slavery novel Uncle Tom’s Cabin. It had a surge in popularity during two of America’s greatest crises: the Civil War and the Vietnam War.

Ironically, this stirring song, closely associated with the African-American community, was written by a former slave trader, John Newton.

John was born on July 24, 1725, in Wapping, England, to a seafaring father, John Newton, Sr., and a devout Christian mother, Elizabeth Newton. His father loved him but was gone at sea most of the time. On the other hand, his mother was tender and nurturing, teaching him the Word of God. She would instruct him in memorizing the Bible whole chapters at a time and took him to church. Unfortunately, when he was almost seven, his mother died of tuberculosis. His father remarried a short time later and sent him to a boarding school. During his time at the boarding school, he made bad friends. His character disintegrated to the point that he was dismissed from one school and moved to another. By the time he was 11 years old, the boarding schools didn’t want him, so his father took him along to sea. He spent the next six years on the Atlantic Ocean with his father.

When John was 17, his father arranged to send him to Jamaica for a well-paying job overseeing a plantation. On his way, while waiting for the ship’s departure, John received an invitation to the home of some old-time friends, the Catletts. It was in this home that John’s mother had died ten years earlier. As he reacquainted himself with them, he got to know their daughter, Mary. John and Mary’s mothers were best of friends. John had been invited to stay four days, but he stayed two weeks and missed the ship to Jamaica.

At age 18, John was conscripted into the Royal Navy, and his life went from bad to worse. He wanted to return and see Mary, so he deserted the ship but was caught, publicly flogged, and laid in irons. His life on the ship was so profane that even the other ungodly sailors cringed at his curses and blasphemies. He gained the title “The Great Blasphemer” and was such an unwanted man on the ship that he was sent to work on a slave ship.

One of the owners of the slave ship where he now worked, offered John a job once they reached the African coast. However, once on shore, he was tied up and forced to work with little food, clothing, or shelter. He sent several letters back to his father during this time, pleading for help.

A ship called The Greyhound was sailing near the coast, which John had now called home. The captain had been instructed by John’s father to look for his son. The ship, while being almost too far from shore to trade, decided to give trading a try. A friend of John’s rowed out from shore to trade. As he turned to leave, the captain asked him whether he knew anyone named John Newton. He did to the captain’s surprise, and John was brought on board to go home.

On board the ship, Newton picked up a copy of Thomas á Kempis’s Christian classic, The Imitation of Christ. He had never encountered anything like it, and he began to wonder if the Christian claims might be true. That night, on March 10, 1748, a fierce storm nearly swamped the ship. Men, animals, and provisions were swept overboard. The storm awakened Newton, the ship’s rotten timbers broken by the waves and floodwater swirling into his cabin. John prayed for the first time in years.

The Greyhound thrashed about in the North Atlantic storm for over 11 days. With little hope of survival, the sailors mechanically worked the pumps, trying to keep the vessel afloat. On the eleventh day of the storm, John was too exhausted to pump, so he was tied to the helm, where he did his best to hold the ship to its course. From one o’clock until midnight, he was at the helm. He feared he was going to die, and if the Christian faith were true, then he surely would not be forgiven. He reflected on all he had done over the past few years. His life seemed as ruined and wrecked as the battered ship he was trying to steer through the storm. During those long and grueling hours, Newton cried out to God like he never had before, and that was the turning point in his life.

That was a day John Newton remembered ever after. “On that day, the Lord sent from on high and delivered me out of deep waters.” Over 50 years later, John wrote in his diary on March 21, 1805: “Not well able to write; but I endeavor to observe the return of this day with humiliation, prayer, and praise.”

Only God’s amazing grace could take a rude, profane, slave-trading sailor and transform him into a child of God. John never ceased to stand in awe of God’s work in his life. He took an interest in prayer, reading and meditating on the Scriptures, and only speaking words pleasing to God.

On his return home, Mary and her parents recognized the change the Lord had brought in John. The two were married on February 1, 1750.

For the next four years, Newton was captain of his own slave ship. This occupation kept him separated from Mary for months at a time. While they were apart, the two corresponded constantly. In his letters, John repeatedly wrote how their love and marriage increased his thankfulness and gratefulness to the Lord. “... When I indulge myself with a particular thought of you, it usually carries me on farther and brings me upon my knees to bless the Lord for giving me such a treasure and to pray for your peace and welfare”

John endeavored to “Christianize” his slave ship by holding Sunday services for his crew of 30 sin-hardened men. He made three more voyages to bring slaves from Africa to North America. As he planned his fourth trip, he became sick with malaria. God used this sickness to end his involvement in the slave trade.

As John began a new chapter in his life, he felt called to be a minister. For more than 50 years, he preached the gospel and was one of the most influential men of his day.

John Newton often composed a hymn to go with his Sunday evening services. In 1779, 280 of these were collected and combined with 68 hymns by Newton’s friend and parishioner, William Cowper, and published as the Olney Hymns. The most famous of all the Olney Hymns, “Faith’s Review and Expectation”, grew out of David’s exclamation in 1 Chronicles 17:16-17. We know it today as “Amazing Grace”. “Amazing Grace” originally had six stanzas, and the last verse was added about a century later. Most hymnals have four or five of these verses.

As minister in the church, John continued to be more and more troubled by the slave trade that was still going on. In 1788, 34 years after he left the slave trade, He wrote a book entitled Thoughts Upon the African Slave Trade and sent it to all the members of parliament. This book brought an awareness to the public of the evils of the slave trade. He quotes this, “Needless to say, the capturing, selling and transporting of black slaves to the plantations in the West Indies and America was a cruel and vicious way of life.” With the help and providence of God, John saw the day, several months before his death, in 1807, when slavery was officially banned from England.

When John was in his sixties, his beloved wife Mary passed away. This was a great trial for John, and he spent the remaining 17 years of his life without her.

After John suffered a stroke and shortly before his death, a spokesman for the church encouraged Newton to consider retiring from preaching because of failing health, eyesight, and memory. John replied, “What, shall the old African blasphemer stop while he can still speak? I will continue to preach. Although my memory’s fading, I remember two things very clearly: I am a great sinner, and Christ is a great Savior.”

The last words of John Newton as he lay on his deathbed were as follows: “I am still in the land of the dying; I shall be in the land of the living soon.”

The tune “Amazing Grace” is an early American folk melody. It was first known as a plantation melody entitled “Loving Lambs”. This tune was first published in 1831 in the book The Virginia Harmony. The majority of hymn books published after this time included this song. In 1910, Edwin O. Excell added the last verse, which eventually replaced the last three original verses of the song. His edition of the song is most common in our hymnals today. Several other Olney hymns by Newton continue to be sung today, including “How Sweet the Name of Jesus Sounds” and “Glorious Things of Thee are Spoken”.

Hur ofattbart är det inte att Gud kan ta en eländig syndare, utan fruktan för Herren, och förvandla honom till en helig människa, renad i blodet, och en förkunnare av evangeliet! I denna berättelse ser vi Guds livsförvandlande kraft verka i vår psalmförfattares liv.

På den lilla kyrkogården i Olney i England står en gravsten av granit med denna inskrift, som Newton själv skrev före sin död:

John Newton, en gång en gudsförnekare och utsvävande människa, en slavars tjänare i Afrika, blev genom vår Herre och Frälsare Jesu Kristi rika barmhärtighet bevarad, återupprättad, förlåten och utsedd att predika den tro som han länge hade arbetat för att förstöra!

Denna gravskrift beskriver väl denne mans ovanliga och färgstarka liv. Han var en av 1700-talets stora evangeliska förkunnare. Hans vittnesbörd var: ”Genom Guds nåd är jag vad jag är!”

”Amazing Grace” var en psalm som publicerades 1779, med en text skriven 1772 av den engelske poeten och anglikanske prästen John Newton (1725–1807). ”Amazing Grace” är förmodligen de senaste två århundradenas mest älskade psalm. Den beräknas framföras 10 miljoner gånger om året. Den har förekommit på över 11 000 album och översatts till omkring 60 språk. Den omnämndes i Harriet Beecher Stowes roman mot slaveriet, Onkel Toms stuga. Dess popularitet ökade kraftigt under två av Amerikas största kriser: inbördeskriget och Vietnamkriget.

Ironiskt nog skrevs denna gripande sång, som är nära förknippad med den afroamerikanska befolkningen, av en före detta slavhandlare, John Newton.

John föddes den 24 juli 1725 i Wapping i England. Hans far, John Newton den äldre, var sjöman, och hans mor, Elizabeth Newton, var en hängiven kristen. Hans far älskade honom men var borta till sjöss större delen av tiden. Hans mor däremot var öm och omsorgsfull och undervisade honom i Guds ord. Hon lärde honom att memorera hela kapitel ur Bibeln åt gången och tog med honom till kyrkan. När han var nästan sju år gammal dog hans mor tyvärr i tuberkulos. Hans far gifte om sig en kort tid senare och skickade honom till en internatskola. Under tiden på internatskolan fick han dåliga vänner. Hans karaktär försämrades så mycket att han blev relegerad från en skola och flyttad till en annan. När han var 11 år ville internatskolorna inte längre ha honom, så hans far tog med honom till sjöss. De följande sex åren tillbringade han på Atlanten tillsammans med sin far.

När John var 17 år ordnade hans far så att han skulle skickas till Jamaica för ett välbetalt arbete som tillsynsman på en plantage. På vägen dit, medan han väntade på fartygets avgång, blev John inbjuden hem till några gamla vänner, familjen Catlett. Det var i detta hem som Johns mor hade dött tio år tidigare. När han återknöt kontakten med dem lärde han känna deras dotter Mary. Johns och Marys mödrar hade varit de bästa vänner. John hade blivit inbjuden att stanna i fyra dagar, men han stannade i två veckor och missade fartyget till Jamaica.

Vid 18 års ålder tvångsvärvades John till den brittiska flottan, och hans liv gick från dåligt till ännu sämre. Han ville återvända och träffa Mary, så han deserterade från fartyget men blev infångad, piskad offentligt och lagd i bojor. Hans liv på fartyget var så ogudaktigt att till och med de andra gudlösa sjömännen ryggade tillbaka inför hans svordomar och hädelser. Han fick tillnamnet ”Den store hädaren” och var så oönskad ombord att han skickades för att arbeta på ett slavskepp.

En av ägarna till slavskeppet där han nu arbetade erbjöd John ett arbete när de nådde den afrikanska kusten. Men väl i land bands han och tvingades arbeta med föga mat, kläder eller tak över huvudet. Under denna tid skickade han flera brev hem till sin far och vädjade om hjälp.

Ett fartyg som hette The Greyhound seglade nära den kust som John nu hade kommit att kalla sitt hem. Kaptenen hade fått i uppdrag av Johns far att leta efter hans son. Trots att fartyget var nästan för långt från land för att bedriva handel bestämde man sig för att försöka. En vän till John rodde ut från stranden för att handla. När han vände sig om för att ge sig av frågade kaptenen om han kände någon som hette John Newton. Till kaptenens förvåning gjorde han det, och John fördes ombord för att resa hem.

Ombord på fartyget tog Newton upp ett exemplar av Thomas a Kempis kristna klassiker Om Kristi efterföljelse. Han hade aldrig stött på något liknande, och han började undra om de kristna påståendena kunde vara sanna. Den natten, den 10 mars 1748, höll en våldsam storm på att sänka fartyget. Män, djur och proviant spolades överbord. Stormen väckte Newton; vågorna hade brutit sönder fartygets murkna timmer, och vatten virvlade in i hans hytt. John bad för första gången på flera år.

The Greyhound kastades omkring i stormen på Nordatlanten i över 11 dagar. Med föga hopp om att överleva arbetade sjömännen mekaniskt vid pumparna och försökte hålla fartyget flytande. På stormens elfte dag var John för utmattad för att pumpa, så han bands vid rodret, där han gjorde sitt bästa för att hålla fartyget på rätt kurs. Från klockan ett till midnatt stod han vid rodret. Han fruktade att han skulle dö, och om den kristna tron var sann skulle han säkerligen inte bli förlåten. Han tänkte på allt han hade gjort under de senaste åren. Hans liv tycktes lika förstört och sönderslaget som det illa tilltygade fartyg han försökte styra genom stormen. Under dessa långa och plågsamma timmar ropade Newton till Gud som han aldrig tidigare hade gjort, och det blev vändpunkten i hans liv.

Det var en dag som John Newton mindes resten av sitt liv. ”Den dagen sände Herren hjälp från höjden och räddade mig ur djupa vatten.” Mer än 50 år senare skrev John i sin dagbok den 21 mars 1805: ”Har svårt att skriva, men jag försöker uppmärksamma denna dags återkomst med ödmjukhet, bön och lovprisning.”

Endast Guds förunderliga nåd kunde ta en ohyfsad, hädisk, slavhandlande sjöman och förvandla honom till ett Guds barn. John upphörde aldrig att förundras över Guds verk i sitt liv. Han började intressera sig för bön, för att läsa och begrunda Skriften och för att bara tala ord som behagade Gud.

När han återvände hem såg Mary och hennes föräldrar den förändring som Herren hade åstadkommit i John. De två gifte sig den 1 februari 1750.

Under de följande fyra åren var Newton kapten på sitt eget slavskepp. Detta yrke höll honom skild från Mary i månader åt gången. Medan de var åtskilda brevväxlade de ständigt. I sina brev skrev John gång på gång om hur deras kärlek och äktenskap ökade hans tacksamhet till Herren. ”... När jag tillåter mig att dröja vid en särskild tanke på dig, för den mig vanligen vidare och får mig att falla på knä för att välsigna Herren för att han har gett mig en sådan skatt och för att be om din frid och välgång.”

John försökte ”kristna” sitt slavskepp genom att hålla söndagsgudstjänster för sin besättning på 30 män som var förhärdade i synd. Han gjorde ytterligare tre resor för att föra slavar från Afrika till Nordamerika. När han planerade sin fjärde resa insjuknade han i malaria. Gud använde denna sjukdom för att sätta punkt för hans deltagande i slavhandeln.

När John inledde ett nytt kapitel i sitt liv kände han sig kallad att bli präst. I mer än 50 år predikade han evangeliet och var en av sin tids mest inflytelserika män.

John Newton skrev ofta en psalm till sina söndagskvällsgudstjänster. År 1779 samlades 280 av dessa och sammanfördes med 68 psalmer av Newtons vän och församlingsmedlem William Cowper och publicerades som Olney Hymns. Den mest berömda av alla psalmerna i Olney Hymns, ”Trons återblick och förväntan”, växte fram ur Davids utrop i Första Krönikeboken 17:16-17. I dag känner vi den som ”Amazing Grace”. ”Amazing Grace” hade ursprungligen sex strofer, och den sista versen lades till omkring ett århundrade senare. De flesta psalmböcker har fyra eller fem av dessa verser.

Som präst i kyrkan blev John alltmer bekymrad över den slavhandel som fortfarande pågick. År 1788, 34 år efter att han hade lämnat slavhandeln, skrev han en bok med titeln Thoughts Upon the African Slave Trade och skickade den till alla parlamentsledamöter. Denna bok gjorde allmänheten medveten om slavhandelns ondska. Han citerar följande: ”Det behöver knappast sägas att tillfångatagandet, försäljningen och transporten av svarta slavar till plantagerna i Västindien och Amerika var ett grymt och ondskefullt sätt att leva.” Med Guds hjälp och försyn fick John uppleva dagen år 1807, några månader före sin död, då slaveriet officiellt förbjöds i England.

När John var i sextioårsåldern gick hans älskade hustru Mary bort. Detta var en svår prövning för John, och han tillbringade de återstående 17 åren av sitt liv utan henne.

Efter att John hade drabbats av ett slaganfall, och kort före hans död, uppmanade en talesman för kyrkan Newton att överväga att sluta predika på grund av sviktande hälsa, syn och minne. John svarade: ”Vad, ska den gamle hädaren från Afrika sluta medan han fortfarande kan tala? Jag kommer att fortsätta predika. Även om mitt minne sviker minns jag två saker mycket tydligt: Jag är en stor syndare, och Kristus är en stor Frälsare.”

John Newtons sista ord när han låg på sin dödsbädd var dessa: ”Jag är fortfarande i de döendes land; snart ska jag vara i de levandes land.”

Melodin till ”Amazing Grace” är en tidig amerikansk folkmelodi. Den var först känd som en plantagemelodi med titeln ”Loving Lambs”. Denna melodi publicerades första gången 1831 i boken The Virginia Harmony. De flesta psalmböcker som publicerades efter denna tid innehöll sången. År 1910 lade Edwin O. Excell till den sista versen, som så småningom ersatte sångens tre sista ursprungliga verser. Hans version av sången är den vanligaste i våra psalmböcker i dag. Flera andra av Newtons psalmer i Olney Hymns sjungs fortfarande i dag, däribland ”Hur ljuvligt Jesu namn klingar” och ”Härliga ting sägs om dig”.
