Posso ancora sentire l'invitante cacofonia di odori mentre stringevo la mano forte di mio padre, facendomi largo tra la folla di turisti che affollava l'edificio. I venditori al Green Dragon Farmer’s Market a Ephrata, PA, facevano del loro meglio per attirare acquirenti con file di pesce fresco sul ghiaccio, formaggi di ogni tipo, salumi e panini, e cumuli di frutta fresca. E, oh, le caramelle! La mia giovane mente da prescolare non aveva mai visto così tanti dolci deliziosi tutti insieme.

Gli ultimi due giorni per me sono stati come il ragazzino al negozio di caramelle. Ho avuto il privilegio di partecipare al primo Annual Writers’ Conference di Christian Aid Ministries. Ho incrociato autori noti come Katrina Hoover Lee, Johnny Miller e Ruthann Stelfox. Ho chiacchierato con aspiranti scrittori e insegnanti di lungo corso. Ho avuto l'opportunità di assistere per ore a workshop ispiratori e formativi su come scrivere per comunicare, usare dialoghi realistici, scrittura descrittiva e molto altro. Avevamo tutti un obiettivo comune. Insieme condividiamo e impariamo come comunicare efficacemente ciò che abbiamo nel cuore e, attraverso il potere della parola scritta, trasmettere quei pensieri ai vostri cuori.

Il Battito del Residuo è un mezzo per comunicare pensieri ispiratori a lettori desiderosi sparsi nel mondo. Scrittori coraggiosi si fanno avanti con penna e carta o con tastiera e monitor e aiutano a diffondere la Buona Novella della Parola di Dio con cautela, correzione ed edificazione. Eppure, abbiamo bisogno di altri scrittori simili. Abbiamo bisogno di giovani credenti che con coraggio presentino i loro primi racconti per bambini. Di nonni navigati che portino parole di ammonimento alla generazione più giovane. Di madri che condividano esperienze e prove con altre madri che stanno crescendo dei piccoli. Di giovani che incoraggino i coetanei a tendere verso il premio della suprema vocazione in Cristo Gesù. Di padri che con occhio preoccupato osservano il mondo che preme sulle case cristiane. Insieme, questi aspiranti scrittori produrranno un periodico che durerà sul tavolino da caffè delle famiglie per molti anni. Vi incoraggio, fratelli credenti, a provarci. Nelson Mandela, ex presidente del Sud Africa, scrisse: “Il fallimento è un maestro, e alla fine della tua vita, cosa pensi che ti farà sentire peggio: fallire o non aver mai provato?”

The Berean Voice si propone di fornire materiale stampato che aiuti i lettori a orientarsi attraverso le stagioni varie e difficili della vita. Tutto il nostro materiale è disponibile gratuitamente, ma siamo dipendenti dalle donazioni dei nostri sostenitori. Ecco un elenco dei libri che abbiamo a disposizione:

Nel 2017 e nel 2018, The Berean Voice ha pubblicato una serie di articoli sui vaccini nella rivista Il Battito del Residuo. Questi articoli sono stati un sincero tentativo di esaminare vari aspetti dell'uso dei vaccini con un approccio imparziale. Abbiamo cercato di presentare i fatti nel modo più chiaro possibile e lasciare che i lettori traessero le proprie conclusioni.

Da allora abbiamo ricevuto numerose richieste dai nostri lettori di pubblicare tutti gli articoli sui vaccini in un opuscolo, cosa alla quale abbiamo acconsentito. Ma poi è arrivato il 2019, portando con sé il coronavirus. Questo evento monumentale ha sconvolto il dibattito sui vaccini e ha dato il via a una frenesia per portare sul mercato rimedi per il COVID-19, molti dei quali non sono stati adeguatamente testati. Abbiamo sospeso la stampa, incerti sul fatto di includere informazioni su questi nuovi e non provati “vaccini” per il COVID-19. Col passare del tempo e con l'attenuarsi della natura letale del COVID-19, abbiamo deciso di pubblicare gli articoli originali sui vaccini in un opuscolo senza ulteriori articoli sul dibattito relativo al COVID-19. Siamo lieti che il progetto sia vicino al completamento e sarà annunciato quando verrà pubblicato.

Benedizioni a tutti,

Edward Martin

Our Father’s world is a world unspoiled by human invention and intervention. While sin and technology have warped and stolen many lovely things from the human race, there abide still a few that remain unmarred by civilization. Little children in the fresh innocence of their unsoiled morning top the ranks as a bit of heaven on earth and call all observers heavenward. Another is the fowl of the air as prescribed in Genesis. Paul pleaded with the Corinthian church, “Doth not nature itself teach you?” We are exhorted to consider the lilies, the ravens, and the grass of the field. Each of these bears a significant dimension of the eternal God in their existence and gives us definition to their Creator. Perhaps all of nature can give us snapshots into heavenly places if we had the time and eyes to observe it.

Birds hold a unique place in God’s creation, for their sphere is in the heavens. Man may mount on the wings of a plane and evade the lower earth for a few hours, but the heavens will never be a place of his common dominion. The birds are a picture of a heavenly race, for they are at home there. They are a natural representation of the saints and angels of God and so we do well to give them due attention. While there may be dozens of lessons to be drawn from these vessels of grace and beauty, one of the most prominent and outstanding virtues will be observed in the song that they raise. Many animals dwelling on the earth are virtually mute. Of the ones that do speak, it is often to threaten or express complaint. “Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?” (Job 6:5). When they are happy and content, they have no message to convey. The dog barks at an intruder to drive him away, while the cat mews for attention. They speak when they are threatened or dissatisfied, in fear or in pain. Similarly, the earthly human shares its nature with the mammals of the field.

Birds are diverse. They exercise their joyous vocals so much that they are the epitome of happiness. The expression “happy as a lark” is so common a term that it is used by people who have never even ventured to the meadow to see or hear a lark. While some may inform us that these songs are mere mating calls and have little to do with their feelings, we cannot escape the inner conviction that, whether mating or not, these birds delight in bearing a jubilant expression of joy and we do well to let them teach us. “Is any merry? Let him sing psalms” (James 5:13). The birds do this incessantly and it seems impossible to draw any other conclusion but that they are happy while doing so. Wander near the nest of a swallow and you will find that they have ways of expressing depreciation as well. The killdeer also has no qualms with expressing rash disfavor to those who intrude their domain, but these are not to be mistaken as songs. The singing birds are a beautiful painted picture of the saints and angels of God.

How little knowledge of heaven is committed to our understanding. The scenes of heavens described and laid out before us in Revelations can hardly bring our finite minds into its infinite realm. One dimension that we can connect with is that it is a place filled with singing. Little wonder, for it is the culminating end of the contented and joy-filled saints of God, and there they will sing a new song. Nearly every scene at the throne in Revelations is marked by some dimension of praise. “And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God” (Ps 40:3). On 22 occasions, the Scriptures reiterate the phrase, I will sing.

It is the nature of the birds to sing. It is their waking thought as morning guilds the sky, and it flows from within them like a fountain. Not all of their songs are alike. Some are elaborate in their duration, meter, and pitch, while others are plain. Some merely chirp with a merry heart. The robin opens up the choir in early spring, but his song is soon surpassed in beauty by the song sparrow and again by the rose-breasted grosbeak. The song of the wren trumps them all for longevity and vibrancy. The canary sings in a cage, while the nightingale sings in the dark. The robins sing in the rain. The buntings fill in the heat of the day when other birds are silent. As diverse as their song may be, they all commonly burst forth in exuberant happiness. It is here that they shall instruct us.

“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord” (Eph 5:19). The advent of Christ was marked by the angelic host announcing peace and goodwill toward men. All those who will bear His name must deliver the same tidings. In John 4, we happen upon the scene at Jacob’s well, where Christ asks the woman for a drink. Her reply seems to bear a tinge of bitterness. “Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” Though she esteemed herself as a spiritual person and willingly followed Him into religious discourse, she had no song. Like the well that they speak over, her water was buried deep below the surface and how laborious the effort to bring it forth. Christ offers another alternative. “But the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

The well of Christ is an artesian well. One needs neither pitcher nor labor to draw it out, for it spews forth abundantly on its own accord. While Christ is probably speaking of the Spirit as in John 7:38, surely this may be just as applicable to a joy-laden heart. What is a more apt outpouring to flow from a Christ-inspired wellspring than the rapture of a song? “Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart” (Is 65:14). Now this should all seem plain enough to understand and easy enough to do but, alas, we find we have a constant and persistent adversary who seeks to thwart our song. We are not unaware of his devices...

Sin. Not all birds sing. There are some whose visage is black as sin. These only seem to screech and scream and are no example for the saints of God to emulate. The babbling noise we hear emanating from many passing vehicles certainly parallels the songs of such foul fowl. “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird” (Rev 18:2). These abundant creatures are the fallen spirits, the fowls waiting to devour the seed sown by the wayside. Of such are the worthless blackbirds, starlings, and grackles. The crows show themselves also at the roadside, feeding on rotting carcasses. Often you will find them in large numbers feeding themselves on the corn the farmer painstakingly planted for himself. So transgresses the selfish soul in his pursuit of happiness, feeding gleefully on the calamity of another and exploiting their sin. He bears no song, for his day is constantly clouded by the misdeeds of others who cross his path.

Neglect. The cowbird is also black (the female is brown/gray). She will be found sitting on a high vantage, shamelessly calling to her lovers by her shrill screeching. She then has the audacity to lay her egg in another bird’s nest, forcing them to raise her offspring. This is certainly a fitting emblem for a good number of females in our day. Though justified by circumstances, these women care not for their own, but are products of neglect. They have no lullaby to share with their young, for they have escorted them to the nest of another while her mind is preoccupied with work and business. “But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts” (Ps 22:9). No doubt that the singing mother can implant copious songs in her infant and set the stage for a happy and hope-filled life. While we may show mercy to a woman in dire circumstances, the major song of modern women bears chords that are but dissident and melancholy. These are stopped-up wells like unto the wells that Isaac found upon his return to Gerar. The Philistines “had filled them with earth” (Gen 26:15). So run the spiritually neglected homes of many families today, who pack their schedules so full of earthly commitments that they have no time to spend an hour in song together. If the birds stopped singing, would they even notice?

Ingratitude. Find a soul bathed in unthankfulness, and you will find a soul without a song. If the canary were to refuse to sing in captivity, few of us would ever have heard his rollicking melody. “We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD’S song in a strange land?” (Ps 137:2-4). God’s people had been instructed by Jeremiah to build houses, plant gardens, and raise families. “… And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace” (Jer. 29:5-7). But they could see no worth in it. With their eyes fixed upon the dismal scene around them, they lost their song. Israel had within its history a rich tradition of song. Their singing erupted at the passage of the Red Sea in the days of Jehoshaphat and had been known to defeat armies. Earthly discomfort is no excuse to withhold gratitude, for our God reigns, and we are His children. Such were the conditions of the Philippian prison where two jailbirds, Paul and Silas, opened the concert at midnight and rocked the corridors with their joyful singing.

When we open our mouths and stretch our vocals in praise, we enact the grace of God. We join the faithful choir alongside Miriam, Deborah, and Hannah, and blend harmoniously with Moses, David, Paul, and Barnabas. At evening, we sing with our Lord and His disciples after supper, and with legions of angels “giving glory to God in the highest.” If that isn’t enough, perhaps we should consider rising at early dawn and singing with the innumerable hosts of our feathered friends who are thankful for God’s loving providence. “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord … And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men” (Col 3:16, 23).

हामारे पिता की दुनिया मानव अविष्कार और हस्तक्षेप से अप्रभावित दुनिया है। जबकि पाप और प्रौद्योगिकी ने मानव जाति से कई सुन्दर चीजें विकृत और छीन ली हैं, फिर भी कुछ ऐसे हैं जो सभ्यता द्वारा अप्रभावित बने हुए हैं। उनके मधुर, अनलक्षित प्रभात में बिना दाग के छोटे बच्चे पृथ्वी पर स्वर्ग के सामान हैं और सभी प्रेक्षकों को स्वर्ग की ओर खींच लेते हैं। एक और है उत्पत्ति में निर्देशित वायु के परिंदे। पौलुस कोरिंथ के गिरजाघर से निवेदन करते थे, “Doth not nature itself teach you?” हमें लिलियों, कौवों और खेत की घास पर विचार करने के लिए प्रेरित किया जाता है। इन प्रत्येक के अस्तित्व में अनन्त ईश्वर का एक महत्वपूर्ण आयाम विद्यमान है और वे हमें अपने स्रष्टा की परिभाषा देते हैं। शायद संपूर्ण प्रकृति हमें स्वर्गीय स्थानों के झलकियाँ दे सकती है यदि हमारे पास देखने और समझने का समय और आँखें हों।

परिंदों का परमेश्वर की सृष्टि में एक विशिष्ट स्थान है, क्योंकि उनका क्षेत्र आकाश में है। मानव हवाई जहाज के पंखों पर चढ़कर कुछ घंटे के लिए निचली पृथ्वी से बच सकता है, परन्तु आकाश कभी भी उसकी सामान्य साम्राज्य की जगह नहीं होगा। परिंदे स्वर्गीय जाति की एक तस्वीर हैं, क्योंकि वे उसी में गृहस्थ हैं। वे परमेश्वर के संतों और स्वर्गदूतों का प्राकृतिक प्रतिनिधित्व हैं और इसलिए हमें उन्हें ध्यानपूर्वक देखना चाहिए। यद्यपि इन कृपा और सुंदरता के पात्रों से सदियों तक अनेक पाठ निकाले जा सकते हैं, परन्तु उनमें से सबसे प्रमुख और विशिष्ट गुण उनके द्वारा उठाए जाने वाले गीत में निहित रहेगा। जमीन पर रहने वाले कई जानवर लगभग मूक हैं। जो बोलते भी हैं, वे अक्सर धमकी देने या शिकायत व्यक्त करने के लिए बोलते हैं। “Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?” (Job 6:5). जब वे प्रसन्न और संतुष्ट होते हैं, तो उनके पास व्यक्त करने के लिए कोई संदेश नहीं होता। कुत्ता अतिक्रमणकारी पर भौंकता है ताकि उसे भगा सके, जबकि बिल्ली ध्यान के लिए म्याऊँ करती है। वे भय या पीड़ा में या खतरे में बोलते हैं। इसी प्रकार, पृथ्वी का मानव अपने स्वभाव में मैदान के स्तनों के साथ साझा करता है।

पक्षी विविध हैं। वे अपने आनंदमय स्वरों का इतना अभ्यास करते हैं कि वे खुशियों का प्रतीक बन जाते हैं। अभिव्यक्ति “खुश जैसे एक लार्क” इतनी आम है कि उसे वे लोग भी उपयोग करते हैं जिन्होंने कभी घास के मैदान में जाकर लार्क को देखने या सुनने की हिमाकत नहीं की। जबकि कुछ लोग हमें बताएँगे कि ये गीत मात्र मिलन कॉल हैं और इनके भावनाओं से कम लेना-देना है, हम उस अंतःप्रत्यय से बच नहीं सकते कि, चाहे मिलन हो या न हो, ये पक्षी उल्लासित हर्ष व्यक्त करने में आनंद लेते हैं और हमें उन्हें सीखने देना चाहिए। “Is any merry? Let him sing psalms” (James 5:13). पक्षी यह लगातार करते हैं और ऐसा लगना असंभव है कि हम किसी अन्य निष्कर्ष पर पहुँचें सिवाय इसके कि वे यह करते हुए प्रसन्न हैं। किसी स्वालो की घोंसले के पास घूमें और आप पाएँगे कि उनके पास अवमूल्यन व्यक्त करने के तरीके भी हैं। किल्डियर भी अपने क्षेत्र में अतिक्रमण करने वालों के प्रति तीव्र नापसंदगी व्यक्त करने में संकोच नहीं करता, पर इन्हें गीत न समझा जाए। गाने वाले पक्षी परमेश्वर के संतों और स्वर्गदूतों की एक सुन्दर चित्रित तस्वीर हैं।

हमारे समझ में स्वर्ग का कितना कम ज्ञान संचित है। प्रकाशितवाक्य में वर्णित और हमारे सामने रखे गए स्वर्ग के दृश्यों से हमारी सीमित मनक की अनन्त वैश्विकता में लाना कठिन है। एक आयाम जिससे हम जुड़ सकते हैं वह यह है कि यह एक ऐसा स्थान है जो गानों से भरा हुआ है। आश्चर्य की कोई बात नहीं, क्योंकि यह परमेश्वर के संतों की संतुष्ट और आनन्द-पूर्ण चरम समाप्ति है, और वहां वे एक नया गीत गायेंगे। सिंहासन पर लगभग हर दृश्य प्रशंसा के किसी न किसी आयाम से चिह्नित है। “And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God” (Ps 40:3). 22 अवसरों पर, शास्त्र वाक्यांश, I will sing, दोहराते हैं।

गाना पक्षियों का स्वभाव है। यह उनका जागरण विचार है जब सुबह आकाश को रंगती है, और यह उनके भीतर से एक फव्वारे की तरह प्रवाहित होता है। उनके सभी गीत समान नहीं होते। कुछ अपने अवधी, मीटर और पिच में विस्तृत होते हैं, जबकि अन्य सरल होते हैं। कुछ केवल हर्षित हृदय से चहकते हैं। रॉबिन शुरुआती वसंत में गायन-दलीयता खोलता है, पर उसका गीत शीघ्र ही सॉन्ग स्पैरो और फिर रोज-ब्रेस्टेड ग्रॉसबीक के गीत से श्रेष्ठता में पीछे रह जाता है। रेन का गीत उनकी सभी से लंबाई और जीवंतता में बढ़कर ट्रम्प करता है। कैनरी पिंजरे में गाती है, जबकि नाइटिंगेल अँधेरे में गाती है। रॉबिन वर्षा में गाते हैं। बन्टिंग्स उन दिनों के गरमी में भर देते हैं जब अन्य पक्षी मौन रहते हैं। उनकी आवाज कितनी भी विविध हो, वे सभी आम तौर पर उल्लासित खुशी में फूट पड़ते हैं। यहीं से वे हमें निर्देशित करेंगे।

“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord” (Eph 5:19). मसीह का आगमन दैवीय दूतों की होस्ट द्वारा शांति और मनुष्यों के प्रति सद्भाव की घोषणा से चिन्हित था। सभी जो उसका नाम धारण करेंगे वे वही समाचार पहुँचना चाहेंगे। यूहन्ना 4 में, हम याकूब के कुएँ के पास के दृश्य पर पहुँचते हैं, जहाँ मसीह उस स्त्री से एक घूँट माँगते हैं। उसकी प्रतिक्रिया कड़वाहट का स्पर्श लगती है। “Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” यद्यपि उसने स्वयं को आध्यात्मिक व्यक्ति माना और स्वेच्छा से धार्मिक वार्तालाप में उसका अनुसरण किया, उसके पास कोई गीत नहीं था। जिस कुएँ पर वे बोलते हैं, उसकी तरह उसका पानी सतह के नीचे गहरा दबा हुआ था और उसे निकालना कितना श्रमसाध्य था। मसीह एक और विकल्प प्रस्तुत करते हैं। “But the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

मसीह का कुआँ एक आर्टेजियन कुआँ है। उसे निकालने के लिए न तो घड़ा चाहिए न श्रम, क्योंकि यह स्वतंत्र रूप से प्रचुर मात्रा में फूटता है। जबकि मसीह शायद यूहन्ना 7:38 में बताए गए आत्मा की बात कर रहे हैं, निसन्देह यह आनंद से भरे हृदय पर भी समान रूप से लागू हो सकता है। मसीह-प्रेरित स्रोत से बहने के लिए किस बात से अधिक उपयुक्त बहाव है यदि नृत्य-जैसी खुशी का गीत न हो? “Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart” (Is 65:14). अब यह सब समझने में सरल और करने में सहज लगना चाहिए परन्तु, अफसोस, हमें एक लगातार और दृढ़ प्रतिद्वन्द्वी मिलता है जो हमारे गीत को विफल करने की کوشش करता है। हम उसके उपकरणों से अनभिज्ञ नहीं हैं...

पाप। सभी पक्षी नहीं गाते। कुछ ऐसे हैं जिनका स्वरूप पाप के समान काला है। ये केवल चीखने और चिल्लाने जैसे प्रतीत होते हैं और परमेश्वर के संतों के लिए अनुकरणीय नहीं हैं। हम कई गुजरते वाहनों से निकलने वाली बकवास आवाज़ को भी ऐसे गंदे परिंदों के गीतों के तुल्य पाते हैं। “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird” (Rev 18:2). ये प्रचुर जीव गिरे हुए आत्माएँ हैं, वे पंछी हैं जो उस बीज को निगलने के लिए प्रतीक्षा करते हैं जो सड़क के किनारे बोया गया है। ऐसे ही हैं बेकार काले पक्षी, स्टार्लिंग्स, और ग्रैकल्स। कौवे भी सड़क किनारे दिखते हैं, सड़े हुए शवों पर भोजन करते हैं। अक्सर आप उन्हें बड़ी संख्या में पाएँगे जो उस मकई पर भोजन कर रहे हैं जो किसान ने अपने लिए मेहनत करके बोई थी। इसी प्रकार सुख की खोज में स्वार्थी आत्मा अपराध करती है, दूसरों की विपत्ति पर आनंदपूर्वक भोजन करती है और उनके पाप का शोषण करती है। उसके पास कोई गीत नहीं है, क्योंकि उसका दिन हमेशा दूसरों की बुराइयों से छाया हुआ रहता है जो उसके मार्ग में आती हैं।

उपेक्षा। कौयाई पक्षी भी काला होता है (मादा भूरा/धूसर होती है)। उसे ऊँचे स्थान पर बैठे पाया जाएगा, निःसंकोच अपने प्रेमियों को तेज़ चिल्लाहट से बुलाते हुए। फिर उसके पास दुस्साहस होता है कि वह अपना अंडा दूसरे पक्षी के घोंसले में दे दे, और उन्हें मजबूर करे कि वे उसकी संतानों को पाले। यह निश्चित रूप से हमारे समय की कई महिलाओं के लिए एक उपयुक्त प्रतिक है। हालात द्वारा न्यायोचित ठहराए जाने के बावजूद, ये महिलाएँ अपने लोगों की परवाह नहीं करतीं, बल्कि उपेक्षा की पैदाइश होती हैं। उनके पास अपने नवजात को सुनाने के लिए कोई लोरी नहीं होती, क्योंकि उन्होंने उन्हें किसी और के घोंसले में छोड़ा होता है जबकि उनका मन कार्य और व्यापार में व्यस्त रहता है। “But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts” (Ps 22:9). निस्संदेह गीतात्मक माँ अपने शिशु में प्रचुर गीत अंकित कर सकती है और एक खुश और आशा-भरी जिंदगी के लिए मंच स्थापित कर सकती है। जबकि हम विपन्न स्त्री पर दया दिखा सकते हैं, आधुनिक महिलाओं का प्रमुख गीत वे तार बजाता है जो केवल असहमत और उदासीन होते हैं। ये उन बंद कुओँ जैसे हैं जो इसहाक ने गेहड़ लौटकर पाए थे। फिलिस्तियों ने “had filled them with earth” (Gen 26:15). आज कई परिवारों के आध्यात्मिक रूप से उपेक्षित घर ऐसे ही चलते हैं, जो अपने कार्यक्रमों को सांसारिक प्रतिबद्धताओं से इतना भर देते हैं कि उनके पास साथ में एक घंटा गीत में बिताने का समय ही नहीं होता। यदि पक्षी गाना बंद कर दें, तो क्या वे हैरान भी होंगे?

अकृतज्ञता। अकृतज्ञता में नहा हुआ कोई भी व्यक्ति ढूँढो, और तुम ऐसे व्यक्ति पाओगे जिसके पास गीत नहीं है। यदि कैनरी बंदी अवस्था में गाना ही छोड़ दे, तो हम में से बहुत-से लोग कभी उसके उल्लसित संगीत को नहीं सुन पाते। “We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD’S song in a strange land?” (Ps 137:2-4). ईश्वर के लोग Jeremiah द्वारा निर्देशित थे कि वे घर बनाएं, बगिचे लगाएँ, और परिवार बढ़ाएँ. “… And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace” (Jer. 29:5-7). पर वे उसमें कोई मूल्य नहीं देख सके। अपने दृष्टि को चारों ओर के उदास दृश्य पर टिका देखकर, उन्होंने अपना गीत खो दिया। इज़राइल के इतिहास में गीत की एक समृद्ध परम्परा थी। उनका गायन लाल समुद्र के पार के समय फूट पड़ा था और यह युद्धों को हराने के लिए जाना जाता था। सांसारिक असुविधा आभार व्यक्त करने से रोकेगी नहीं, क्योंकि हमारा परमेश्वर राज्य करता है, और हम उसके बच्चे हैं। ऐसे ही परिस्थितियाँ फिलिप्पियन जेल की थीं जहाँ दो कैदी, पौलुस और साइलस, मध्यरात्रि में कंसर्ट खोलते हैं और अपने हर्षित गान से गलियारों को झँका देते हैं।

जब हम अपने मुख खोलते हैं और स्तुति में स्वर फैलाते हैं, तो हम परमेश्वर की कृया का अभिनय करते हैं। हम मीरियम, देबोरा, और हन्ना के साथ विश्वासी गायकों की मंडली में शामिल होते हैं, और मूसा, दाऊद, पौलुस, और बर्नबास के साथ सामंजस्यपूर्ण मिश्रण करते हैं। संध्या में, हम अपने प्रभु और उसके चेलों के साथ भोजन के बाद गाते हैं, और अनगिनत स्वर्गदूतों के साथ “giving glory to God in the highest.” यदि यह काफी नहीं है, तो शायद हमें भोर उठकर हमारे पंखधारी मित्रों की अनगिनत होस्टों के साथ गाना चाहिए जो ईश्वर की प्रेमपूर्ण प्राविडेंस के लिए आभारी हैं। “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord … And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men” (Col 3:16, 23).

Arise be glad! For dawn is here!
Rejoice and sing! The night is past,
The Dayspring shineth from on high,
The grace of God to man is nigh!
Rejoice and praise the King of Kings!
Give thanks and laud, for more is here!

Arise and glorify the Lord!
Extol and praise His worthy name!
He shineth from the heav’ns in love,
And showers blessings from above,
His mercy reaches down to men-
Adore and praise our mighty Lord!

Give thanks and sing to Christ our King
And worship Him with reverent praise;
Bow down in awful, holy fear-
The Holiness of God is here;
In wondrous beauty bend the knee;
Adore th’ almighty King of Kings!

Eight-year-old Jamin wasn’t very smart. Or at least that’s what his older brother told him. Almost daily, brother Kenny found ways to remind Jamin of his shortcomings and laugh at his blunders.

“Jamin, you will never be smart”, Kenny said. Deep inside Jamin felt resigned to a life of muddled trip-ups. Would he always be clumsy? Would he always say things wrong? That’s what Kenny said.

Jamin believed Kenny’s lectures with wide-eyed belief. Kenny was three years older than him, so he must be right. Very well, then Jamin would be simple. Kenny would be smart. Life was not fair. Dad and Mom disliked Kenny’s proud talk and punished him whenever they walked in on one of his speeches. But Kenny had a way of avoiding earshot. So he continued mocking Jamin.

Grandma Otto watched these trials from her rocker on the porch. She was a quiet old lady.

“Jamin, do you know where Kenny is?” Mom asked with a smile. “It’s almost supper time.”

“He went to check his coyote traps. I’ll go find him.”

There was a chill in the air as he tramped up over the lawn, and the sun was growing old as he crossed the border of the woods. The fleeting shadows scurried over the hills. The chill deepened as he stumped further in. He breathed the rich air and followed Kenny’s trail. Eventually, the trail would end up in a meadow, but Jamin hoped he would find Kenny before he had to go that far. The various traps had been checked already, so Jamin knew Kenny had come this way. Jamin trudged on resolutely. His golden head caught the tired beams that fled from the sun as they flickered through the trees. And soon those too had faded leaving behind the musky smell of the woods. The fall webworms had been at work, and their web curtains shuttered from branches overhead.

At length, as the trees subdued and thinned, and the meadow appeared Jamin knew this was the end of his brother’s trap route. If Kenny wasn’t here, he wouldn’t know where else to look.

But Kenny was there. As Jamin clumped into the meadow, he could see a frustrated heap to his right. The heap’s voice had a familiar ring. The heap’s face was lit in pain. The heap was Kenny. “Are you alright? What happened?” Jamin felt strange, seeing Kenny scrunched in the dirt. Kenny was smart. “Did you step in a trap?”

“Yes, Jamin. I..I wasn’t looking where I was going. Help me. Please.”

Jamin bent and found an ankle firmly held in the jaws of a steel trap. Darkness stained the ground around Kenny. Quickly, Jamin’s strong arms pried open the jaws. Kenny reeled free. “Can you walk?”

“Yes. I think so. If you support me, I can hobble along.”

“Dad and Mom will be worried. We’ve missed supper.”

Sure enough, as the brothers hobbled back through the woods, they heard the long calling of their father. Jamin called back, and he was by their side in a moment, seeing the ankle and scooping up Kenny like a hurt sheep. The odd little band hurried home, and the screen door banged shut as Dad swept across the porch. Jamin went to the wash house and scrubbed his hands. He headed for the front door.

“Jamin.” It was Grandma. The porch light showed her in her old rocker. A heavy comforter lay on her shoulders.

“Yes, Grandma?”

“Do you think you are not very smart?”

“That’s what Kenny says.” Jamin squirmed.

“You were strong enough to open the trap, and Kenny wasn’t. You were brave enough to find him in the dark. Lots of young boys wouldn’t be.” Jamin was silent. Grandma Otto rocked some more, then smiled. “God made you the way you are for a reason, Jamin. He made Kenny the way he is for a reason. He has a plan for you, and a place only you can fill, you know.”

Jamin turned and walked into the warm kitchen. He was smiling.

De achtjarige Jamin was niet erg slim. Of althans dat zei zijn oudere broer tegen hem. Bijna elke dag vond broer Kenny manieren om Jamin aan zijn tekortkomingen te herinneren en te lachen om zijn misstappen.

“Jamin, je zult nooit slim zijn”, zei Kenny. Diep vanbinnen voelde Jamin zich berust in een leven vol verwarde struikelingen. Zou hij altijd onhandig blijven? Zou hij altijd dingen verkeerd zeggen? Dat zei Kenny.

Jamin geloofde Kennys preken met grote ogen. Kenny was drie jaar ouder, dus hij moest wel gelijk hebben. Goed dan, Jamin zou simpel zijn. Kenny zou slim zijn. Het leven was oneerlijk. Pa en Ma hielden niet van Kennys trotse praatjes en straften hem telkens als ze een van zijn toespraken opvingen. Maar Kenny wist hoe hij buiten gehoor kon blijven. Dus ging hij door met het uitschelden van Jamin.

Oma Otto keek vanuit haar schommelstoel op de veranda naar deze beproevingen. Ze was een stille oude vrouw.

“Jamin, weet je waar Kenny is?” vroeg Ma met een glimlach. “Het is bijna etenstijd.”

“Hij is zijn coyotenvallen gaan controleren. Ik zal hem zoeken.”

Er hing een kilte in de lucht toen hij over het gazon naar boven stapte, en de zon werd oud terwijl hij de grens van het bos overstak. De vluchtige schaduwen schoten over de heuvels. De kilte verdiepte zich naarmate hij dieper het bos in stapte. Hij ademde de rijke lucht in en volgde Kennys spoor. Uiteindelijk zou het pad in een wei uitkomen, maar Jamin hoopte Kenny te vinden voordat hij zo ver moest gaan. De verschillende vallen waren al gecontroleerd, dus Jamin wist dat Kenny deze kant op was gekomen. Jamin ploeterde vastberaden door. Zijn gouden hoofd ving de moegejaagde zonnestralen die door de bomen flikkerden. En spoedig waren ook die vervaagd en lieten de muskuslucht van het bos achter. De herfstspinners hadden hun werk gedaan en hun webgordijnen hingen van takken boven hem.

Ten langen leste, toen de bomen gelijkmatiger werden en dunner, en de wei verscheen, wist Jamin dat dit het einde van Kennys valroute was. Als Kenny hier niet was, wist hij niet waar anders hij moest zoeken.

Maar Kenny was daar. Toen Jamin de wei inklom, zag hij rechts een gefrustreerde hoop liggen. De stem van de hoop klonk bekend. Het gezicht van de hoop was van pijn verlicht. De hoop was Kenny. “Gaat het? Wat is er gebeurd?” Jamin voelde zich vreemd om Kenny zo ineengedoken in de modder te zien. Kenny was slim. “Ben je in een val getrapt?”

“Ja, Jamin. Ik… ik keek niet waar ik liep. Help me. Alsjeblieft.”

Jamin boog zich en vond een enkel die stevig door de kaken van een stalen val werd vastgehouden. Donkerte bevlekte de grond rond Kenny. Snel wreven Jamins sterke armen de kaken open. Kenny trok zich los. “Kun je lopen?”

“Ja. Ik denk het. Als je me ondersteunt, kan ik hinkelen.”

“Pa en Ma zullen zich zorgen maken. We hebben het eten gemist.”

Inderdaad, terwijl de broers terugstapten door het bos, hoorden ze het lange roepen van hun vader. Jamin riep terug, en hij stond op een ogenblik naast hen, zag de enkel en tilde Kenny op als een gewond schaap. Het rare gezelschap haastte zich naar huis en de hor deur sloeg dicht toen Pa over de veranda snelde. Jamin ging naar het washuis en schrobde zijn handen. Hij liep naar de voordeur.

“Jamin.” Het was Oma. Het licht op de veranda liet haar in haar oude schommelstoel zien. Een zware deken lag over haar schouders.

“Ja, Oma?”

“Denk je dat je niet erg slim bent?”

“Dat zegt Kenny.” Jamin wrong zich.

“Je was sterk genoeg om de val te openen, en Kenny niet. Je was dapper genoeg om hem in het donker te vinden. Veel jongens van jouw leeftijd zouden dat niet zijn.” Jamin zweeg. Oma Otto schommelde nog wat, en glimlachte toen. “God heeft je gemaakt zoals je bent met een doel, Jamin. Hij heeft Kenny zo gemaakt met een doel. Hij heeft een plan voor jou, en een plaats die alleen jij kunt vullen, weet je dat.”

Jamin draaide zich om en liep de warme keuken in. Hij glimlachte.

Do you believe in miracles? Do you believe in the supernatural? What about divine intervention? Or a better question might be, have you seen God working in your life? Do others see God working in your life?

My brother was working in the greenhouse when a customer walked in and marveled at the beauty of all the plants. He then exclaimed how impressed he was at all our hard work. My brother responded with, “Some plant, some water, but God gives the increase.” To which the customer responded with, “No, no, don’t give the credit to God. You came out here and did all this work. You planted, watered, and fertilized all these plants, and you all deserve the credit, not God!” The reason the man felt this way is because he was a humanist.

What is Humanism?

The dictionary defines humanism like this; an outlook or system of thought attaching prime importance to human rather than divine or supernatural matters. Humanist beliefs stress the potential value and goodness of human beings, emphasize common human needs, and seek solely rational ways of solving human problems.

If God does exist, then we will have to recognize this fact and answer to Him. Humanists attempt to prove that God does not exist, so they can freely live their lives as they please. According to humanism, there is no God. If so, then we, the human race, are superior to God. Everything is for us and our ultimate happiness. This is the definition of humanism.

Two Types of Humanism

There are two types of humanistic beliefs, and we will look at both. The first belief is the theory that there is no God. In reality, this seems to be the only rational way to be a humanist. Everything is created by man and for man. There are no other factors or supernatural involvement. Everything happens by reason and common sense. There is a logical explanation for everything that happens. Of course, some things do not make sense, but humanists brush those aside and look only at the things that can be explained. Like the plants in the greenhouse, they look at all that man does and ignore the supernatural part of a plant springing forth with new life. Scientists around the world are working diligently to put human reasoning into everything that has ever happened, even the creation of the world. Scientists, with all their learning and wisdom, attempt to give logical explanations for why natural disasters and global crises happen. If they can explain everything, then they can rule out God and His existence. This allows the human race to do as it pleases without eternal consequences. This, in turn leads to a great sense of false peace.

The humanists, with all their reasoning, mock the very existence of God. If you go to most colleges in America and talk to people about Christianity, they laugh at you and mock the fact that Christians actually believe in God.

The second type of humanistic belief is a theory of humanism that acknowledges the existence of God. One anthropologist argued that humanism is a project of modernity and a secularized continuation of Western Christian theology. But if you ask people what they think humanism means, you will likely get different responses, and it becomes very confusing. But why the confusion? Because people are trying to be Christian humanists. Christian Humanism has frequently been criticized for its vagueness and difficulty to define. The reason it has become so confusing is that people want to believe in God but also believe in themselves and that the world revolves around them.

In Romans, we read, “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them” (Romans 1:18-32).

So how can one be a humanist and believe in God? This is where we hit a little closer to home. This type of humanist believes God wants him to be happy. He believes in a Creator God but does not believe he has to serve Him In reality. He doesn’t believe in the true God but, in his mind, created a fictitious god that does not exist. This allows him to live for himself and his own happiness. This type of person will talk about God, go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, he will look only to man for all his needs. If he is sick, he calls a doctor. If he needs money, he goes to the banker. If the need is a break from reality, he takes a vacation or retreat. He lives life for his own happiness and then thanks God though he did not look to God for his needs. These people are dependent on themselves. They have confidence in themselves.

Here is an example: A Christian plants a garden and takes care of it each day. He waters and fertilizes weeds and prunes. Finally, his plants all begin to bear fruit, nice fruit. He thanks God for the plentiful harvest. His neighbor, an atheistic humanist, also planted a garden. He, too, went out each day and watered, pruned, weeded, and fertilized. He also received a bountiful harvest. This man, however, boasted of all that he had accomplished. Both men did the same things and had similar results. One gave God the credit, and one credited himself. He will say he accomplished the same thing without God that his neighbor did with God. Christians know that he is wrong and that he actually did need God to grow his garden.

When something happens that requires supernatural intervention, the Christian humanist prays and asks others to pray. However, he does not believe God will answer their prayers and instantly gets to work to solve his problem, with only human reasoning. Then, if the problem is resolved, he thanks God for it. This type of humanism has confused the modern world. It has caused unbelievers to mock the Christian faith and to call it a false religion with no power.

The Christian does not believe in human reasoning. The Christian believes that the God of heaven is the reason for everything. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him” (Colossians 1:16). We are nothing without Him, and without Him, we can do nothing. Christianity is the opposite of humanism. When the Christian does something supernatural, something the humanist or atheist cannot do, then we have something that will confound the wise.

When the neighbor sees the Christian loving his enemies, forgiving someone who wronged him, and doing things that he cannot do, he then begins to wonder where the power to do these things came from. This then leads him to the Father. When there is nothing supernatural that we are doing, he is confused.

What About Us?

I fear that we are falling into this trap of ‘Christian Humanism.’ We talk the talk; we say we believe in God. We go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, from outward appearances, we trust in ourselves. Because we have centered our lives around ourselves and our well-being, the God of heaven does not hear us. Our prayers are not answered, and the time on our knees is a struggle at best. We go through the motions because that is how we’ve been taught, but our faith lies in human reasoning.

It can be extremely difficult to seek the Lord while living in a humanistic society. A society that has perfected the pursuit of liberty and happiness. Slowly, the church is caving to the ways of this world.

A minister from China was visiting the churches in America. Before departing back to China, he was asked what impressed him most about the churches in America. He replied, “I am amazed at what all they have accomplished without God.”

We would do well to simplify the modern definition of humanism. The humanist proudly denies that there is a God when he boasts of his own strength and abilities. He proclaims the great accomplishments of man and mocks the humble Christian.

The Christian denies himself, picks up his cross, and follows his Master. The Christian thinks nothing of himself or the ability of man, confidently admitting that he is merely dust and back to that dust he will quickly go. The Christian looks for the good in others and trusts God for all his daily needs and cares.

Christians believe they are merely servants to their master. They are hated by the world and despised by most, rejected. “If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. (John 15:18)” To them, this life is not the pursuit of happiness. The things of this world do not even interest them. Their joy and peace comes solely from serving their master, from pleasing their Heavenly Father. To the world, they are strange. Fools. To God, they are His dear children.

God is still looking for people today who will put their trust in Him. He is looking over all the earth for someone, somewhere, who will put aside human reasoning and common sense and obey the voice from heaven. God wants men with faith who will step out into the supernatural, like Abraham, Moses, David, and the thousands of believers that followed. Someone who will deny himself and this world and follow the Savior.

When this life is over, the humanists, whether they say they believe in God or not, will perish. And the Christians will go on to live forever in glory.

Humanist? Christian? Christian Humanist? Which one are you?

Credi nei miracoli? Credi nel soprannaturale? E nell'intervento divino? O una domanda migliore potrebbe essere: hai visto Dio operare nella tua vita? Gli altri vedono Dio operare nella tua vita?

Mio fratello lavorava nella serra quando un cliente entrò e si meravigliò della bellezza di tutte le piante. Poi esclamò quanto fosse impressionato da tutto il nostro duro lavoro. Mio fratello rispose: «Alcune piante, un po' d'acqua, ma è Dio che dà l'aumento». A cui il cliente rispose: «No, no, non attribuite il merito a Dio. Siete venuti qui e avete fatto tutto questo lavoro. Avete piantato, annaffiato e concimato tutte queste piante, e voi tutti meritate il credito, non Dio!» Il motivo per cui l'uomo la pensava così era che era un umanista.

Cos'è l'umanesimo?

Il dizionario definisce l'umanesimo così: una visione o un sistema di pensiero che attribuisce importanza principale alle questioni umane piuttosto che a quelle divine o soprannaturali. Le credenze umaniste sottolineano il valore potenziale e la bontà degli esseri umani, enfatizzano i bisogni umani comuni e cercano modi puramente razionali per risolvere i problemi umani.

Se Dio esiste, allora dovremo riconoscere questo fatto e rendere conto a Lui. Gli umanisti tentano di provare che Dio non esiste, così da poter vivere liberamente la loro vita come vogliono. Secondo l'umanesimo, non c'è Dio. Se così fosse, allora noi, la razza umana, saremmo superiori a Dio. Tutto è per noi e per la nostra felicità ultima. Questa è la definizione di umanesimo.

Due tipi di umanesimo

Esistono due tipi di credenze umaniste, e ne esamineremo entrambe. La prima è la teoria che non esiste alcun Dio. In realtà, questa sembra essere l'unica via razionale per essere umanisti. Tutto è creato dall'uomo e per l'uomo. Non ci sono altri fattori o coinvolgimenti soprannaturali. Tutto accade per ragione e buon senso. C'è una spiegazione logica per tutto ciò che accade. Certo, alcune cose non hanno senso, ma gli umanisti scartano quelle e guardano solo le cose che possono essere spiegate. Come le piante nella serra, osservano tutto ciò che l'uomo fa e ignorano la parte soprannaturale di una pianta che germoglia nuova vita. Scienziati in tutto il mondo lavorano diligentemente per inserire il ragionamento umano in tutto ciò che è mai accaduto, persino nella creazione del mondo. Scienziati, con tutto il loro sapere e saggezza, cercano di dare spiegazioni logiche sul perché avvengono disastri naturali e crisi globali. Se possono spiegare tutto, allora possono escludere Dio e la Sua esistenza. Questo permette alla razza umana di fare come le pare senza conseguenze eterne. Questo, a sua volta, conduce a un grande senso di falsa pace.

Gli umanisti, con tutto il loro ragionamento, deridono la stessa esistenza di Dio. Se vai nella maggior parte dei college in America e parli con le persone del cristianesimo, ridono di te e prendono in giro il fatto che i cristiani credano davvero in Dio.

Il secondo tipo di credenza umanista è una teoria che riconosce l'esistenza di Dio. Un antropologo sosteneva che l'umanesimo è un progetto della modernità e una continuazione laicizzata della teologia cristiana occidentale. Ma se chiedi alle persone cosa pensano significhi umanesimo, probabilmente otterrai risposte diverse, e diventa molto confuso. Ma perché la confusione? Perché le persone cercano di essere umanisti cristiani. L'Umanesimo Cristiano è stato spesso criticato per la sua vaghezza e la difficoltà a definirlo. Il motivo per cui è diventato così confuso è che la gente vuole credere in Dio ma anche credere in se stessa e che il mondo ruoti intorno a loro.

In Romani leggiamo: «Poiché l'ira di Dio è rivelata dal cielo contro ogni empietà e ingiustizia degli uomini che sopprimono la verità mediante l'ingiustizia; poiché ciò che si può conoscere di Dio è manifesto fra loro, perché Dio lo ha loro manifestato. Le cose invisibili di lui, la sua etterna potenza e la divinità, infatti si vedono fin dalla creazione del mondo, essendo intese per mezzo delle cose create; così essi sono inescusabili. Perché, avendo conosciuto Dio, non lo hanno glorificato come Dio né gli hanno reso grazie, ma sono diventati vani nei loro ragionamenti e il loro stolto cuore è stato inaridito. Proclamandosi sapienti, sono diventati stolti e hanno cambiato la gloria dell'Iddio incorruttibile in immagine simile a quella dell'uomo corruttibile e a volatili e quadrupedi e rettili. Perciò Dio li ha abbandonati alle passioni della loro vergogna, alle impurità, perché disonorassero i loro corpi tra loro; essi hanno cambiato la verità di Dio con la menzogna e hanno adorato e servito la creatura più del Creatore, il quale è benedetto in eterno. Amen. Perciò Dio li ha abbandonati a concupiscenze infami; infatti anche le loro donne hanno mutato l'uso naturale in quello contro natura; allo stesso modo anche gli uomini, abbandonando l'uso naturale della donna, si sono infiammati nella loro concupiscenza gli uni per gli altri, compiendo atti indecenti con uomini e ricevendo in se stessi il giusto compenso della loro deviazione. E, non gradando neppure di conservare Dio nel loro conoscere, Dio li ha consegnati a una mente reprobata per fare quelle cose che non sono convenienti; essendo pieni di ogni ingiustizia, fornicazione, malvagità, cupidigia, malignità, pieni d'invidia, omicidio, contesa, frode, malignità; calunniatori, diffamatori, odiatori di Dio, oltraggiosi, superbi, vanagloriosi, inventori di mali cose, disubbidienti ai genitori, senza intelligenza, senza alleanza, senza affetto naturale, implacabili, senza misericordia; i quali, conoscendo la giustizia di Dio, cioè che coloro che fanno tali cose sono degni di morte, non solo le compiono, ma anche approvano chi le compie» (Romani 1:18-32).

Allora come si può essere umanisti e credere in Dio? Qui tocchiamo qualcosa di più vicino a casa. Questo tipo di umanista crede che Dio voglia che egli sia felice. Crede in un Dio Creatore ma non crede di doverGli servire nella realtà. Non crede nel vero Dio, ma nella sua mente ha creato un dio fittizio che non esiste. Questo gli permette di vivere per se stesso e per la propria felicità. Questo tipo di persona parlerà di Dio, andrà in chiesa, canterà inni e dirà preghiere. Tuttavia, cercherà ogni sua necessità solo nell'uomo. Se è malato, chiama un dottore. Se ha bisogno di denaro, va dal banchiere. Se ha bisogno di una pausa dalla realtà, prende una vacanza o un ritiro. Vive la vita per la sua felicità e poi ringrazia Dio anche se non si è rivolto a Dio per i suoi bisogni. Queste persone dipendono da se stesse. Hanno fiducia in se stesse.

Ecco un esempio: un cristiano pianta un orto e se ne prende cura ogni giorno. Annaffia e concima, estirpa le erbacce e pota. Infine, le sue piante cominciano a dare frutto, frutti belli. Ringrazia Dio per il raccolto abbondante. Il suo vicino, un umanista ateo, ha anche lui piantato un orto. Anche lui usciva ogni giorno e annaffiava, potava, estirpava e concimava. Anche lui ha ricevuto un raccolto abbondante. Quest'uomo, tuttavia, si vantava di tutto ciò che aveva realizzato. Entrambi gli uomini hanno fatto le stesse cose e hanno ottenuto risultati simili. Uno ha dato il merito a Dio, e uno ha dato il merito a se stesso. Dirà di aver compiuto lo stesso risultato senza Dio che il suo vicino ha ottenuto con Dio. I cristiani sanno che si sbaglia e che in realtà aveva bisogno di Dio per far crescere il suo orto.

Quando accade qualcosa che richiede intervento soprannaturale, l'umanista cristiano prega e chiede ad altri di pregare. Tuttavia, non crede che Dio risponderà alle loro preghiere e si mette subito al lavoro per risolvere il suo problema, usando solo il ragionamento umano. Poi, se il problema si risolve, ringrazia Dio per questo. Questo tipo di umanesimo ha confuso il mondo moderno. Ha portato gli increduli a deridere la fede cristiana e a chiamarla una religione falsa senza potere.

Il cristiano non crede nel ragionamento umano. Il cristiano crede che il Dio dei cieli sia la ragione di ogni cosa. «Perché in lui sono state create tutte le cose che sono nei cieli e sulla terra, visibili e invisibili, siano essi troni o dominazioni o principati o potestà; tutte le cose sono state create per mezzo di lui e in vista di lui» (Colossesi 1:16). Noi non siamo nulla senza di Lui, e senza di Lui non possiamo fare nulla. Il cristianesimo è l'opposto dell'umanesimo. Quando il cristiano compie qualcosa di soprannaturale, qualcosa che l'umanista o l'ateo non possono fare, allora abbiamo qualcosa che confonde i saggi.

Quando il vicino vede il cristiano amare i suoi nemici, perdonare chi gli ha fatto torto e fare cose che lui non può fare, allora comincia a domandarsi da dove venga il potere di fare queste cose. Questo lo conduce al Padre. Quando non c'è nulla di soprannaturale in ciò che facciamo, rimane confuso.

E noi?

Temo che stiamo cadendo in questa trappola dell'«Umanesimo Cristiano». Parliamo bene; diciamo di credere in Dio. Andiamo in chiesa, cantiamo inni e preghiamo. Tuttavia, dall'apparenza esteriore, confidiamo in noi stessi. Poiché abbiamo centrato le nostre vite su noi stessi e sul nostro benessere, il Dio dei cieli non ci ascolta. Le nostre preghiere non vengono esaudite e il tempo sulle nostre ginocchia è una lotta, nella migliore delle ipotesi. Facciamo le cose per abitudine perché così ci è stato insegnato, ma la nostra fede risiede nel ragionamento umano.

Può essere estremamente difficile cercare il Signore vivendo in una società umanistica. Una società che ha perfezionato la ricerca della libertà e della felicità. Lentamente, la chiesa sta cedendo ai modi di questo mondo.

Un ministro dalla Cina stava visitando le chiese in America. Prima di ritornare in Cina, gli fu chiesto che cosa lo avesse impressionato maggiormente delle chiese americane. Rispose: «Sono stupito di ciò che hanno compiuto senza Dio».

Faremmo bene a semplificare la moderna definizione di umanesimo. L'umanista nega con orgoglio che esista un Dio quando si vanta della propria forza e abilità. Proclama i grandi risultati dell'uomo e deride il cristiano umile.

Il cristiano si nega, prende la sua croce e segue il suo Maestro. Il cristiano non pensa nulla di se stesso o della capacità dell'uomo, ammettendo con fiducia che è solo polvere e che a quella polvere tornerà presto. Il cristiano cerca il bene negli altri e confida in Dio per tutti i suoi bisogni e le sue preoccupazioni quotidiane.

I cristiani credono di essere semplicemente servi del loro padrone. Sono odiati dal mondo e disprezzati dalla maggior parte, rifiutati. «Se il mondo vi odia, ricordate che ha odiato me prima di voi» (Giovanni 15:18). Per loro, questa vita non è la ricerca della felicità. Le cose di questo mondo non li interessano nemmeno. La loro gioia e pace viene esclusivamente dal servire il loro padrone, dal compiacere il loro Padre celeste. Per il mondo, sono strani. Sciocchi. Per Dio, sono i suoi cari figli.

Dio sta ancora cercando persone oggi che pongano la loro fiducia in Lui. Sta guardando tutta la terra sperando di trovare qualcuno, da qualche parte, che metta da parte il ragionamento umano e il buon senso e obbedisca alla voce dal cielo. Dio vuole uomini con fede che facciano un passo nel soprannaturale, come Abramo, Mosè, Davide e le migliaia di credenti che li seguirono. Qualcuno che si neghi e questo mondo e segua il Salvatore.

Quando questa vita sarà finita, gli umanisti, che dicano o meno di credere in Dio, periranno. E i cristiani vivranno per sempre nella gloria.

Umanista? Cristiano? Umanista Cristiano? Quale sei tu?

Do you believe in miracles? Do you believe in the supernatural? What about divine intervention? Or a better question might be, have you seen God working in your life? Do others see God working in your life?

My brother was working in the greenhouse when a customer walked in and marveled at the beauty of all the plants. He then exclaimed how impressed he was at all our hard work. My brother responded with, “Some plant, some water, but God gives the increase.” To which the customer responded with, “No, no, don’t give the credit to God. You came out here and did all this work. You planted, watered, and fertilized all these plants, and you all deserve the credit, not God!” The reason the man felt this way is because he was a humanist.

What is Humanism?

The dictionary defines humanism like this; an outlook or system of thought attaching prime importance to human rather than divine or supernatural matters. Humanist beliefs stress the potential value and goodness of human beings, emphasize common human needs, and seek solely rational ways of solving human problems.

If God does exist, then we will have to recognize this fact and answer to Him. Humanists attempt to prove that God does not exist, so they can freely live their lives as they please. According to humanism, there is no God. If so, then we, the human race, are superior to God. Everything is for us and our ultimate happiness. This is the definition of humanism.

Two Types of Humanism

There are two types of humanistic beliefs, and we will look at both. The first belief is the theory that there is no God. In reality, this seems to be the only rational way to be a humanist. Everything is created by man and for man. There are no other factors or supernatural involvement. Everything happens by reason and common sense. There is a logical explanation for everything that happens. Of course, some things do not make sense, but humanists brush those aside and look only at the things that can be explained. Like the plants in the greenhouse, they look at all that man does and ignore the supernatural part of a plant springing forth with new life. Scientists around the world are working diligently to put human reasoning into everything that has ever happened, even the creation of the world. Scientists, with all their learning and wisdom, attempt to give logical explanations for why natural disasters and global crises happen. If they can explain everything, then they can rule out God and His existence. This allows the human race to do as it pleases without eternal consequences. This, in turn leads to a great sense of false peace.

The humanists, with all their reasoning, mock the very existence of God. If you go to most colleges in America and talk to people about Christianity, they laugh at you and mock the fact that Christians actually believe in God.

The second type of humanistic belief is a theory of humanism that acknowledges the existence of God. One anthropologist argued that humanism is a project of modernity and a secularized continuation of Western Christian theology. But if you ask people what they think humanism means, you will likely get different responses, and it becomes very confusing. But why the confusion? Because people are trying to be Christian humanists. Christian Humanism has frequently been criticized for its vagueness and difficulty to define. The reason it has become so confusing is that people want to believe in God but also believe in themselves and that the world revolves around them.

In Romans, we read, “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them” (Romans 1:18-32).

So how can one be a humanist and believe in God? This is where we hit a little closer to home. This type of humanist believes God wants him to be happy. He believes in a Creator God but does not believe he has to serve Him In reality. He doesn’t believe in the true God but, in his mind, created a fictitious god that does not exist. This allows him to live for himself and his own happiness. This type of person will talk about God, go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, he will look only to man for all his needs. If he is sick, he calls a doctor. If he needs money, he goes to the banker. If the need is a break from reality, he takes a vacation or retreat. He lives life for his own happiness and then thanks God though he did not look to God for his needs. These people are dependent on themselves. They have confidence in themselves.

Here is an example: A Christian plants a garden and takes care of it each day. He waters and fertilizes weeds and prunes. Finally, his plants all begin to bear fruit, nice fruit. He thanks God for the plentiful harvest. His neighbor, an atheistic humanist, also planted a garden. He, too, went out each day and watered, pruned, weeded, and fertilized. He also received a bountiful harvest. This man, however, boasted of all that he had accomplished. Both men did the same things and had similar results. One gave God the credit, and one credited himself. He will say he accomplished the same thing without God that his neighbor did with God. Christians know that he is wrong and that he actually did need God to grow his garden.

When something happens that requires supernatural intervention, the Christian humanist prays and asks others to pray. However, he does not believe God will answer their prayers and instantly gets to work to solve his problem, with only human reasoning. Then, if the problem is resolved, he thanks God for it. This type of humanism has confused the modern world. It has caused unbelievers to mock the Christian faith and to call it a false religion with no power.

The Christian does not believe in human reasoning. The Christian believes that the God of heaven is the reason for everything. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him” (Colossians 1:16). We are nothing without Him, and without Him, we can do nothing. Christianity is the opposite of humanism. When the Christian does something supernatural, something the humanist or atheist cannot do, then we have something that will confound the wise.

When the neighbor sees the Christian loving his enemies, forgiving someone who wronged him, and doing things that he cannot do, he then begins to wonder where the power to do these things came from. This then leads him to the Father. When there is nothing supernatural that we are doing, he is confused.

What About Us?

I fear that we are falling into this trap of ‘Christian Humanism.’ We talk the talk; we say we believe in God. We go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, from outward appearances, we trust in ourselves. Because we have centered our lives around ourselves and our well-being, the God of heaven does not hear us. Our prayers are not answered, and the time on our knees is a struggle at best. We go through the motions because that is how we’ve been taught, but our faith lies in human reasoning.

It can be extremely difficult to seek the Lord while living in a humanistic society. A society that has perfected the pursuit of liberty and happiness. Slowly, the church is caving to the ways of this world.

A minister from China was visiting the churches in America. Before departing back to China, he was asked what impressed him most about the churches in America. He replied, “I am amazed at what all they have accomplished without God.”

We would do well to simplify the modern definition of humanism. The humanist proudly denies that there is a God when he boasts of his own strength and abilities. He proclaims the great accomplishments of man and mocks the humble Christian.

The Christian denies himself, picks up his cross, and follows his Master. The Christian thinks nothing of himself or the ability of man, confidently admitting that he is merely dust and back to that dust he will quickly go. The Christian looks for the good in others and trusts God for all his daily needs and cares.

Christians believe they are merely servants to their master. They are hated by the world and despised by most, rejected. “If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. (John 15:18)” To them, this life is not the pursuit of happiness. The things of this world do not even interest them. Their joy and peace comes solely from serving their master, from pleasing their Heavenly Father. To the world, they are strange. Fools. To God, they are His dear children.

God is still looking for people today who will put their trust in Him. He is looking over all the earth for someone, somewhere, who will put aside human reasoning and common sense and obey the voice from heaven. God wants men with faith who will step out into the supernatural, like Abraham, Moses, David, and the thousands of believers that followed. Someone who will deny himself and this world and follow the Savior.

When this life is over, the humanists, whether they say they believe in God or not, will perish. And the Christians will go on to live forever in glory.

Humanist? Christian? Christian Humanist? Which one are you?

Tror du på mirakler? Tror du på det övernaturliga? Vad sägs om gudomlig ingripande? Eller en bättre fråga kanske är: har du sett Gud verka i ditt liv? Ser andra Gud verka i ditt liv?

Min bror arbetade i växthuset när en kund kom in och förundrades över skönheten hos alla växterna. Han utropade hur imponerad han var över allt vårt hårda arbete. Min bror svarade: ”Viss planta, viss vatten, men Gud ger tillväxten.” Kunden svarade då: ”Nej, nej, ge inte äran åt Gud. Ni gick ut här och gjorde allt detta arbete. Ni planterade, vattnade och gödslade alla dessa plantor, och ni förtjänar äran, inte Gud!” Anledningen till att mannen kände så var att han var humanist.

Vad är humanism?

Ordboken definierar humanism så här: en syn eller ett tankesystem som fäster främsta vikt vid mänskliga snarare än gudomliga eller övernaturliga frågor. Humanistiska uppfattningar betonar människors potentiella värde och godhet, framhäver gemensamma mänskliga behov och söker endast rationella sätt att lösa mänskliga problem.

Om Gud finns måste vi erkänna detta faktum och svara inför Honom. Humanister försöker bevisa att Gud inte finns, så att de fritt kan leva sina liv som de behagar. Enligt humanismen finns ingen Gud. Om så är fallet är vi, människosläktet, överlägsna Gud. Allt är för oss och vår yttersta lycka. Detta är definitionen av humanism.

Två typer av humanism

Det finns två typer av humanistiska uppfattningar, och vi ska se på båda. Den första uppfattningen är teorin att det inte finns någon Gud. I verkligheten verkar detta vara det enda rationella sättet att vara humanist på. Allt är skapat av människan och för människan. Det finns inga andra faktorer eller övernaturligt ingripande. Allt händer genom förnuft och sunt förnuft. Det finns en logisk förklaring till allt som händer. Visst, vissa saker är obegripliga, men humanister bortser från dem och ser bara till det som kan förklaras. Som växterna i växthuset ser de allt som människan gör och ignorerar den övernaturliga delen av en växts uppvaknande till nytt liv. Forskare runt om i världen arbetar ihärdigt för att föra in mänskligt tänkande i allt som någonsin hänt, till och med världens skapelse. Forskare, med all sin kunskap och visdom, försöker ge logiska förklaringar till varför naturkatastrofer och globala kriser inträffar. Om de kan förklara allt kan de utesluta Gud och Hans existens. Detta tillåter människosläktet att göra som det behagar utan eviga konsekvenser. Detta leder i sin tur till en stor känsla av falsk frid.

Humanisterna, med allt sitt resonemang, förlöjligar själva Guds existens. Om du går till de flesta högskolor i Amerika och pratar med folk om kristendomen skrattar de åt dig och hånar det faktum att kristna faktiskt tror på Gud.

Den andra typen av humanistisk uppfattning är en teori om humanism som erkänner Guds existens. En antropolog hävdade att humanism är ett modernitetsprojekt och en sekulariserad fortsättning på västerländsk kristen teologi. Men om du frågar folk vad de tycker att humanism betyder kommer du sannolikt att få olika svar, och det blir mycket förvirrande. Men varför förvirringen? För att människor försöker vara kristna humanister. Kristen humanism har ofta kritiserats för sin vaghet och svårighet att definieras. Anledningen till att det blivit så förvirrande är att människor vill tro på Gud men också tro på sig själva och att världen kretsar kring dem.

I Romarbrevet läser vi, “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them” (Romans 1:18-32).

Så hur kan man vara humanist och tro på Gud? Här kommer vi lite närmare hemma. Denna typ av humanist tror att Gud vill att han ska vara lycklig. Han tror på en skapande Gud men tror inte att han i verkligheten måste tjäna Honom. I verkligheten tror han inte på den sanna Guden utan i sitt sinne har han skapat en fiktiv gud som inte existerar. Detta tillåter honom att leva för sig själv och sin egen lycka. Denna typ av person pratar om Gud, går till kyrkan, sjunger sånger och ber böner. Han vänder sig dock endast till människan för alla sina behov. Är han sjuk ringer han en läkare. Behöver han pengar går han till bankiren. Om behovet är en paus från verkligheten tar han en semester eller reträtt. Han lever för sin egen lycka och tackar sedan Gud fastän han inte vände sig till Gud för sina behov. Dessa människor är beroende av sig själva. De har förtroende för sig själva.

Här är ett exempel: En kristen planterar en trädgård och tar hand om den varje dag. Han vattnar och gödslar, rensar ogräs och beskär. Slutligen börjar hans växter bära frukt, fin frukt. Han tackar Gud för den rikliga skörden. Hans granne, en ateistisk humanist, planterade också en trädgård. Han gick också ut varje dag och vattnade, beskärde, rensade ogräs och gödslade. Han fick också en riklig skörd. Denne man skryter dock om allt han åstadkommit. Båda männen gjorde samma saker och fick liknande resultat. Den ene gav Gud äran, den andre berömde sig själv. Han kommer att säga att han uppnådde samma sak utan Gud som hans granne gjorde med Gud. Kristna vet att han har fel och att han faktiskt behövde Gud för att få sin trädgård att växa.

När något händer som kräver övernaturlig ingripande ber den kristna humanisten och ber andra att be. Han tror dock inte att Gud kommer att svara på deras böner och sätter genast igång för att lösa sitt problem med endast mänskligt resonemang. Sedan, om problemet blir löst, tackar han Gud för det. Denna typ av humanism har förvirrat den moderna världen. Den har fått otroende att håna den kristna tron och kalla den en falsk religion utan kraft.

Den kristne tror inte på mänskligt resonemang. Den kristne tror att himlens Gud är orsaken till allt. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him” (Colossians 1:16). Vi är ingenting utan Honom, och utan Honom kan vi ingenting göra. Kristendomen är motsatsen till humanism. När den kristne gör något övernaturligt, något som humanisten eller ateisten inte kan göra, då har vi något som förvirrar de vise.

När grannen ser den kristne älska sina fiender, förlåta någon som gjort fel mot honom och göra saker som han inte kan göra, börjar han undra var kraften att göra dessa saker kom ifrån. Detta leder honom då till Fadern. När det inte finns något övernaturligt vi gör blir han förvirrad.

Vad sägs om oss?

Jag fruktar att vi faller i denna fälla av ”kristen humanism.” Vi talar väl; vi säger att vi tror på Gud. Vi går till kyrkan, sjunger sånger och ber böner. Men utåt sett litar vi på oss själva. Eftersom vi har centrerat våra liv kring oss själva och vårt välbefinnande hör himlens Gud oss inte. Våra böner besvaras inte, och tiden på knä är i bästa fall en kamp. Vi går igenom ritualerna eftersom det är så vi blivit undervisade, men vår tro vilar i mänskligt resonemang.

Det kan vara oerhört svårt att söka Herren medan man lever i ett humanistiskt samhälle. Ett samhälle som fulländat jakten på frihet och lycka. Sakta men säkert viker kyrkan för denna världens sätt.

En predikant från Kina besökte kyrkorna i Amerika. Innan han återvände till Kina blev han frågad vad som imponerade mest på honom med kyrkorna i Amerika. Han svarade: ”Jag är förundrad över vad de alla har åstadkommit utan Gud.”

Vi skulle göra väl i att förenkla den moderna definitionen av humanism. Humanisten förnekar stolt att det finns en Gud när han skryter om sin egen styrka och förmåga. Han proklamerar människans stora bedrifter och förlöjligar den ödmjuka kristne.

Den kristne förnekar sig själv, tar upp sitt kors och följer sin Mästare. Den kristne tänker intet om sig själv eller människans förmåga, och erkänner tryggt att han blott är stoft och snart ska återgå till det stoftet. Den kristne ser det goda i andra och litar på Gud för alla sina dagliga behov och bekymmer.

Kristna anser sig blott vara tjänare åt sin Herre. De blir hatade av världen och föraktade av de flesta, avvisade. ”If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. (John 15:18)” För dem är detta liv inte jakten på lycka. Världens ting intresserar dem inte ens. Deras glädje och frid kommer enbart från att tjäna sin Herre, från att behaga sin himmelske Fader. För världen är de främmande. Dårar. För Gud är de Hans kära barn.

Gud söker fortfarande människor idag som vill sätta sitt förtroende till Honom. Han söker över hela jorden efter någon, någonstans, som vill lägga åt sidan mänskligt resonemang och sunt förnuft och lyda rösten från himlen. Gud vill ha människor med tro som vågar träda in i det övernaturliga, som Abraham, Mose, David och de tusentals troende som följde. Någon som vill förneka sig själv och denna värld och följa Frälsaren.

När detta livet är över ska humanisterna, vare sig de säger att de tror på Gud eller inte, gå under. Och de kristna ska gå vidare för att leva för evigt i härlighet.

Humanist? Kristen? Kristen humanist? Vilken är du?
