How unbelievable it is that God can take a wretched sinner, void of the fear of the Lord, and turn him into a blood-washed saint and preacher of the gospel! In this story, we see God’s life-changing power at work in our hymn writer’s life.

In the small cemetery of a churchyard in Olney, England, stands a granite tombstone with this inscription, written by Newton himself before his death:

John Newton, once an infidel and libertine, a servant of slaves in Africa, was, by the rich mercy of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, preserved, restored, pardoned, and appointed to preach the faith he had long labored to destroy!

This epitaph aptly describes the unusual and colorful life of this man, one of the great evangelical preachers of the eighteenth century. His testimony was, “By the grace of God, I am what I am!”

“Amazing Grace” was a hymn published in 1779, with words written in 1772 by the English poet and Anglican clergyman John Newton (1725–1807). “Amazing Grace” is probably the most beloved hymn of the last two centuries. This hymn is estimated to be performed 10 million times annually. It has appeared on over 11,000 albums and translated into about 60 languages. It was referenced in Harriet Beecher Stowe’s anti-slavery novel Uncle Tom’s Cabin. It had a surge in popularity during two of America’s greatest crises: the Civil War and the Vietnam War.

Ironically, this stirring song, closely associated with the African-American community, was written by a former slave trader, John Newton.

John was born on July 24, 1725, in Wapping, England, to a seafaring father, John Newton, Sr., and a devout Christian mother, Elizabeth Newton. His father loved him but was gone at sea most of the time. On the other hand, his mother was tender and nurturing, teaching him the Word of God. She would instruct him in memorizing the Bible whole chapters at a time and took him to church. Unfortunately, when he was almost seven, his mother died of tuberculosis. His father remarried a short time later and sent him to a boarding school. During his time at the boarding school, he made bad friends. His character disintegrated to the point that he was dismissed from one school and moved to another. By the time he was 11 years old, the boarding schools didn’t want him, so his father took him along to sea. He spent the next six years on the Atlantic Ocean with his father.

When John was 17, his father arranged to send him to Jamaica for a well-paying job overseeing a plantation. On his way, while waiting for the ship’s departure, John received an invitation to the home of some old-time friends, the Catletts. It was in this home that John’s mother had died ten years earlier. As he reacquainted himself with them, he got to know their daughter, Mary. John and Mary’s mothers were best of friends. John had been invited to stay four days, but he stayed two weeks and missed the ship to Jamaica.

At age 18, John was conscripted into the Royal Navy, and his life went from bad to worse. He wanted to return and see Mary, so he deserted the ship but was caught, publicly flogged, and laid in irons. His life on the ship was so profane that even the other ungodly sailors cringed at his curses and blasphemies. He gained the title “The Great Blasphemer” and was such an unwanted man on the ship that he was sent to work on a slave ship.

One of the owners of the slave ship where he now worked, offered John a job once they reached the African coast. However, once on shore, he was tied up and forced to work with little food, clothing, or shelter. He sent several letters back to his father during this time, pleading for help.

A ship called The Greyhound was sailing near the coast, which John had now called home. The captain had been instructed by John’s father to look for his son. The ship, while being almost too far from shore to trade, decided to give trading a try. A friend of John’s rowed out from shore to trade. As he turned to leave, the captain asked him whether he knew anyone named John Newton. He did to the captain’s surprise, and John was brought on board to go home.

On board the ship, Newton picked up a copy of Thomas á Kempis’s Christian classic, The Imitation of Christ. He had never encountered anything like it, and he began to wonder if the Christian claims might be true. That night, on March 10, 1748, a fierce storm nearly swamped the ship. Men, animals, and provisions were swept overboard. The storm awakened Newton, the ship’s rotten timbers broken by the waves and floodwater swirling into his cabin. John prayed for the first time in years.

The Greyhound thrashed about in the North Atlantic storm for over 11 days. With little hope of survival, the sailors mechanically worked the pumps, trying to keep the vessel afloat. On the eleventh day of the storm, John was too exhausted to pump, so he was tied to the helm, where he did his best to hold the ship to its course. From one o’clock until midnight, he was at the helm. He feared he was going to die, and if the Christian faith were true, then he surely would not be forgiven. He reflected on all he had done over the past few years. His life seemed as ruined and wrecked as the battered ship he was trying to steer through the storm. During those long and grueling hours, Newton cried out to God like he never had before, and that was the turning point in his life.

That was a day John Newton remembered ever after. “On that day, the Lord sent from on high and delivered me out of deep waters.” Over 50 years later, John wrote in his diary on March 21, 1805: “Not well able to write; but I endeavor to observe the return of this day with humiliation, prayer, and praise.”

Only God’s amazing grace could take a rude, profane, slave-trading sailor and transform him into a child of God. John never ceased to stand in awe of God’s work in his life. He took an interest in prayer, reading and meditating on the Scriptures, and only speaking words pleasing to God.

On his return home, Mary and her parents recognized the change the Lord had brought in John. The two were married on February 1, 1750.

For the next four years, Newton was captain of his own slave ship. This occupation kept him separated from Mary for months at a time. While they were apart, the two corresponded constantly. In his letters, John repeatedly wrote how their love and marriage increased his thankfulness and gratefulness to the Lord. “... When I indulge myself with a particular thought of you, it usually carries me on farther and brings me upon my knees to bless the Lord for giving me such a treasure and to pray for your peace and welfare”

John endeavored to “Christianize” his slave ship by holding Sunday services for his crew of 30 sin-hardened men. He made three more voyages to bring slaves from Africa to North America. As he planned his fourth trip, he became sick with malaria. God used this sickness to end his involvement in the slave trade.

As John began a new chapter in his life, he felt called to be a minister. For more than 50 years, he preached the gospel and was one of the most influential men of his day.

John Newton often composed a hymn to go with his Sunday evening services. In 1779, 280 of these were collected and combined with 68 hymns by Newton’s friend and parishioner, William Cowper, and published as the Olney Hymns. The most famous of all the Olney Hymns, “Faith’s Review and Expectation”, grew out of David’s exclamation in 1 Chronicles 17:16-17. We know it today as “Amazing Grace”. “Amazing Grace” originally had six stanzas, and the last verse was added about a century later. Most hymnals have four or five of these verses.

As minister in the church, John continued to be more and more troubled by the slave trade that was still going on. In 1788, 34 years after he left the slave trade, He wrote a book entitled Thoughts Upon the African Slave Trade and sent it to all the members of parliament. This book brought an awareness to the public of the evils of the slave trade. He quotes this, “Needless to say, the capturing, selling and transporting of black slaves to the plantations in the West Indies and America was a cruel and vicious way of life.” With the help and providence of God, John saw the day, several months before his death, in 1807, when slavery was officially banned from England.

When John was in his sixties, his beloved wife Mary passed away. This was a great trial for John, and he spent the remaining 17 years of his life without her.

After John suffered a stroke and shortly before his death, a spokesman for the church encouraged Newton to consider retiring from preaching because of failing health, eyesight, and memory. John replied, “What, shall the old African blasphemer stop while he can still speak? I will continue to preach. Although my memory’s fading, I remember two things very clearly: I am a great sinner, and Christ is a great Savior.”

The last words of John Newton as he lay on his deathbed were as follows: “I am still in the land of the dying; I shall be in the land of the living soon.”

The tune “Amazing Grace” is an early American folk melody. It was first known as a plantation melody entitled “Loving Lambs”. This tune was first published in 1831 in the book The Virginia Harmony. The majority of hymn books published after this time included this song. In 1910, Edwin O. Excell added the last verse, which eventually replaced the last three original verses of the song. His edition of the song is most common in our hymnals today. Several other Olney hymns by Newton continue to be sung today, including “How Sweet the Name of Jesus Sounds” and “Glorious Things of Thee are Spoken”.

Como é extraordinário que Deus possa tomar um pecador miserável, desprovido do temor do Senhor, e transformá-lo num santo lavado pelo sangue e pregador do evangelho! Nesta história, vemos o poder transformador de Deus em ação na vida do autor do nosso hino.

No pequeno cemitério de uma igreja em Olney, Inglaterra, encontra-se uma lápide de granito com esta inscrição, escrita pelo próprio Newton antes de sua morte:

John Newton, outrora incrédulo e libertino, servo de escravos na África, foi, pela rica misericórdia de nosso Senhor e Salvador Jesus Cristo, preservado, restaurado, perdoado e designado para pregar a fé que por tanto tempo se empenhara em destruir!

Este epitáfio descreve bem a vida incomum e cheia de acontecimentos deste homem, um dos grandes pregadores evangélicos do século XVIII. Seu testemunho era: “Pela graça de Deus, sou o que sou!”

“Graça Maravilhosa” foi um hino publicado em 1779, cuja letra foi escrita em 1772 pelo poeta inglês e clérigo anglicano John Newton (1725–1807). “Graça Maravilhosa” é provavelmente o hino mais amado dos últimos dois séculos. Estima-se que este hino seja executado 10 milhões de vezes por ano. Foi incluído em mais de 11.000 álbuns e traduzido para cerca de 60 línguas. Foi mencionado no romance antiescravagista de Harriet Beecher Stowe, A Cabana do Pai Tomás. Sua popularidade aumentou durante duas das maiores crises dos Estados Unidos: a Guerra Civil e a Guerra do Vietnã.

Ironicamente, esta canção comovente, intimamente associada à comunidade afro-americana, foi escrita por um antigo traficante de escravos, John Newton.

John nasceu em 24 de julho de 1725, em Wapping, Inglaterra, filho de um pai marinheiro, John Newton, Sr., e de uma mãe cristã devota, Elizabeth Newton. Seu pai o amava, mas passava a maior parte do tempo no mar. Sua mãe, por outro lado, era terna e carinhosa, ensinando-lhe a Palavra de Deus. Ela o orientava a memorizar capítulos inteiros da Bíblia de cada vez e o levava à igreja. Infelizmente, quando ele tinha quase sete anos, sua mãe morreu de tuberculose. Seu pai casou-se novamente pouco tempo depois e o enviou para um internato. Durante o tempo que passou no internato, fez más amizades. Seu caráter deteriorou-se a tal ponto que foi expulso de uma escola e transferido para outra. Quando chegou aos 11 anos, os internatos já não o queriam, de modo que seu pai o levou consigo para o mar. Ele passou os seis anos seguintes no oceano Atlântico com seu pai.

Quando John tinha 17 anos, seu pai providenciou sua ida para a Jamaica, onde teria um emprego bem remunerado como supervisor de uma plantação. No caminho, enquanto aguardava a partida do navio, John recebeu um convite para visitar a casa de antigos amigos, os Catlett. Fora naquela casa que a mãe de John havia morrido dez anos antes. Ao retomar o contato com eles, conheceu sua filha, Mary. As mães de John e Mary haviam sido grandes amigas. John fora convidado a ficar quatro dias, mas ficou duas semanas e perdeu o navio para a Jamaica.

Aos 18 anos, John foi recrutado à força para a Marinha Real, e sua vida foi de mal a pior. Queria voltar para ver Mary, por isso desertou do navio, mas foi capturado, açoitado publicamente e posto a ferros. Sua vida no navio era tão profana que até os outros marinheiros ímpios se horrorizavam com suas imprecações e blasfêmias. Ganhou o título de “O Grande Blasfemador” e era tão indesejado no navio que foi enviado para trabalhar num navio negreiro.

Um dos proprietários do navio negreiro onde agora trabalhava ofereceu a John um emprego para quando chegassem à costa africana. Contudo, assim que desembarcou, foi amarrado e forçado a trabalhar, com pouca comida, roupa ou abrigo. Durante esse período, enviou várias cartas ao pai, suplicando ajuda.

Um navio chamado The Greyhound navegava perto da costa que John agora chamava de lar. O capitão recebera instruções do pai de John para procurar seu filho. Embora o navio estivesse quase longe demais da costa para negociar, decidiu tentar fazer algum comércio. Um amigo de John remou desde a costa para negociar. Quando se virou para partir, o capitão perguntou-lhe se conhecia alguém chamado John Newton. Para surpresa do capitão, ele conhecia, e John foi levado a bordo para voltar para casa.

A bordo do navio, Newton pegou um exemplar do clássico cristão de Tomás de Kempis, A Imitação de Cristo. Nunca havia encontrado nada semelhante e começou a se perguntar se as afirmações cristãs poderiam ser verdadeiras. Naquela noite, em 10 de março de 1748, uma violenta tempestade quase afundou o navio. Homens, animais e provisões foram arrastados para fora do navio. A tempestade despertou Newton, com as madeiras apodrecidas do navio quebradas pelas ondas e a água da inundação invadindo sua cabine em redemoinhos. John orou pela primeira vez em anos.

The Greyhound foi sacudido pela tempestade no Atlântico Norte durante mais de 11 dias. Com pouca esperança de sobrevivência, os marinheiros operavam mecanicamente as bombas, tentando manter a embarcação à tona. No décimo primeiro dia da tempestade, John estava exausto demais para bombear, de modo que foi amarrado ao leme, onde fez o possível para manter o navio no rumo. Da uma hora até a meia-noite, permaneceu ao leme. Temia morrer e pensava que, se a fé cristã fosse verdadeira, certamente não seria perdoado. Refletiu sobre tudo o que havia feito nos últimos anos. Sua vida parecia tão arruinada e destroçada quanto o navio castigado que tentava conduzir pela tempestade. Durante aquelas longas e penosas horas, Newton clamou a Deus como nunca antes, e esse foi o ponto de viragem em sua vida.

John Newton se lembraria daquele dia para sempre. “Naquele dia, o Senhor enviou socorro do alto e me livrou das águas profundas.” Mais de 50 anos depois, em 21 de março de 1805, John escreveu em seu diário: “Não estou em boas condições para escrever; mas procuro assinalar o retorno deste dia com humilhação, oração e louvor.”

Somente a graça maravilhosa de Deus poderia tomar um marinheiro rude, profano e traficante de escravos e transformá-lo num filho de Deus. John nunca deixou de se maravilhar com a obra de Deus em sua vida. Passou a se interessar pela oração, pela leitura e meditação nas Escrituras e por falar somente palavras agradáveis a Deus.

Quando voltou para casa, Mary e seus pais reconheceram a mudança que o Senhor havia operado em John. Os dois se casaram em 1 de fevereiro de 1750.

Durante os quatro anos seguintes, Newton foi capitão de seu próprio navio negreiro. Essa ocupação o mantinha separado de Mary por meses a fio. Enquanto estavam separados, os dois se correspondiam constantemente. Em suas cartas, John escreveu repetidamente como o amor e o casamento deles aumentavam sua gratidão e reconhecimento ao Senhor. “... Quando me permito pensar especialmente em ti, isso geralmente me leva mais longe e me põe de joelhos para bendizer o Senhor por me ter dado tão grande tesouro e para orar por tua paz e teu bem-estar”

John procurou “cristianizar” seu navio negreiro, realizando cultos aos domingos para sua tripulação de 30 homens endurecidos pelo pecado. Fez mais três viagens para trazer escravos da África para a América do Norte. Enquanto planejava sua quarta viagem, adoeceu de malária. Deus usou essa doença para pôr fim ao seu envolvimento no tráfico de escravos.

Ao começar um novo capítulo de sua vida, John sentiu-se chamado a ser ministro. Durante mais de 50 anos, pregou o evangelho e foi um dos homens mais influentes de seu tempo.

John Newton frequentemente compunha um hino para acompanhar seus cultos de domingo à noite. Em 1779, 280 desses hinos foram reunidos e combinados com 68 hinos de William Cowper, amigo e paroquiano de Newton, e publicados como os Hinos de Olney. O mais famoso de todos os Hinos de Olney, “Retrospectiva e Expectativa da Fé”, nasceu da exclamação de Davi em 1 Crônicas 17:16-17. Hoje o conhecemos como “Graça Maravilhosa”. “Graça Maravilhosa” tinha originalmente seis estrofes, e a última estrofe foi acrescentada cerca de um século depois. A maioria dos hinários contém quatro ou cinco dessas estrofes.

Como ministro na igreja, John continuou a se inquietar cada vez mais com o tráfico de escravos que ainda prosseguia. Em 1788, 34 anos depois de ter abandonado o tráfico de escravos, escreveu um livro intitulado Reflexões sobre o Tráfico de Escravos Africanos e o enviou a todos os membros do parlamento. Esse livro conscientizou o público sobre os males do tráfico de escravos. Nele, escreveu: “Não é preciso dizer que capturar, vender e transportar escravos negros para as plantações nas Índias Ocidentais e na América era um modo de vida cruel e perverso.” Com a ajuda e a providência de Deus, John viu chegar o dia, vários meses antes de sua morte, em 1807, em que a escravidão foi oficialmente proibida na Inglaterra.

Quando John estava na casa dos sessenta anos, sua amada esposa Mary faleceu. Isso foi uma grande provação para John, e ele passou os 17 anos restantes de sua vida sem ela.

Depois de John sofrer um acidente vascular cerebral, e pouco antes de sua morte, um porta-voz da igreja encorajou Newton a considerar a possibilidade de deixar de pregar devido ao declínio de sua saúde, visão e memória. John respondeu: “O quê? Há de parar o velho blasfemador africano enquanto ainda pode falar? Continuarei a pregar. Embora minha memória esteja enfraquecendo, lembro-me de duas coisas com muita clareza: sou um grande pecador, e Cristo é um grande Salvador.”

As últimas palavras de John Newton, em seu leito de morte, foram estas: “Ainda estou na terra dos que morrem; em breve estarei na terra dos que vivem.”

A melodia de “Graça Maravilhosa” é uma antiga melodia popular americana. Foi inicialmente conhecida como uma melodia das plantações intitulada “Cordeiros Amorosos”. Essa melodia foi publicada pela primeira vez em 1831 no livro The Virginia Harmony. A maioria dos hinários publicados depois dessa época incluía essa canção. Em 1910, Edwin O. Excell acrescentou a última estrofe, que acabou por substituir as três últimas estrofes originais da canção. Sua edição da canção é a mais comum em nossos hinários hoje. Vários outros Hinos de Olney de Newton continuam a ser cantados hoje, incluindo “Quão Doce Soa o Nome de Jesus” e “Coisas Gloriosas São Ditas de Ti”.

Arise be glad! For dawn is here!
Rejoice and sing! The night is past,
The Dayspring shineth from on high,
The grace of God to man is nigh!
Rejoice and praise the King of Kings!
Give thanks and laud, for more is here!

Arise and glorify the Lord!
Extol and praise His worthy name!
He shineth from the heav’ns in love,
And showers blessings from above,
His mercy reaches down to men-
Adore and praise our mighty Lord!

Give thanks and sing to Christ our King
And worship Him with reverent praise;
Bow down in awful, holy fear-
The Holiness of God is here;
In wondrous beauty bend the knee;
Adore th’ almighty King of Kings!

“Dr. Waldron, Elsie needs help!” Elsie’s husband was adamant, almost angry, as he stared at me. On the other hand, Elsie stared at the floor, almost as though she wasn’t present. I had never met either of the couple before and was struggling just a little to figure out what was needed from me to help her.

“What is going on?” I asked as I flipped through her chart. This was still in the days of paper charts, and I headed to the lab section of her chart. There wasn’t anything too crazy that I could see there—her liver enzymes were a little elevated, but otherwise, everything seemed OK.

“It’s her drinking!” Her husband told me. “She is drinking more and more every night. She won’t go out except to get whiskey. She drinks till she passes out every night and has to have something every morning to get her started.”

“Is that true?” I asked Elsie, feeling like a judge overseeing a jury trial.

“Yes,” she said. Her face was emotionless, and I couldn’t tell if she wanted to be there or not.

“Do you want help?” I asked her. This was a loaded question. Many people who struggle with alcoholism aren’t ready to break free from its vice-like hold on them. Maybe Elsie was different.

“I guess so,” she said, indifferently. Once again, I couldn’t tell whether she wanted to be there or not.

“At the rate at which you are drinking, you will kill yourself within a year – maybe two at best – if you don’t give up alcohol entirely,” I told her. “If you want to, I will try to find you an inpatient program to detox you and get you off of alcohol.”

“She’s ready,” he husband said firmly.

When dealing with someone who drinks heavily, it is crucial that they don’t simply stop drinking without medical support. Abrupt cessation of alcohol use causes the body to go into withdrawal which can produce a state called Delirium Tremens and even seizures.

I stepped out of the exam room and to make phone calls. It is never easy to find a place for someone to attempt to rehabilitate from any kind of substances, and it was over an hour and a half before I found a facility that was willing to take Elsie and try to help her get off of the whiskey.

I sighed as I reentered her exam room. I had been afraid that I wouldn’t find anywhere for her to go.

I told them about the plan, and her husband nodded vigorously, while Elise continued to stare silently at the floor. “Can we pray together before you go?” I asked them, and when they nodded assent, I prayed with them, asking for freedom and Jesus’ presence in both of their lives.

They left my office with marching orders and directions on where to go. I had a happy glow about me for the rest of the morning, knowing that I had gone the extra mile and had really made a difference in this middle-aged couple’s life.

Around 2 pm, I got a call from the rehab facility. They hadn’t seen even a shadow of Elsie or her husband, which was surprising, since it was a bright sunny day and the facility wasn’t that far away. With a sinking feeling, I dialed the couple’s phone number.

“She won’t go!” Her husband told me. “She tells me that she told me this ahead of time. She’ll try to cut back, but she isn’t willing to go into a rehab facility or any such thing. I guess just tell them that we’ll let them know if she changes her mind.”

My nurse called the rehab facility and told them the bad news, and I sat down in my chair, stunned. What else could I have done? Was there a solution for Elsie—something different that I could have said that would have made a difference in her life?

About a year later, I received the sad news that Elsie had died at home. I was certain that things would have been different if she had gone to rehab and if she had given control to Jesus. None of that had happened, and I felt cynicism pushing into my heart.

Cynicism

We live in an age of cynicism. In ancient Greece, the cynics were an odd assortment of men who specialized in being grouchy and saying mean (they would have said truthful) things to people. They often dressed in rags and behaved in such a way that most of the polite Athenians did not want to be close to them.

Today, cynicism means a tendency to believe the worst about people and circumstances. Cynical people believe that all people are motivated purely by selfishness and that bad events will tend to prevail.

Many young doctors are idealistic and very hopeful. They believe that if they exert the utmost effort, they can make a real, positive impact on their patient’s lives. Unfortunately, as time goes by and they try their hardest and their patients don’t change, they can give up. These doctors still try, but they no longer really hope that their efforts will make much of a difference.

It seems as though people who get involved with politics often have the best of intentions. They see this as a path to changing society for the better. Unfortunately, as time goes by and the faces in charge change, the policies don’t really change, they tend to become cynical.

Sometimes this cynicism is directed against all politicians. Sometimes it is only anger directed against members of the party that opposes their party’s positions. Hope is replaced by cynicism.

Cynicism in the Bible

If there is a book in the Bible that seems to have been written by a cynical man, it is the book of Ecclesiastes. The Preacher, who we understand to be Solomon, lists all of the things that he endeavored in an attempt to find joy.

In chapter 2:17-23 Solomon describes work as futile. He finishes by saying, “For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun? For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.” (Ecclesiastes 2:22,23)

He saw the world as being dominated by tyrants and there was little that the people could do about it. Solomon went so far as to say that political power was meaningless “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor” (Ecclesiastes 4:13).

In Ecclesiastes 6:6, he seems to disparage long life. “Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?”

Of course, he finishes his short book with the instruction to remember our Creator in the days of our youth. There is a blessing for those who choose to focus on God when they have a little bit of energy left and not, when they are old and jaded, like Solomon.

Later on, it almost seemed as though God had given up on His people. He still sent prophets to them, but He knew without a doubt that the people would refuse to respond. “Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee” (Jeremiah 7:27).

Even in the New Testament, Paul told Timothy that the time was coming when people would no longer listen to sound doctrine. “For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;” (2 Timothy 4:3).

By picking and choosing these passages, we can come away with a very gloomy view of the future and, more specifically, of human’s willingness to change. It seems there is little point of investing ourselves in the people around us. They are full of woe and are as likely to change as a chipmunk is to master differential calculus.

The Opposite of Cynicism

The opposite of cynicism is hope. It is the belief that the future could be better.

It is interesting that the Apostle Paul spoke of tribulations in the Epistle to the Romans, “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us” (Romans 5:3-5).

We may not have reached the place where we glory in the trials we experience, but certainly, they should bring us these other things that he mentions. For, we grow in patience and experience, even as we deal with trials, but more than that, we come to realize that we have hope for tomorrow because we serve a great God.

The contrast in the story of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15 teaches us much about hope. The father and the older brother were strikingly different in their attitudes.

The father had never given up hope – he knew that his son had failed him and gone far from what he knew was right and yet, the father still desired to see the prodigal come to himself and return home.

On the other hand, the older brother not only had no hope for his younger brother, but he was also angry with him. The prodigal had wasted his money, he had lived in sin, and now, he had returned home just because he was out of money.

Certainly, there was no reason to trust the younger son. Yet, that is exactly what our Heavenly Father does for us.

Look for Hope in the Right Places

Part of the problem is that we look for hope in the wrong places. A number of years ago, a presidential candidate ran for office under the slogan “Hope and Change,” and yet, even though he was elected, I imagine most folks did not feel that their lives were significantly changed for the better.

Pursuing the things this world values—political power and wealth is guaranteed to bring emptiness. This is Satan’s pattern—he always over-promises and under-delivers.

This was what he did when he tempted Jesus, “All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:8). All of the things Satan offered, nothing compared with the glory that Jesus eventually received from the road that led to the cross.

In the same way, Satan would like to distract Christians from seeking the things that are valuable, and that will bring hope. Satan tells Christians that politics will not only change the world for the better, it is an easier way to change the world.

The Bible is clear that we build hope as we nurture our relationship with God and then work to help our brothers and sisters build that same relationship in their own lives. The reason that we can hope is not because people are so wonderful—we don’t have to live very long to realize that they aren’t. The reason we hope is because we serve an awesome, faithful God who walks with us through the worst of our trials.

Remember that We Have Undeserved Hope

Jesus’ messages about forgiveness make it clear that one of the major reasons that we have for forgiving others in our lives is that we have received great and undeserved forgiveness. The same is true for hope.

Each one of us was hopeless and without reason to expect to receive hope and we were still given a ray of light in the midst of our darkness. Maybe part of the reason that we have so much trouble hoping for good things for the people around us is that we do not remember how hopeless we were before we found grace.

If Jesus was able to bring hope to our hopeless existence, then certainly He can do wonderful things in the hearts and lives of others around us. The only people we should give up on are the ones that our Savior has given up on as well.

Small Efforts Do Make a Difference

I remember having a conversation with a young person who was planning to go into medicine and had a plan to go to a foreign country and serve the people there. As we were talking, an older man entered the conversation and shared that he saw little hope for change in developing countries.

The people in those countries just weren’t interested in getting better and didn’t do the minimum necessary to stave off things like worms and parasites. Doctors and nurses couldn’t make a difference in such an environment.

I could sense the heart of the youth sinking as this older man shared. He had experience, and he had given up hope. The sad thing was that he was also stealing the hope of someone who still had a desire to serve.

When I was in training, I had a surgeon tell me that family doctors didn’t really do anything. They simply kept their patients alive till their next office visit, whereas surgeons really “fixed” people—taking out (or off) the offending body part.

At the end of the day, small efforts do make a difference. I don’t do brain surgery, but I still can make a difference in someone else’s life— maybe just by spending a little time and listening and praying. This is true for all of us.

More than that, we come to realize that making this effort changes our own lives for the better. Jesus told the sheep that as they ministered to “the least of these my brethren,” they were ministering to Him.

Even if no one’s life is improved, our Savior knows our desires and feels our efforts, and will reward them someday.

A Few Things to Remember

When we face failures, we tend to move in one of two directions. Those of us who are optimists tend to believe that this episode was an isolated event and that the future is still bright. On the other hand, pessimists believe that failures are permanent, personal, and pervasive.

Pessimists believe that their failures are the result of intrinsic character flaws that they have and that these things affect all of their lives and are unlikely to change. Unlike the righteous man who falls to rise again, these people fall and lie where they fall, defeated at the outset.

When we are dealing with other people, we need to give them the same grace that we should give ourselves. They, too, are growing, and if they have a failure today, they will do better tomorrow. Maybe they will fail again, but they will at least “fail better.”

Conclusion

Cynicism is rife in our world. Many have given up hope for a better future, and it is understandable for those who have invested their hope in this world’s institutions. There is no real hope in government or in armies or in bureaucracy.

The song says, “Oh to have no hope in Jesus, how dark this world must be!” For, Jesus is the one who brings light into our darkness and allows us to continue, even when others fail us.

God is the one who redeems us. He is the one who sent the prophets, even though their messages were ignored, and the prophets were persecuted. He is the one who continues to hope for us, even when we have failed Him so many times in the past.

He is the reason we carry on. He is the reason that we have hope, not only for ourselves but also for our brothers.

“डॉ. वॉल्ड्रन, एल्सी को मदद चाहिए!” एल्सी का पति दृढ़ था, लगभग क्रोधित, जब वह मुझ पर घूर रहा था। दूसरी ओर, एल्सी फर्श की ओर घूर रही थी, मानो वह वहाँ मौजूद ही नहीं हो। मैं उस दम्पत्ति से पहले कभी मिला नहीं था और मुझे थोड़ी सिहरन हो रही थी कि मैं उसकी मदद के लिए क्या करना चाहिए।

“क्या चल रहा है?” मैंने उसके चार्ट पलटते हुए पूछा। यह अभी भी कागजी चार्ट के दिनों की बात थी, और मैं उसके चार्ट के लैब सेक्शन की ओर गया। वहाँ ऐसा कुछ भी पागलपन जैसा नहीं था—उसके लिवर एंजाइम थोड़े बढ़े हुए थे, परंतु अन्यथा सब कुछ ठीक लग रहा था।

“मुद्दा उसका शराब पीना है!” उसके पति ने मुझे बताया। “वह हर रात और अधिक पीती जा रही है। वह शराब लेने के अलावा कहीं नहीं जाती। वह हर रात तब तक पीती है जब तक बेहोश न हो जाए और हर सुबह कुछ न कुछ पीकर ही शुरू कर पाती है।”

“क्या यह सच है?” मैंने एल्सी से पूछा, मानो मैं किसी जूरी ट्रायल का जज हूँ।

“हाँ,” उसने कहा। उसका चेहरा भावहीन था, और मैं नहीं बता पा रहा था कि क्या वह वहाँ होना चाहती थी या नहीं।

“क्या तुम सहायता चाहती हो?” मैंने उससे पूछा। यह एक भारी प्रश्न था। कई लोग जो शराब की लत से जूझ रहे होते हैं, उसकी कसौटी छोड़ने को तैयार नहीं होते। शायद एल्सी अलग थी।

“शायद,” उसने उदासीनता से कहा। फिर भी, मैं यह नहीं जान पाया कि क्या वह वहाँ होना चाहती थी।

“जिस दर से तुम पी रही हो, यदि तुम पूरी तरह शराब छोड़ नहीं दोगी तो एक साल—शायद दो साल के भीतर—तुम अपनी जान गंवा दोगी,” मैंने उससे कहा। “यदि तुम चाहो तो मैं तुम्हारे लिए किसी इनपेशेंट प्रोग्राम की खोज करूँगा ताकि तुम्हें डिटॉक्स किया जा सके और शराब से बाहर निकाला जा सके।”

“वह तैयार है,” उसके पति ने दृढ़तापूर्वक कहा।

जब किसी के साथ भारी शराब की लत का सामना होता है, तो यह बेहद आवश्यक है कि वे केवल अचानक शराब लेना बंद न कर दें बिना चिकित्सकीय समर्थन के। शराब का अचानक त्याग शरीर को विदड्रॉल में ले जाता है जो डिलीरियम ट्रेमेन्स नामक स्थिति और यहाँ तक कि दौरे पैदा कर सकती है।

मैं परीक्षा कक्ष से बाहर गया और फोन कॉल्स करने लगा। किसी के लिए भी किसी प्रकार के पदार्थों से पुनर्वास की जगह ढूंढना कभी आसान नहीं होता, और एक घंटे से अधिक डेढ़ घंटे बाद ही मुझे एक ऐसी सुविधा मिली जो एल्सी को लेने के लिए तैयार थी और उसे व्हिस्की से छुड़ाने की कोशिश कर सकती थी।

मैंने साँस छोड़ी जब मैं फिर से उसकी परीक्षा कक्ष में गया। मुझे डर था कि मुझे उसके लिए कहीं भी स्थान नहीं मिलेगा।

मैंने उन्हें योजना के बारे में बताया, और उसका पति जोर से सिर हिलाने लगा, जबकि एलिसे चुपचाप फर्श को घूरती रही। “क्या हम प्रार्थना कर सकते हैं जाने से पहले?” मैंने उनसे पूछा, और जब उन्होंने सहमति में सिर हिलाया, तो मैंने उनके साथ प्रार्थना की, उनकी आज़ादी और दोनों के जीवन में यीशु की उपस्थिति के लिए प्रार्थना की।

वे मेरे कार्यालय से मार्गदर्शिका निर्देश लेकर चले गए और कहाँ जाना है यह जानकर। बाकी सुबह मेरे अंदर एक सुखद माहौल रहा, यह जानकर कि मैंने अतिरिक्त प्रयास किया और वास्तव में इस मध्य-वयस्क दम्पत्ति के जीवन में अंतर लाया।

लगभग 2 बजे, मुझे रिहैब सुविधा से कॉल आया। उन्होंने न तो एल्सी का अक्स देखा और न ही उसके पति का, जो आश्चर्यजनक था, चूँकि दिन उजला था और वह सुविधा इतनी दूर भी नहीं थी। एक डूबता हुआ अहसास लेकर, मैंने दम्पत्ति का फोन नंबर डायल किया।

“वह नहीं जाएगी!” उसके पति ने मुझे बताया। “वह कहती है कि उसने मुझे पहले ही बता दिया था। वह कम पीने की कोशिश करेगी, पर वह किसी रिहैब सुविधा या ऐसी किसी चीज़ में जाने को तैयार नहीं है। मुझे लगता है बस उन्हें बता देना कि अगर वह अपना मन बदलेगी तो हम उन्हें बताएँगे।”

मेरी नर्स ने रिहैब सुविधा को बुरी खबर बताई, और मैं अपनी कुर्सी पर बैठ गया, स्तब्ध। और क्या कर सकता था मैं? क्या एल्सी के लिए कोई समाधान था—ऐसा कुछ अलग जो मैंने कहा होता जो उसके जीवन में फर्क डाल देता?

लगभग एक साल बाद, मुझे दुःखद खबर मिली कि एल्सी घर पर ही मर गई थी। मैं निश्चय था कि अगर वह रिहैब गई होती और अगर उसने नियंत्रण यीशु को सौंप दिया होता तो चीजें अलग होतीं। ऐसा कुछ भी नहीं हुआ, और मैं महसूस कर रहा था कि मेरे ह्रदय में निंदकता घुस आई है।

निंदकता

हम निंदकता के युग में रहते हैं। प्राचीन ग्रीस में, साइनिक्स एक अजीब समूह थे जो खट्टे और कठोर बातें कहने में माहिर थे (वे कहते कि वे सच्ची बातें कह रहे थे)। वे अक्सर फटे-पुराने कपड़े पहनते और इतने अजीब व्यवहार करते कि अधिकांश सभ्य एथेनियन उनके पास रहना पसंद नहीं करते थे।

आज, निंदकता का अर्थ है लोगों और परिस्थितियों के बारे में सबसे बुरा मानने की प्रवृत्ति। निंदक लोग मानते हैं कि सभी लोग केवल स्वार्थ से प्रेरित होते हैं और बुरी घटनाएँ अधिक संभावना से हावी होंगी।

कई युवा डॉक्टर्स आदर्शवादी और बहुत आशावादी होते हैं। वे मानते हैं कि अगर वे अपनी पूरी मेहनत लगाएंगे तो वे अपने मरीजों के जीवन में वास्तव में सकारात्मक प्रभाव डाल सकते हैं। दुर्भाग्यवश, समय के साथ जब वे अपनी पूरी कोशिश करते हैं और उनके मरीज नहीं बदलते, तो वे हार मान सकते हैं। ये डॉक्टर अभी भी प्रयास करते हैं, पर अब वे वास्तव में उम्मीद नहीं रखते कि उनके प्रयास बड़ा फर्क डालेंगे।

ऐसा प्रतीत होता है कि राजनीति में शामिल लोग अक्सर सबसे अच्छे इरादों के साथ आते हैं। वे इसे समाज को बेहतर बनाने का मार्ग मानते हैं। दुर्भाग्यवश, समय के साथ और जब नेतृत्व के चेहरे बदलते हैं पर नीतियाँ वास्तव में बदलती नहीं हैं, तो वे निंदक हो जाते हैं।

कभी-कभी यह निंदकता सभी राजनेताओं के खिलाफ निर्देशित होती है। कभी-कभी यह केवल विरोधी दल के सदस्यों के प्रति क्रोध होता है। आशा की जगह निंदकता आ जाती है।

बाइबल में निंदकता

यदि बाइबल में कोई किताब ऐसी है जिसे लगता है कि किसी निंदक व्यक्ति ने लिखा है, तो वह उपदेशक की किताब (Ecclesiastes) है। उपदेशक, जिसे हम समझते हैं कि वह सुलैमान है, उसने उन सभी चीज़ों की सूची दी जो उसने आनंद खोजने के प्रयास में कीं।

अध्याय 2:17-23 में सुलैमान ने काम को व्यर्थ बताया। वह समाप्त करते हुए कहता है, “For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun? For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.” (Ecclesiastes 2:22,23)

उसने दुनिया को तानाशाहों द्वारा नियंत्रित देखा और लोगों के पास इसके खिलाफ बहुत कम करने का साधन था। सुलैमान इतना कह गए कि राजनीतिक शक्ति अर्थहीन है: “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor” (Ecclesiastes 4:13).

Ecclesiastes 6:6 में, वह लंबी उम्र की उपेक्षा करता प्रतीत होता है। “Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?”

बेशक, वह अपनी संक्षिप्त पुस्तक को हमारे सृष्टिकर्ता को अपनी युवावस्था के दिनों में याद रखने के निर्देश के साथ समाप्त करता है। जो लोग कुछ ऊर्जा के साथ परमेश्वर पर ध्यान केंद्रित करते हैं, उनके लिए आशीर्वाद है, न कि जब वे बूढ़े और ऊब चुके हों, जैसे सुलैमान।

बाद में, ऐसा प्रतीत होता है कि परमेश्वर ने अपने लोगों को छोड़ दिया था। उसने फिर भी उन्हें भविष्यवक्ता भेजे, पर वह निश्चय जानता था कि लोग जवाब देने से इंकार करेंगे। “Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee” (Jeremiah 7:27).

यहाँ तक कि नए नियम में भी, पौलुस ने तिमोथी से कहा कि ऐसा समय आएगा जब लोग ध्वनि शिक्षाशास्त्र को सुनना बंद कर देंगे। “For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;” (2 Timothy 4:3).

इन पदों को चुन-चुनकर पढ़कर, हम भविष्य और विशेषकर मानवों की बदलने की इच्छा के बारे में बहुत उदास दृष्टिकोण लेकर जा सकते हैं। ऐसा लगता है कि अपने आस-पास के लोगों में खुद को निवेश करने का कोई खास उद्देश्य नहीं है। वे दुःख से भरे हैं और उतने ही संभावना से बदलेंगे जितना कि एक चिपमंक विभेदनीय कलन का मास्टर बनने की संभावना रखता हो।

निंदकता का विपरीत

निंदकता का विपरीत है आशा। यह विश्वास है कि भविष्य बेहतर हो सकता है।

यह रोचक है कि प्रेरित पौलुस ने रोमियों को लिखे पौत्र में कष्टों के संबंध में कहा, “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us” (Romans 5:3-5).

हम शायद उस स्थान तक नहीं पहुंचे जहाँ हम अपने अनुभव किए trials में महिमा करते हैं, पर निश्चय ही वे हमें वे अन्य चीजें लानी चाहिए जो वह बताता है। क्योंकि, हम धैर्य और अनुभव में बढ़ते हैं, भले ही हम परीक्षाओं से गुज़र रहे हों, परन्तु उससे भी अधिक, हम यह समझने लगते हैं कि हमारे पास कल के लिए आशा है क्योंकि हम एक महान परमेश्वर की सेवा करते हैं।

ल्यूक 15 की आवारा पुत्र की कहानी में विरोध हमारे लिए आशा के बारे में बहुत सिखाता है। पिता और बड़े भाई के दृष्टिकोण में भारी अंतर था।

पिता ने कभी आशा नहीं छोड़ी—वह जानता था कि उसका पुत्र ने उसे धोखा दिया और वह उस सही मार्ग से दूर चला गया, फिर भी पिता चाहता था कि आवारा अपने को जानकर घर लौट आए।

दूसरी ओर, बड़े भाई ने न केवल अपने छोटे भाई के लिए कोई आशा नहीं रखी, बल्कि वह उससे क्रोधित भी था। आवारा ने अपना धन बर्बाद कर दिया था, वह पाप में रहा, और अब वह केवल इसलिए घर लौटा था कि उसके पास पैसे नहीं रहे।

निश्चित रूप से, छोटे पुत्र पर भरोसा करने का कोई कारण नहीं था। फिर भी, यही हमारे स्वर्गीय पिता हमारे लिए करते हैं।

सही जगहों पर आशा ढूँढो

समस्या का हिस्सा यह है कि हम आशा को गलत जगहों पर ढूंढते हैं। कई साल पहले, एक राष्ट्रपति पद के उम्मीदवार ने “Hope and Change” का नारा दिया, और फिर भी, भले ही वह चुना गया, मुझे लगता है ज्यादातर लोगों ने महसूस नहीं किया कि उनके जीवन में उल्लेखनीय रूप से कोई सुधार हुआ।

इस दुनिया की वे चीज़ें जो मूल्यवान मानी जाती हैं—राजनीतिक सत्ता और धन—उनका पीछा करने से खालीपन निश्चित है। यह शैतान का तरीका है—वह हमेशा अधिक वादा करता है और कम देता है।

यही उसने यीशु का प्रलोभन करते समय किया, “All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:8). शैतान ने जो भी चीजें प्रस्तावित कीं, उन सबका कोई तुलना नहीं था उस महिमा से जो यीशु को अंततः क्रूस के रास्ते से मिली।

इसी तरह, शैतान ईसाइयों को उन चीज़ों की खोज से भटका देना चाहता है जो मूल्यवान हैं और जो आशा लाएँगी। शैतान ईसाइयों से कहता है कि राजनीति न केवल दुनिया को बेहतर बनाएगी, बल्कि यह दुनिया बदलने का एक आसान तरीका है।

बाइबल स्पष्ट कहती है कि हम आशा का निर्माण करते हैं जब हम परमेश्वर के साथ अपने संबंध को पोषित करते हैं और फिर अपने भाइयों और बहनों की मदद करते हैं कि वे भी अपने जीवन में वही संबंध बनाएँ। हम आशा इसलिए कर सकते हैं क्योंकि लोग इतने अद्भुत हैं—हमें बहुत ज़्यादा जीवन नहीं जीना पड़ता यह समझने के लिए कि वे नहीं हैं। हम आशा इसलिए करते हैं क्योंकि हम एक भयानक, वफादार परमेश्वर की सेवा करते हैं जो हमारे साथ हमारे कष्टों के सबसे बुरे समय से भी चलता है।

याद रखो कि हमारे पास अनर्थित आशा है

यीशु के क्षमा के संदेश स्पष्ट करते हैं कि हमारे जीवन में दूसरों को क्षमा करने के प्रमुख कारणों में से एक यह है कि हमें भी बड़ा और बिना हक का क्षमा मिला है। आशा के लिए भी यही सत्य है।

हम में से हर एक असहाय था और आशा प्राप्त करने की कोई वजह नहीं थी और फिर भी हमें अंधकार के बीच एक किरण दी गई। शायद उस कारण का हिस्सा है कि हमें अपने आस-पास के लोगों के लिए अच्छी चीजों की आशा करने में इतनी परेशानी होती है, कि हम यह याद नहीं करते कि जब हमने अनुग्रह पाया उससे पहले हम कितने असहाय थे।

यदि यीशु हमारी असहाय उपस्थिति में आशा ला सके, तो निश्चय ही वह हमारे आसपास के अन्य लोगों के दिलों और जीवन में अद्भुत कार्य कर सकता है। केवल उन्हीं लोगों को हमें छोड़ देना चाहिए जिनके लिए हमारे उद्धारकर्ता ने भी छोड़ दिया हो।

छोटे प्रयास वास्तव में फर्क डालते हैं

मुझे एक युवा से हुई बातचीत याद है जो चिकित्सा में जाना चाहता था और विदेश जाकर वहाँ के लोगों की सेवा करने की योजना बना रहा था। जब हम बात कर रहे थे, एक बड़ा आदमी बातचीत में आया और साझा किया कि वह विकासशील देशों में परिवर्तन की बहुत कम आशा देखता है।

उन देशों के लोग बेहतर होने में दिलचस्पी नहीं रखते थे और वर्म्स और परजीवियों जैसी चीज़ों को टालने के लिए न्यूनतम आवश्यक चीज़ें भी नहीं करते थे। ऐसे माहौल में डॉक्टर और नर्सें फर्क नहीं कर सकती थीं।

मैं उस युवा का मन धीमा होता हुआ महसूस कर पाया जब उस बड़े आदमी ने साझा किया। उसके पास अनुभव था, और उसने आशा छोड़ दी थी। दुःख की बात यह थी कि वह किसी ऐसे व्यक्ति की आशा भी चुरा रहा था जिसमें अभी भी सेवा की इच्छा थी।

जब मैं प्रशिक्षण में था, एक सर्जन ने मुझसे कहा था कि परिवार के डॉक्टर वास्तव में कुछ नहीं करते। वे केवल अपने मरीजों को अगले ऑफिस विज़िट तक जीवित रखते हैं, जबकि सर्जन वास्तव में लोगों को “ठीक” करते हैं—आक्रमणकारी अंग को निकाल देते हैं।

दिन के अंत में, छोटे प्रयास वाकई फर्क डालते हैं। मैं ब्रेन सर्जरी नहीं करता, पर मैं फिर भी किसी और के जीवन में फर्क कर सकता हूँ—शायद केवल थोड़ा समय देकर सुनकर और प्रार्थना कर के। यह हम सभी के लिए सच है।

उससे भी अधिक, हम यह महसूस करने लगते हैं कि यह प्रयास करना हमारे अपने जीवन को बेहतर बनाता है। यीशु ने भेड़ों से कहा कि जब वे “मेरे भाईयों में से सबसे छोटे को” सेवा करते हैं तो वे मुझसे सेवा कर रहे होते हैं।

यहाँ तक कि यदि किसी का जीवन सुधरता भी नहीं, हमारा उद्धारकर्ता हमारी इच्छाओं को जानता है और हमारे प्रयासों को महसूस करता है, और उन्हें कभी न कभी पुरस्कार देगा।

कुछ बातें याद रखने के लिए

जब हम असफलताओं का सामना करते हैं, तो हम दो दिशाओं में से एक की ओर जाने लगते हैं। हम में से जो आशावादी हैं, वह मानते हैं कि यह घटना एक अलग-थलग घटना थी और भविष्य अभी भी उज्जवल है। दूसरी ओर, निराशावादी मानते हैं कि असफलताएँ स्थायी, व्यक्तिगत और सर्वव्यापी हैं।

निराशावादी मानते हैं कि उनकी असफलताएँ उनके अंदर मौजूद मूलभूत चरित्र दोषों का परिणाम हैं और ये बातें उनके पूरे जीवन को प्रभावित करती हैं और बदलने की संभावना कम है। धर्मी व्यक्ति जो गिरता है और फिर उठता है, उन लोगों के विपरीत, ये लोग गिरते हैं और जहाँ गिरे वहीं पड़े रहते हैं, शुरु से ही पराजित।

जब हम दूसरों के साथ व्यवहार कर रहे होते हैं, तो हमें उन्हें वही अनुग्रह देना चाहिए जो हमें खुद को देना चाहिए। वे भी बढ़ रहे हैं, और यदि आज वे असफल होते हैं, तो वे कल बेहतर करेंगे। शायद वे फिर से असफल होंगे, पर कम से कम वे “बेहतर असफल” होंगे।

निष्कर्ष

हमारी दुनिया में निंदकता व्यापक है। कई लोगों ने बेहतर भविष्य की आशा छोड़ दी है, और उन लोगों के लिए यह समझ में आता है जिन्होंने अपनी आशा इस दुनिया की संस्थाओं में निवेश की है। सरकार या सेनाओं या नौकरशाही में कोई वास्तविक आशा नहीं है।

गीत कहता है, “Oh to have no hope in Jesus, how dark this world must be!” क्योंकि यीशु वही है जो हमारे अंधकार में प्रकाश लाता है और हमें जारी रखने की अनुमति देता है, भले ही अन्य लोग हमें नाकाम करें।

परमेश्वर ही हमें उद्धार करता है। वही है जिसने भविष्यद्वक्ताओं को भेजा, भले ही उनके संदेशों की अनदेखी की गई और भविष्यद्वक्ताओं का उत्पीड़न हुआ। वही है जो हमारे लिए आशा करना जारी रखता है, भले ही हमने उसे अतीत में इतने बार असफल किया हो।

वही कारण है कि हम चलते रहते हैं। वही कारण है कि हमारे पास आशा है, न केवल अपने लिए बल्कि अपने भाइयों के लिए भी।

“Dr. Waldron, Elsie needs help!” Elsie’s husband was adamant, almost angry, as he stared at me. On the other hand, Elsie stared at the floor, almost as though she wasn’t present. I had never met either of the couple before and was struggling just a little to figure out what was needed from me to help her.

“What is going on?” I asked as I flipped through her chart. This was still in the days of paper charts, and I headed to the lab section of her chart. There wasn’t anything too crazy that I could see there—her liver enzymes were a little elevated, but otherwise, everything seemed OK.

“It’s her drinking!” Her husband told me. “She is drinking more and more every night. She won’t go out except to get whiskey. She drinks till she passes out every night and has to have something every morning to get her started.”

“Is that true?” I asked Elsie, feeling like a judge overseeing a jury trial.

“Yes,” she said. Her face was emotionless, and I couldn’t tell if she wanted to be there or not.

“Do you want help?” I asked her. This was a loaded question. Many people who struggle with alcoholism aren’t ready to break free from its vice-like hold on them. Maybe Elsie was different.

“I guess so,” she said, indifferently. Once again, I couldn’t tell whether she wanted to be there or not.

“At the rate at which you are drinking, you will kill yourself within a year – maybe two at best – if you don’t give up alcohol entirely,” I told her. “If you want to, I will try to find you an inpatient program to detox you and get you off of alcohol.”

“She’s ready,” he husband said firmly.

When dealing with someone who drinks heavily, it is crucial that they don’t simply stop drinking without medical support. Abrupt cessation of alcohol use causes the body to go into withdrawal which can produce a state called Delirium Tremens and even seizures.

I stepped out of the exam room and to make phone calls. It is never easy to find a place for someone to attempt to rehabilitate from any kind of substances, and it was over an hour and a half before I found a facility that was willing to take Elsie and try to help her get off of the whiskey.

I sighed as I reentered her exam room. I had been afraid that I wouldn’t find anywhere for her to go.

I told them about the plan, and her husband nodded vigorously, while Elise continued to stare silently at the floor. “Can we pray together before you go?” I asked them, and when they nodded assent, I prayed with them, asking for freedom and Jesus’ presence in both of their lives.

They left my office with marching orders and directions on where to go. I had a happy glow about me for the rest of the morning, knowing that I had gone the extra mile and had really made a difference in this middle-aged couple’s life.

Around 2 pm, I got a call from the rehab facility. They hadn’t seen even a shadow of Elsie or her husband, which was surprising, since it was a bright sunny day and the facility wasn’t that far away. With a sinking feeling, I dialed the couple’s phone number.

“She won’t go!” Her husband told me. “She tells me that she told me this ahead of time. She’ll try to cut back, but she isn’t willing to go into a rehab facility or any such thing. I guess just tell them that we’ll let them know if she changes her mind.”

My nurse called the rehab facility and told them the bad news, and I sat down in my chair, stunned. What else could I have done? Was there a solution for Elsie—something different that I could have said that would have made a difference in her life?

About a year later, I received the sad news that Elsie had died at home. I was certain that things would have been different if she had gone to rehab and if she had given control to Jesus. None of that had happened, and I felt cynicism pushing into my heart.

Cynicism

We live in an age of cynicism. In ancient Greece, the cynics were an odd assortment of men who specialized in being grouchy and saying mean (they would have said truthful) things to people. They often dressed in rags and behaved in such a way that most of the polite Athenians did not want to be close to them.

Today, cynicism means a tendency to believe the worst about people and circumstances. Cynical people believe that all people are motivated purely by selfishness and that bad events will tend to prevail.

Many young doctors are idealistic and very hopeful. They believe that if they exert the utmost effort, they can make a real, positive impact on their patient’s lives. Unfortunately, as time goes by and they try their hardest and their patients don’t change, they can give up. These doctors still try, but they no longer really hope that their efforts will make much of a difference.

It seems as though people who get involved with politics often have the best of intentions. They see this as a path to changing society for the better. Unfortunately, as time goes by and the faces in charge change, the policies don’t really change, they tend to become cynical.

Sometimes this cynicism is directed against all politicians. Sometimes it is only anger directed against members of the party that opposes their party’s positions. Hope is replaced by cynicism.

Cynicism in the Bible

If there is a book in the Bible that seems to have been written by a cynical man, it is the book of Ecclesiastes. The Preacher, who we understand to be Solomon, lists all of the things that he endeavored in an attempt to find joy.

In chapter 2:17-23 Solomon describes work as futile. He finishes by saying, “For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun? For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.” (Ecclesiastes 2:22,23)

He saw the world as being dominated by tyrants and there was little that the people could do about it. Solomon went so far as to say that political power was meaningless “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor” (Ecclesiastes 4:13).

In Ecclesiastes 6:6, he seems to disparage long life. “Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?”

Of course, he finishes his short book with the instruction to remember our Creator in the days of our youth. There is a blessing for those who choose to focus on God when they have a little bit of energy left and not, when they are old and jaded, like Solomon.

Later on, it almost seemed as though God had given up on His people. He still sent prophets to them, but He knew without a doubt that the people would refuse to respond. “Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee” (Jeremiah 7:27).

Even in the New Testament, Paul told Timothy that the time was coming when people would no longer listen to sound doctrine. “For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;” (2 Timothy 4:3).

By picking and choosing these passages, we can come away with a very gloomy view of the future and, more specifically, of human’s willingness to change. It seems there is little point of investing ourselves in the people around us. They are full of woe and are as likely to change as a chipmunk is to master differential calculus.

The Opposite of Cynicism

The opposite of cynicism is hope. It is the belief that the future could be better.

It is interesting that the Apostle Paul spoke of tribulations in the Epistle to the Romans, “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us” (Romans 5:3-5).

We may not have reached the place where we glory in the trials we experience, but certainly, they should bring us these other things that he mentions. For, we grow in patience and experience, even as we deal with trials, but more than that, we come to realize that we have hope for tomorrow because we serve a great God.

The contrast in the story of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15 teaches us much about hope. The father and the older brother were strikingly different in their attitudes.

The father had never given up hope – he knew that his son had failed him and gone far from what he knew was right and yet, the father still desired to see the prodigal come to himself and return home.

On the other hand, the older brother not only had no hope for his younger brother, but he was also angry with him. The prodigal had wasted his money, he had lived in sin, and now, he had returned home just because he was out of money.

Certainly, there was no reason to trust the younger son. Yet, that is exactly what our Heavenly Father does for us.

Look for Hope in the Right Places

Part of the problem is that we look for hope in the wrong places. A number of years ago, a presidential candidate ran for office under the slogan “Hope and Change,” and yet, even though he was elected, I imagine most folks did not feel that their lives were significantly changed for the better.

Pursuing the things this world values—political power and wealth is guaranteed to bring emptiness. This is Satan’s pattern—he always over-promises and under-delivers.

This was what he did when he tempted Jesus, “All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:8). All of the things Satan offered, nothing compared with the glory that Jesus eventually received from the road that led to the cross.

In the same way, Satan would like to distract Christians from seeking the things that are valuable, and that will bring hope. Satan tells Christians that politics will not only change the world for the better, it is an easier way to change the world.

The Bible is clear that we build hope as we nurture our relationship with God and then work to help our brothers and sisters build that same relationship in their own lives. The reason that we can hope is not because people are so wonderful—we don’t have to live very long to realize that they aren’t. The reason we hope is because we serve an awesome, faithful God who walks with us through the worst of our trials.

Remember that We Have Undeserved Hope

Jesus’ messages about forgiveness make it clear that one of the major reasons that we have for forgiving others in our lives is that we have received great and undeserved forgiveness. The same is true for hope.

Each one of us was hopeless and without reason to expect to receive hope and we were still given a ray of light in the midst of our darkness. Maybe part of the reason that we have so much trouble hoping for good things for the people around us is that we do not remember how hopeless we were before we found grace.

If Jesus was able to bring hope to our hopeless existence, then certainly He can do wonderful things in the hearts and lives of others around us. The only people we should give up on are the ones that our Savior has given up on as well.

Small Efforts Do Make a Difference

I remember having a conversation with a young person who was planning to go into medicine and had a plan to go to a foreign country and serve the people there. As we were talking, an older man entered the conversation and shared that he saw little hope for change in developing countries.

The people in those countries just weren’t interested in getting better and didn’t do the minimum necessary to stave off things like worms and parasites. Doctors and nurses couldn’t make a difference in such an environment.

I could sense the heart of the youth sinking as this older man shared. He had experience, and he had given up hope. The sad thing was that he was also stealing the hope of someone who still had a desire to serve.

When I was in training, I had a surgeon tell me that family doctors didn’t really do anything. They simply kept their patients alive till their next office visit, whereas surgeons really “fixed” people—taking out (or off) the offending body part.

At the end of the day, small efforts do make a difference. I don’t do brain surgery, but I still can make a difference in someone else’s life— maybe just by spending a little time and listening and praying. This is true for all of us.

More than that, we come to realize that making this effort changes our own lives for the better. Jesus told the sheep that as they ministered to “the least of these my brethren,” they were ministering to Him.

Even if no one’s life is improved, our Savior knows our desires and feels our efforts, and will reward them someday.

A Few Things to Remember

When we face failures, we tend to move in one of two directions. Those of us who are optimists tend to believe that this episode was an isolated event and that the future is still bright. On the other hand, pessimists believe that failures are permanent, personal, and pervasive.

Pessimists believe that their failures are the result of intrinsic character flaws that they have and that these things affect all of their lives and are unlikely to change. Unlike the righteous man who falls to rise again, these people fall and lie where they fall, defeated at the outset.

When we are dealing with other people, we need to give them the same grace that we should give ourselves. They, too, are growing, and if they have a failure today, they will do better tomorrow. Maybe they will fail again, but they will at least “fail better.”

Conclusion

Cynicism is rife in our world. Many have given up hope for a better future, and it is understandable for those who have invested their hope in this world’s institutions. There is no real hope in government or in armies or in bureaucracy.

The song says, “Oh to have no hope in Jesus, how dark this world must be!” For, Jesus is the one who brings light into our darkness and allows us to continue, even when others fail us.

God is the one who redeems us. He is the one who sent the prophets, even though their messages were ignored, and the prophets were persecuted. He is the one who continues to hope for us, even when we have failed Him so many times in the past.

He is the reason we carry on. He is the reason that we have hope, not only for ourselves but also for our brothers.

“沃尔德伦医生，埃尔西需要帮助！”埃尔西的丈夫盯着我，态度坚决，几乎带着怒气。埃尔西却盯着地板，仿佛人不在这里。我以前从未见过这对夫妇，一时有些摸不清，要帮助她究竟需要我做些什么。

“出了什么事？”我一边翻阅她的病历，一边问道。那时还在使用纸质病历，我翻到了化验记录的部分。我没有发现什么特别异常的情况——她的肝酶略有升高，但除此之外，一切看起来都还好。

“是她喝酒的问题！”她丈夫告诉我。“她每晚喝得越来越多。除了买威士忌，她根本不出门。她每天晚上都喝到不省人事，每天早晨还得喝点酒才能开始一天的生活。”

“是这样吗？”我问埃尔西，感觉自己像个主持陪审团审判的法官。

“是的，”她说。她脸上毫无表情，我看不出她是否愿意来这里。

“你想得到帮助吗？”我问她。这是个分量很重的问题。许多深陷酒瘾的人还没有准备好挣脱酒精对他们如虎钳般的控制。也许埃尔西会不一样。

“大概吧，”她冷淡地说。我仍然看不出她是否愿意来这里。

“照你现在这样喝下去，如果不彻底戒酒，一年之内你就会把自己的命喝掉——最多也许两年，”我告诉她。“如果你愿意，我会尽力为你找一个住院治疗项目，帮助你度过戒断期，戒掉酒精。”

“她准备好了，”她丈夫坚定地说。

面对一个大量饮酒的人，至关重要的是，不能让他们在没有医疗支持的情况下就直接停酒。突然停止饮酒会使身体出现戒断反应，可能引发一种叫作震颤谵妄的状态，甚至导致癫痫发作。

我走出诊室去打电话。为需要戒除任何成瘾物质的人找到康复治疗的地方，从来都不容易。过了一个半小时多，我才找到一家愿意接收埃尔西、尝试帮助她戒掉威士忌的机构。

重新走进诊室时，我叹了口气。我一直担心找不到任何可以让她去的地方。

我把计划告诉他们，她丈夫使劲点头，埃莉斯却依然默默地盯着地板。“你们走之前，我们能一起祷告吗？”我问他们。他们点头同意后，我便与他们一起祷告，求主使他们得自由，也求耶稣与他们两人的生命同在。

他们带着明确的行动指示和前往那里的路线离开了我的诊所。那天上午余下的时间，我心里一直洋溢着喜悦，因为我知道自己多付出了努力，确实为这对中年夫妇的生活带来了改变。

下午两点左右，康复机构给我打来电话。他们连埃尔西或她丈夫的影子都没见到。这很令人意外，因为那天天气晴朗，阳光明媚，而且那家机构离得并不远。我心里一沉，拨通了这对夫妇的电话。

“她不肯去！”她丈夫告诉我。“她说她早就跟我说过了。她会试着少喝一点，但她不愿意进康复机构，也不愿意接受诸如此类的安排。我想，你就告诉他们，要是她改变主意，我们会通知他们。”

我的护士打电话把这个坏消息告诉了康复机构，我则呆呆地坐进椅子里。我还能做些什么呢？有没有能帮助埃尔西的办法——我是否可以换一种说法，从而改变她的生活？

大约一年后，我得知了埃尔西在家中去世的噩耗。我确信，如果她去了康复机构，如果她把掌管权交给耶稣，事情就会不一样。然而，这两件事都没有发生，我感到愤世嫉俗的情绪正侵入我的内心。

愤世嫉俗

我们生活在一个愤世嫉俗的时代。在古希腊，犬儒派是一群古怪的人，他们专门向人发牢骚，说些刻薄的话（他们自己会说那是真话）。他们常常衣衫褴褛，举止也让大多数彬彬有礼的雅典人不愿靠近他们。

如今，愤世嫉俗指的是一种倾向，即总把人和处境往最坏的方面想。愤世嫉俗的人认为，所有人的动机都纯粹出于自私，而坏事往往会占上风。

许多年轻医生怀抱理想，满怀希望。他们相信，只要竭尽全力，就能给病人的生活带来真正积极的影响。可惜，随着时间过去，他们已经尽了最大努力，病人却没有改变，他们便可能放弃。这些医生仍然在努力，却不再真正期望自己的努力能带来多大的改变。

参与政治的人似乎往往怀着最好的初衷。他们把政治看作一条让社会变得更好的道路。可惜，随着时间过去，掌权的人换了，政策却没有真正改变，他们往往就变得愤世嫉俗。

有时，这种愤世嫉俗针对的是所有政治人物。有时，它只是针对那些与自己所属政党的立场相对立的政党成员的怒气。愤世嫉俗取代了希望。

圣经中的愤世嫉俗

如果圣经中有一卷书看起来像是由一个愤世嫉俗的人写成的，那就是《传道书》。我们认为其中的传道者就是所罗门，他列举了自己为寻求喜乐而尝试的一切事情。

在第2:17-23节中，所罗门将工作描述为徒劳。他最后说：“人在日光之下劳碌，心中烦忧，他这一切的劳碌究竟给他带来什么呢？因为他一生的日子都是忧愁，他的劳苦都是悲伤；甚至夜间，他的心也不得安歇。这也是虚空。”（传道书2:22,23）

他看见世界被暴君统治，而百姓几乎无能为力。所罗门甚至说，政治权力毫无意义：“贫穷而有智慧的少年，胜过年老而愚昧、不再肯接受劝诫的君王。因为他从监牢出来作王；而那生在自己国中的，也会变得贫穷。”（传道书4:13）

在传道书6:6中，他似乎贬低长寿的价值。“即使他活了一千年的两倍，却没有见过福乐，众人岂不都归到同一个地方吗？”

当然，他在这卷短书的结尾，教导我们要在年轻的日子记念创造我们的主。那些选择在还剩一些精力时就专注于上帝，而不是像所罗门那样，等到年老、厌倦一切时才这样做的人，是有福的。

后来，上帝几乎像是已经放弃了祂的子民。祂仍然向他们差遣先知，但祂毫无疑问地知道，这些人会拒绝回应。“所以，你要把这一切话告诉他们，他们却不听从你；你也要呼唤他们，他们却不回答你。”（耶利米书7:27）

即使在新约中，保罗也告诉提摩太，时候将到，人们不再听从纯正的教导。“因为时候将到，他们不肯容忍纯正的教导，反倒因耳朵发痒，照着自己的欲望，为自己聚集许多教师；”（提摩太后书4:3）

如果挑选这些经文来读，我们可能对未来产生非常阴暗的看法，尤其是对人愿不愿意改变的看法。这样看来，把自己投入到身边的人身上似乎没什么意义。他们满是愁苦，要他们改变，就像要一只花栗鼠精通微分学一样不可能。

愤世嫉俗的反面

愤世嫉俗的反面是盼望，是相信未来可以更好。

有趣的是，使徒保罗在《罗马书》中谈到了患难：“不但如此，我们也以患难为荣；因为知道患难产生忍耐，忍耐产生老练，老练产生盼望；盼望不会使人蒙羞，因为上帝的爱藉着赐给我们的圣灵，倾注在我们心里。”（罗马书5:3-5）

我们也许还没有达到以自己经历的试炼为荣的地步，但试炼当然应当给我们带来他所提到的其他这些品质。因为即使在应对试炼时，我们也在忍耐和老练上成长。更重要的是，我们逐渐认识到，自己对明天有盼望，因为我们所事奉的是一位伟大的上帝。

路加福音15章浪子故事中的对比，教导了我们许多有关盼望的事。父亲和哥哥的态度截然不同。

父亲从未放弃盼望——他知道儿子辜负了他，远远偏离了自己明知是正确的道路，然而，父亲依然渴望看见浪子醒悟过来，回到家中。

另一方面，哥哥不仅对弟弟没有盼望，而且还对他满怀怒气。浪子挥霍了钱财，活在罪中，如今只是因为钱花光了才回家。

的确，没有理由信任这个小儿子。然而，我们的天父对我们所做的，恰恰就是如此。

在正确的地方寻找盼望

问题部分在于，我们在错误的地方寻找盼望。若干年前，一位总统候选人以“希望与变革”为口号竞选。然而，尽管他当选了，我想大多数人并没有觉得自己的生活明显变好了。

追求这个世界所看重的东西——政治权力和财富——必定带来空虚。这就是撒但的惯常做法：他总是承诺过多，兑现过少。

他试探耶稣时就是这样做的：“你若俯伏敬拜我，我就把这一切都赐给你。”（马太福音4:8）撒但所提供的一切，没有一样能与耶稣最终沿着通往十字架的道路所获得的荣耀相比。

同样，撒但想使基督徒分心，不去追求那些有价值、能带来盼望的事物。撒但告诉基督徒，政治不但能让世界变得更好，而且是改变世界的一条更轻松的道路。

圣经清楚表明，当我们培育自己与上帝的关系，并努力帮助弟兄姐妹在他们的生命中建立同样的关系时，盼望就会增长。我们能够盼望，并不是因为人有多么美好——我们不必活很久就会发现，人并非如此。我们怀有盼望，是因为我们所事奉的是一位令人敬畏、信实的上帝，祂在我们最艰难的试炼中与我们同行。

记得我们拥有本不配得的盼望

耶稣关于饶恕的教导清楚表明，我们饶恕生活中他人的一个主要原因，是我们已经领受了极大、且本不配得的饶恕。盼望也是如此。

我们每一个人原本都毫无盼望，也没有理由期待得到盼望，然而，我们仍然在黑暗中蒙赐一线光明。也许，我们之所以很难盼望身边的人得着好事，部分原因就在于，我们不记得自己在找到恩典之前，是多么没有盼望。

如果耶稣能为我们毫无盼望的生命带来盼望，祂当然也能在我们身边其他人的心中和生命中成就美好的事。我们唯一应当放弃的人，就是我们的救主也已经放弃的人。

微小的努力确实能带来改变

我记得曾和一位年轻人交谈，他打算从医，也计划去国外服事那里的人。我们谈话时，一位年长的男士加入进来，说他认为发展中国家几乎没有改变的希望。

那些国家的人根本不想变得更好，连预防蠕虫和寄生虫之类问题所需的最低限度措施也不愿做。在这样的环境中，医生和护士不可能带来改变。

听着这位年长者的话，我能感觉到那年轻人的心越来越沉重。这位年长者有经验，却已经放弃了盼望。可悲的是，他也在夺走一个仍然渴望服事之人的盼望。

我接受培训时，一位外科医生曾告诉我，家庭医生其实没做什么。他们只不过是让病人活到下次来诊，而外科医生才真正把人“修好”——把出问题的身体部位切除或截掉。

归根结底，微小的努力确实能带来改变。我不做脑部手术，却仍然能够改变别人的生活——也许只是花一点时间倾听和祷告。我们每个人都是如此。

更进一步，我们逐渐认识到，付出这样的努力也会使我们自己的生命变得更好。耶稣告诉那些绵羊，他们服事“我这些弟兄中最微小的”，就是在服事祂。

即使没有任何人的生活得到改善，我们的救主仍知道我们的心愿，感受到我们的努力，并且有一天会给予赏赐。

几件需要记住的事

面对失败时，我们往往会走向两个方向之一。我们当中乐观的人往往相信，这次遭遇只是一个孤立事件，未来依然光明。另一方面，悲观的人则认为，失败是永久的、源于自身的，而且影响一切。

悲观的人认为，自己的失败源于内在的性格缺陷，这些缺陷影响着他们生活的方方面面，而且不太可能改变。他们不像那跌倒后又起来的义人，而是跌倒之后就躺在原地，一开始便认输了。

与他人相处时，我们需要给予他们同样的恩典，就像我们应当给予自己的一样。他们也在成长，今天若失败了，明天就会做得更好。也许他们还会失败，但至少会“失败得更好”。

结语

愤世嫉俗在我们的世界里盛行。许多人已经放弃了对更美好未来的盼望；对于那些把希望寄托在这个世界的制度和机构上的人来说，这是可以理解的。政府、军队和官僚体制中，都没有真正的盼望。

有首歌唱道：“啊，若在耶稣里没有盼望，这世界该是何等黑暗！”因为，正是耶稣为我们的黑暗带来光明，使我们即使在别人辜负我们时，也能继续前行。

上帝是救赎我们的那一位。差遣先知的是祂，尽管先知的信息被置之不理，先知也遭受迫害。即使我们过去多次辜负祂，仍然对我们怀有盼望的，也是祂。

祂是我们继续前行的原因。祂是我们怀有盼望的原因，不仅为自己，也为我们的弟兄。

The urgency of the last minute is something that many homemakers deal with regularly. No matter how organized we are, sometimes we put off tasks because we dislike them or wait until we are under pressure.

Habitual procrastination potentially leads to higher levels of stress. Maybe I’m odd, but it is hard for me to stay calm and collected when the pressure is mounting. By the time the last minute things are completed I’m too exhausted to enjoy the planned event.

Toothaches and Road Trips

It is a mystery to me why a family member ends up in a dentist chair a day or two before we leave on a trip. Maybe it hasn’t happened as often as I think, but the frustration of an unplanned trip to the dentist at an inopportune time is riveted in my mind. Now I schedule an imaginary appointment before a trip. If it is not a dental emergency, some other issue is bound to fill that time slot.

Deadlines are a normal part of life. Without them we would be unmotivated, and our days would lack purpose. Interruptions are also a normal part of life. They constantly give an unpredictable twist to our days and weeks. If we let too many tasks wait until the last minute, interruptions and deadlines collide, and chaos reigns.

Change the Last-Minute Scenario

Deadlines and interruptions cannot be eliminated but we can limit last-minute tasks. Sometimes it takes some honest looking back to figure out what caused our stress. Often, we blame it on interruptions and fail to realize that poor planning or procrastination might have been the culprit.

For example, if guests are coming and we plan to wash windows and make a dessert along with a dozen more tasks on the day of their arrival, there is no room for disruptions. From experience, we know interruptions will come. So, isn’t it better to “plan” for a bee sting and a stubbed toe?

Why not schedule window washing and dessert another day? That might mean some fingerprints on the windows and a simpler dessert, but isn’t that better than a great deal of stress at the last minute?

Do some tasks ahead of time

Deciding early in the day what to make for supper and packing the diaper bag in advance are little things that can make a big difference at the last minute. When our children were young, I started packing suitcases a day before a trip versus the day of leaving. I was better able to cope with the last-minute rush if that job was out of the way.

Do the most important tasks first

This approach gives freedom to skip jobs of lesser importance when up against a time crunch.

Sometimes not everything on the task list is of equal value. Dropping a task is difficult for a perfectionist, but it is possible to develop new habits.

Break work into smaller bits

Sometimes the enormity of a task makes it seem too huge to start. Break down the large task into smaller components. Completing a smaller task is much more manageable. Deep cleaning my kitchen is a task that I do not enjoy. If my planner says, “deep-clean kitchen,” it’s easy to ignore.

But if my planner says, “clean appliances, wipe out cupboards, and wash windows,” it seems more doable.

There are so many joyful events in life; why be hassled by procrastination? Give yourself the liberty to live life differently. A few minor changes can make the biggest difference between a blessed or stressed last minute.

A urgência do último minuto é algo com que muitas donas de casa lidam regularmente. Não importa o quão organizadas sejamos, às vezes adiamos tarefas porque não gostamos delas ou esperamos até estarmos sob pressão.

A procrastinação habitual pode levar a níveis mais altos de estresse. Talvez eu seja estranha, mas é difícil para mim manter a calma e a compostura quando a pressão aumenta. Quando as coisas de última hora são finalmente concluídas, estou exausta demais para aproveitar o evento planejado.

Dores de dente e viagens de carro

É um mistério para mim por que um membro da família acaba na cadeira do dentista um dia ou dois antes de partirmos em uma viagem. Talvez não tenha acontecido com a frequência que penso, mas a frustração de uma visita ao dentista não planejada em um momento inoportuno está gravada na minha memória. Agora eu marco um compromisso imaginário antes de uma viagem. Se não for uma emergência dentária, algum outro problema provavelmente ocupará aquela vaga de horário.

Prazos são uma parte normal da vida. Sem eles ficaríamos desmotivados e nossos dias careceriam de propósito. Interrupções também são uma parte normal da vida. Elas constantemente dão uma reviravolta imprevisível aos nossos dias e semanas. Se deixarmos muitas tarefas para o último minuto, interrupções e prazos colidem, e o caos reina.

Mude o cenário do último minuto

Prazos e interrupções não podem ser eliminados, mas podemos limitar as tarefas de última hora. Às vezes é preciso olhar honestamente para trás para descobrir o que causou nosso estresse. Muitas vezes culpamos as interrupções e não percebemos que um planejamento deficiente ou a procrastinação podem ter sido os culpados.

Por exemplo, se visitas vão chegar e planejamos lavar janelas e fazer uma sobremesa junto com uma dúzia de outras tarefas no dia da chegada, não haverá espaço para imprevistos. Pela experiência, sabemos que as interrupções virão. Então, não é melhor “planejar” uma picada de abelha e um dedo do pé machucado?

Por que não agendar a lavagem das janelas e a sobremesa para outro dia? Isso pode significar algumas impressões digitais nas janelas e uma sobremesa mais simples, mas isso não é melhor do que muito estresse no último minuto?

Faça algumas tarefas com antecedência

Decidir no início do dia o que preparar para o jantar e arrumar a bolsa de fraldas com antecedência são pequenas coisas que podem fazer uma grande diferença no último minuto. Quando nossos filhos eram pequenos, eu comecei a fazer as malas um dia antes da viagem em vez de deixá-las para o dia da partida. Eu conseguia lidar melhor com a correria de última hora se essa tarefa já estivesse resolvida.

Faça primeiro as tarefas mais importantes

Esse método dá liberdade para pular trabalhos de menor importância quando estamos pressionados pelo tempo.

Às vezes nem tudo na lista de tarefas tem igual valor. Abandonar uma tarefa é difícil para uma perfeccionista, mas é possível desenvolver novos hábitos.

Divida o trabalho em partes menores

Às vezes a enormidade de uma tarefa faz com que pareça grande demais para começar. Divida a grande tarefa em componentes menores. Concluir uma tarefa menor é muito mais administrável. Fazer uma limpeza profunda na minha cozinha é uma tarefa que eu não gosto de fazer. Se meu planejador diz “limpeza profunda da cozinha”, é fácil ignorar.

Mas se meu planejador diz “limpar os eletrodomésticos, limpar os armários e lavar as janelas”, parece mais realizável.

Há tantos eventos alegres na vida; por que se incomodar com a procrastinação? Dê a si mesma a liberdade de viver de forma diferente. Algumas pequenas mudanças podem fazer a maior diferença entre um último minuto abençoado ou estressante.
