אני עדיין מריח את התערובת המפתה של ריחות כשאחזתי בידו החזקה של אבי, שוזר את דרכנו בין המוני התיירים שצפפו בבניין. הסוחרים בשוק האיכרים גרין דרגון באפרטה שבפנסילבניה עשו את מיטב מאמציהם לפתות קונים בשורות של דגים טריים על קרח, גבינות מכל הסוגים, סלמי וסנדוויצ’ים, וערימות של פירות טריים. ואוי, הממתקים! מוחי הצעיר לפני בית־הספר לא ראה מעולם כל כך הרבה ממתקים טעימים במקום אחד ובאותו זמן.

שני הימים האחרונים עבורי היו כמו הילד בחנות הממתקים. הייתה לי הזכות להשתתף בכנס הכותבים השנתי הראשון של Christian Aid Ministries. נגעתי בכתפיהם של מחברים ידועים כגון Katrina Hoover Lee, Johnny Miller ו-Ruthann Stelfox. שוחחתי עם כותבים שואפים ומורים ותיקים. הייתה לי ההזדמנות לשבת תחת שעות של סדנאות מעוררות השראה וחינוכיות על איך לכתוב כדי לתקשר, שימוש בדיאלוג מציאותי, כתיבה תיאורית, ועוד. היה לנו יעד משותף. יחד, אנו משתפים ולומדים איך לתקשר ביעילות את מה שבלבנו, ובאמצעות כוח המילה הכתובה להעביר את אותם המחשבות אל לבבכם.

The Heartbeat of the Remnant הוא אמצעי לתקשר מחשבות מעוררות השראה לקוראים צמאים הפזורים ברחבי העולם. כותבים אמיצים עולים עם עט ונייר או מקלדת ומסך ועוזרים להפיץ את הבשורה הטובה של דבר־אלוהים בזהירות, בתיקון ובעידוד רוחני. ועדיין, אנו זקוקים לעוד כותבים כאלה. אנו זקוקים למאמינים צעירים שמגישים באומץ את סיפוריהם הראשונים לילדים. סבים מנוסים שמביאים דברי מוסר לדור הצעיר. לאמהות שמשתפות חוויות וניסיונות עם אמהות אחרות השוקעות בגידול הקטנים. לנוער המעודד נוער לחתור אל המטרה של פרס הקריאה הנשגב במשיח ישוע. לאבות שמתבוננים בדאגה בעולמנו הלוחץ על בתי־נוצרי. יחד, כותבים שואפים אלה יפיקו תקופתון שיישאר על שולחן הקפה המשפחתי לשנים רבות. אני מעודד אתכם, חברים מאמינים, לנסות. נלסון מנדלה, נשיא דרום־אפריקה לשעבר, כתב: “Failure is a teacher, and at the end of your life, what do you think you’ll feel worst about, failing or never trying?”

מטרת The Berean Voice היא לספק חומר מודפס שיעזור לקוראים לנווט בעונות החיים המשתנות והקשות. כל החומר שלנו זמין ללא תשלום, אך אנו תלויים בתרומות מתומכינו. להלן רשימת ספרים שיש לנו:

The Power of the Love of Truth
Christian Counseling- Counterfeit?
The Heart of God
Free Indeed!
Pilgrims and Politics
Cup & Cross
The High Cost of Holistic Healing
Secrets of Successful Writing
The Catholic Connection
Psychiatry and Mood altering Medications
The Mennonite Church and Modernism

ב־2017 ו־2018, The Berean Voice פרסמה סדרת מאמרים על חיסונים במגזין The Heartbeat of the Remnant. מאמרים אלה היו מאמץ כן לבחון היבטים שונים של שימוש בחיסונים בגישה בלתי מוטה. ניסינו להציג את העובדות באופן הברור ביותר ולאפשר לקוראים להסיק את מסקנותיהם בעצמם.

מאז קיבלנו בקשות רבות מהקוראים שלנו לפרסם את כל מאמרי החיסונים בספרון, מה שראינו לנכון לעשות. אך אז הגיע 2019, והביא עמו את נגיף הקורונה. אירוע ענק זה התהפך על דיון החיסונים והניע מהלך קדחתני להשקת תרופות ל־COVID-19, רבות מהן שלא נבדקו כראוי. השהינו את ההדפסה, לא בטוחים אם לכלול מידע על “חיסוני” COVID-19 החדשים והלא־מוכחים האלה. עם חלוף הזמן ודעיכתו של אופיו הקטלני של COVID-19, החלטנו לפרסם את מאמרי החיסונים המקוריים בספרון ללא מאמרים נוספים על המחלוקת סביב COVID-19. אנו שמחים שהפרויקט מתקרב להשלמה ויוכרז עם הוצאתו.

ברכות לכולכם,

Edward Martin

“Dr. Waldron, Elsie needs help!” Elsie’s husband was adamant, almost angry, as he stared at me. On the other hand, Elsie stared at the floor, almost as though she wasn’t present. I had never met either of the couple before and was struggling just a little to figure out what was needed from me to help her.

“What is going on?” I asked as I flipped through her chart. This was still in the days of paper charts, and I headed to the lab section of her chart. There wasn’t anything too crazy that I could see there—her liver enzymes were a little elevated, but otherwise, everything seemed OK.

“It’s her drinking!” Her husband told me. “She is drinking more and more every night. She won’t go out except to get whiskey. She drinks till she passes out every night and has to have something every morning to get her started.”

“Is that true?” I asked Elsie, feeling like a judge overseeing a jury trial.

“Yes,” she said. Her face was emotionless, and I couldn’t tell if she wanted to be there or not.

“Do you want help?” I asked her. This was a loaded question. Many people who struggle with alcoholism aren’t ready to break free from its vice-like hold on them. Maybe Elsie was different.

“I guess so,” she said, indifferently. Once again, I couldn’t tell whether she wanted to be there or not.

“At the rate at which you are drinking, you will kill yourself within a year – maybe two at best – if you don’t give up alcohol entirely,” I told her. “If you want to, I will try to find you an inpatient program to detox you and get you off of alcohol.”

“She’s ready,” he husband said firmly.

When dealing with someone who drinks heavily, it is crucial that they don’t simply stop drinking without medical support. Abrupt cessation of alcohol use causes the body to go into withdrawal which can produce a state called Delirium Tremens and even seizures.

I stepped out of the exam room and to make phone calls. It is never easy to find a place for someone to attempt to rehabilitate from any kind of substances, and it was over an hour and a half before I found a facility that was willing to take Elsie and try to help her get off of the whiskey.

I sighed as I reentered her exam room. I had been afraid that I wouldn’t find anywhere for her to go.

I told them about the plan, and her husband nodded vigorously, while Elise continued to stare silently at the floor. “Can we pray together before you go?” I asked them, and when they nodded assent, I prayed with them, asking for freedom and Jesus’ presence in both of their lives.

They left my office with marching orders and directions on where to go. I had a happy glow about me for the rest of the morning, knowing that I had gone the extra mile and had really made a difference in this middle-aged couple’s life.

Around 2 pm, I got a call from the rehab facility. They hadn’t seen even a shadow of Elsie or her husband, which was surprising, since it was a bright sunny day and the facility wasn’t that far away. With a sinking feeling, I dialed the couple’s phone number.

“She won’t go!” Her husband told me. “She tells me that she told me this ahead of time. She’ll try to cut back, but she isn’t willing to go into a rehab facility or any such thing. I guess just tell them that we’ll let them know if she changes her mind.”

My nurse called the rehab facility and told them the bad news, and I sat down in my chair, stunned. What else could I have done? Was there a solution for Elsie—something different that I could have said that would have made a difference in her life?

About a year later, I received the sad news that Elsie had died at home. I was certain that things would have been different if she had gone to rehab and if she had given control to Jesus. None of that had happened, and I felt cynicism pushing into my heart.

Cynicism

We live in an age of cynicism. In ancient Greece, the cynics were an odd assortment of men who specialized in being grouchy and saying mean (they would have said truthful) things to people. They often dressed in rags and behaved in such a way that most of the polite Athenians did not want to be close to them.

Today, cynicism means a tendency to believe the worst about people and circumstances. Cynical people believe that all people are motivated purely by selfishness and that bad events will tend to prevail.

Many young doctors are idealistic and very hopeful. They believe that if they exert the utmost effort, they can make a real, positive impact on their patient’s lives. Unfortunately, as time goes by and they try their hardest and their patients don’t change, they can give up. These doctors still try, but they no longer really hope that their efforts will make much of a difference.

It seems as though people who get involved with politics often have the best of intentions. They see this as a path to changing society for the better. Unfortunately, as time goes by and the faces in charge change, the policies don’t really change, they tend to become cynical.

Sometimes this cynicism is directed against all politicians. Sometimes it is only anger directed against members of the party that opposes their party’s positions. Hope is replaced by cynicism.

Cynicism in the Bible

If there is a book in the Bible that seems to have been written by a cynical man, it is the book of Ecclesiastes. The Preacher, who we understand to be Solomon, lists all of the things that he endeavored in an attempt to find joy.

In chapter 2:17-23 Solomon describes work as futile. He finishes by saying, “For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun? For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.” (Ecclesiastes 2:22,23)

He saw the world as being dominated by tyrants and there was little that the people could do about it. Solomon went so far as to say that political power was meaningless “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor” (Ecclesiastes 4:13).

In Ecclesiastes 6:6, he seems to disparage long life. “Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?”

Of course, he finishes his short book with the instruction to remember our Creator in the days of our youth. There is a blessing for those who choose to focus on God when they have a little bit of energy left and not, when they are old and jaded, like Solomon.

Later on, it almost seemed as though God had given up on His people. He still sent prophets to them, but He knew without a doubt that the people would refuse to respond. “Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee” (Jeremiah 7:27).

Even in the New Testament, Paul told Timothy that the time was coming when people would no longer listen to sound doctrine. “For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;” (2 Timothy 4:3).

By picking and choosing these passages, we can come away with a very gloomy view of the future and, more specifically, of human’s willingness to change. It seems there is little point of investing ourselves in the people around us. They are full of woe and are as likely to change as a chipmunk is to master differential calculus.

The Opposite of Cynicism

The opposite of cynicism is hope. It is the belief that the future could be better.

It is interesting that the Apostle Paul spoke of tribulations in the Epistle to the Romans, “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us” (Romans 5:3-5).

We may not have reached the place where we glory in the trials we experience, but certainly, they should bring us these other things that he mentions. For, we grow in patience and experience, even as we deal with trials, but more than that, we come to realize that we have hope for tomorrow because we serve a great God.

The contrast in the story of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15 teaches us much about hope. The father and the older brother were strikingly different in their attitudes.

The father had never given up hope – he knew that his son had failed him and gone far from what he knew was right and yet, the father still desired to see the prodigal come to himself and return home.

On the other hand, the older brother not only had no hope for his younger brother, but he was also angry with him. The prodigal had wasted his money, he had lived in sin, and now, he had returned home just because he was out of money.

Certainly, there was no reason to trust the younger son. Yet, that is exactly what our Heavenly Father does for us.

Look for Hope in the Right Places

Part of the problem is that we look for hope in the wrong places. A number of years ago, a presidential candidate ran for office under the slogan “Hope and Change,” and yet, even though he was elected, I imagine most folks did not feel that their lives were significantly changed for the better.

Pursuing the things this world values—political power and wealth is guaranteed to bring emptiness. This is Satan’s pattern—he always over-promises and under-delivers.

This was what he did when he tempted Jesus, “All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:8). All of the things Satan offered, nothing compared with the glory that Jesus eventually received from the road that led to the cross.

In the same way, Satan would like to distract Christians from seeking the things that are valuable, and that will bring hope. Satan tells Christians that politics will not only change the world for the better, it is an easier way to change the world.

The Bible is clear that we build hope as we nurture our relationship with God and then work to help our brothers and sisters build that same relationship in their own lives. The reason that we can hope is not because people are so wonderful—we don’t have to live very long to realize that they aren’t. The reason we hope is because we serve an awesome, faithful God who walks with us through the worst of our trials.

Remember that We Have Undeserved Hope

Jesus’ messages about forgiveness make it clear that one of the major reasons that we have for forgiving others in our lives is that we have received great and undeserved forgiveness. The same is true for hope.

Each one of us was hopeless and without reason to expect to receive hope and we were still given a ray of light in the midst of our darkness. Maybe part of the reason that we have so much trouble hoping for good things for the people around us is that we do not remember how hopeless we were before we found grace.

If Jesus was able to bring hope to our hopeless existence, then certainly He can do wonderful things in the hearts and lives of others around us. The only people we should give up on are the ones that our Savior has given up on as well.

Small Efforts Do Make a Difference

I remember having a conversation with a young person who was planning to go into medicine and had a plan to go to a foreign country and serve the people there. As we were talking, an older man entered the conversation and shared that he saw little hope for change in developing countries.

The people in those countries just weren’t interested in getting better and didn’t do the minimum necessary to stave off things like worms and parasites. Doctors and nurses couldn’t make a difference in such an environment.

I could sense the heart of the youth sinking as this older man shared. He had experience, and he had given up hope. The sad thing was that he was also stealing the hope of someone who still had a desire to serve.

When I was in training, I had a surgeon tell me that family doctors didn’t really do anything. They simply kept their patients alive till their next office visit, whereas surgeons really “fixed” people—taking out (or off) the offending body part.

At the end of the day, small efforts do make a difference. I don’t do brain surgery, but I still can make a difference in someone else’s life— maybe just by spending a little time and listening and praying. This is true for all of us.

More than that, we come to realize that making this effort changes our own lives for the better. Jesus told the sheep that as they ministered to “the least of these my brethren,” they were ministering to Him.

Even if no one’s life is improved, our Savior knows our desires and feels our efforts, and will reward them someday.

A Few Things to Remember

When we face failures, we tend to move in one of two directions. Those of us who are optimists tend to believe that this episode was an isolated event and that the future is still bright. On the other hand, pessimists believe that failures are permanent, personal, and pervasive.

Pessimists believe that their failures are the result of intrinsic character flaws that they have and that these things affect all of their lives and are unlikely to change. Unlike the righteous man who falls to rise again, these people fall and lie where they fall, defeated at the outset.

When we are dealing with other people, we need to give them the same grace that we should give ourselves. They, too, are growing, and if they have a failure today, they will do better tomorrow. Maybe they will fail again, but they will at least “fail better.”

Conclusion

Cynicism is rife in our world. Many have given up hope for a better future, and it is understandable for those who have invested their hope in this world’s institutions. There is no real hope in government or in armies or in bureaucracy.

The song says, “Oh to have no hope in Jesus, how dark this world must be!” For, Jesus is the one who brings light into our darkness and allows us to continue, even when others fail us.

God is the one who redeems us. He is the one who sent the prophets, even though their messages were ignored, and the prophets were persecuted. He is the one who continues to hope for us, even when we have failed Him so many times in the past.

He is the reason we carry on. He is the reason that we have hope, not only for ourselves but also for our brothers.

“Dr. Waldron, a Elsie precisa de ajuda!” O marido de Elsie estava categórico, quase zangado, enquanto me fitava. Por outro lado, Elsie olhava para o chão, quase como se não estivesse presente. Eu nunca havia conhecido nenhum dos dois antes e estava um pouco perdido tentando descobrir o que era necessário da minha parte para ajudá-la.

“O que está acontecendo?” perguntei enquanto folheava seu prontuário. Ainda eram os dias dos prontuários em papel e fui para a seção de exames laboratoriais do seu prontuário. Não havia nada muito estranho ali — suas enzimas hepáticas estavam um pouco elevadas, mas fora isso, tudo parecia OK.

“É por causa da bebida!” disse o marido. “Ela está bebendo cada vez mais todas as noites. Ela não sai, exceto para comprar uísque. Bebe até desmaiar todas as noites e precisa de algo toda manhã para começar o dia.”

“Isso é verdade?” perguntei a Elsie, sentindo-me como um juiz diante de um júri.

“Sim,” ela disse. Seu rosto estava sem expressão, e eu não conseguia dizer se ela queria estar ali ou não.

“Você quer ajuda?” perguntei. Era uma pergunta carregada. Muitas pessoas que lutam contra o alcoolismo não estão prontas para se libertar de seu aperto. Talvez Elsie fosse diferente.

“Acho que sim,” disse ela, indiferente. Mais uma vez, eu não podia dizer se ela queria estar ali ou não.

“No ritmo em que você está bebendo, vai se matar em um ano — talvez dois no máximo — se não abandonar o álcool inteiramente,” disse eu. “Se quiser, vou tentar encontrar um programa de internação para desintoxicá-la e tirá-la do álcool.”

“Ela está pronta,” disse o marido com firmeza.

Ao lidar com alguém que bebe em excesso, é crucial que a pessoa não pare de beber abruptamente sem suporte médico. A cessação abrupta do uso de álcool faz com que o corpo entre em abstinência, o que pode produzir um estado chamado Delírio Tremens e até convulsões.

Saí da sala de exames para fazer telefonemas. Nunca é fácil encontrar um lugar para alguém tentar se reabilitar de qualquer tipo de substância, e levou mais de uma hora e meia até eu encontrar uma instituição disposta a aceitar Elsie e tentar ajudá-la a largar o uísque.

Suspirei ao reentrar na sala de exames. Tinha receado não encontrar lugar para ela.

Expliquei o plano a eles, e o marido assentiu vigorosamente, enquanto Elsie continuava a olhar silenciosamente para o chão. “Podemos orar juntos antes de você ir?” perguntei, e quando eles assentiram, orei com eles, pedindo libertação e a presença de Jesus na vida de ambos.

Saíram do meu consultório com ordens claras e direções de onde ir. Tive um brilho de satisfação pelo resto da manhã, sabendo que me esforcei além do necessário e realmente fiz diferença na vida desse casal de meia-idade.

Perto das 14h, recebi uma ligação do centro de reabilitação. Eles não tinham visto nem a sombra de Elsie ou de seu marido, o que foi surpreendente, já que fazia um dia claro e ensolarado e a instituição não ficava tão longe. Com um sentimento de aperto no estômago, disquei o número do casal.

“Ela não vai!” disse o marido. “Ela me diz que me avisou disso antes. Vai tentar reduzir, mas não está disposta a entrar em uma clínica de reabilitação nem nada do tipo. Acho que diga a eles que avisaremos se ela mudar de ideia.”

Minha enfermeira ligou para o centro de reabilitação e deu a má notícia, e eu me sentei na cadeira, atônito. O que mais poderia eu ter feito? Havia alguma solução para Elsie — algo diferente que eu poderia ter dito que teria feito diferença em sua vida?

Cerca de um ano depois, recebi a triste notícia de que Elsie havia morrido em casa. Eu tinha certeza de que as coisas teriam sido diferentes se ela tivesse ido para a reabilitação e se tivesse entregue o controle a Jesus. Nada daquilo aconteceu, e senti o cinismo invadindo meu coração.

Cinismo

Vivemos numa era de cinismo. Na Grécia antiga, os cínicos eram um grupo estranho de homens que se especializavam em ser mal-humorados e dizer coisas duras (eles diriam verdadeiras) às pessoas. Frequentemente vestiam farrapos e se comportavam de modo que a maioria dos atenienses polidos não queria estar próxima deles.

Hoje, cinismo significa uma tendência a acreditar no pior sobre pessoas e circunstâncias. Pessoas cínicas creem que todos são movidos puramente por egoísmo e que eventos ruins tendem a prevalecer.

Muitos médicos jovens são idealistas e muito esperançosos. Acreditam que, se se esforçarem ao máximo, podem causar um impacto real e positivo na vida de seus pacientes. Infelizmente, com o passar do tempo, quando se esforçam e seus pacientes não mudam, podem desistir. Esses médicos ainda tentam, mas já não realmente esperam que seus esforços façam muita diferença.

Parece que pessoas envolvidas com política frequentemente têm as melhores intenções. Veem isso como um caminho para mudar a sociedade para melhor. Infelizmente, com o passar do tempo e as mudanças nas lideranças, as políticas não mudam verdadeiramente, e eles tendem a tornar-se cínicos.

Por vezes esse cinismo é dirigido contra todos os políticos. Outras vezes é apenas raiva voltada contra os membros do partido que se opõem às posições do seu próprio partido. A esperança é substituída pelo cinismo.

Cinismo na Bíblia

Se há um livro na Bíblia que parece ter sido escrito por um homem cínico, é o livro de Eclesiastes. O Pregador, que entendemos ser Salomão, enumera todas as coisas em que empenhou-se na tentativa de encontrar alegria.

No capítulo 2:17-23 Salomão descreve o trabalho como fútil. Termina dizendo: “For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun? For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.” (Ecclesiastes 2:22,23)

Ele via o mundo dominado por tiranos e pouco havia que o povo pudesse fazer a respeito. Salomão chegou a dizer que o poder político era sem sentido: “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor” (Ecclesiastes 4:13).

Em Eclesiastes 6:6, ele parece menosprezar a vida longa. “Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?”

Claro, ele termina seu breve livro com a instrução de lembrar do nosso Criador nos dias da nossa juventude. Há uma bênção para aqueles que escolhem focar em Deus quando ainda têm um pouco de energia, e não quando estiverem velhos e desgastados, como Salomão.

Mais adiante, pareceu quase que Deus havia desistido de Seu povo. Ele ainda enviava profetas a eles, mas sabia sem dúvida que o povo recusaria responder. “Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee” (Jeremiah 7:27).

Mesmo no Novo Testamento, Paulo disse a Timóteo que viria tempo em que as pessoas não mais ouviriam a sã doutrina. “For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;” (2 Timothy 4:3).

Ao escolher e selecionar essas passagens, podemos ficar com uma visão muito lúgubre do futuro e, mais especificamente, da disposição humana para mudar. Parece haver pouco sentido em investir-nos nas pessoas ao nosso redor. Elas estão cheias de aflição e são tão propensas a mudar quanto um esquilo a dominar cálculo diferencial.

O Oposto do Cinismo

O oposto do cinismo é a esperança. É a crença de que o futuro pode ser melhor.

É interessante que o apóstolo Paulo falou sobre tribulações na Epístola aos Romanos: “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us” (Romans 5:3-5).

Talvez não tenhamos chegado ao ponto de nos gloriarmos nas provações que vivenciamos, mas certamente elas deveriam nos trazer as outras coisas que ele menciona. Pois crescemos em paciência e experiência enquanto lidamos com as provações, e mais que isso, percebemos que temos esperança para o amanhã porque servimos a um grande Deus.

O contraste na história do Filho Pródigo em Lucas 15 nos ensina muito sobre esperança. O pai e o irmão mais velho eram notavelmente diferentes em suas atitudes.

O pai nunca havia perdido a esperança — sabia que seu filho o havia desonrado e se afastado do que sabia ser o certo e, ainda assim, o pai desejava ver o pródigo voltar a si e regressar para casa.

Por outro lado, o irmão mais velho não só não tinha esperança para com o irmão mais novo, como também estava irado com ele. O pródigo havia desperdiçado seu dinheiro, vivido em pecado e agora voltara para casa apenas porque estava sem recursos.

Certamente não havia razão para confiar no filho mais novo. Ainda assim, isso é exatamente o que nosso Pai Celeste faz por nós.

Procure Esperança nos Lugares Certos

Parte do problema é que procuramos esperança nos lugares errados. Anos atrás, um candidato presidencial concorreu com o slogan “Hope and Change”, e apesar de ter sido eleito, imagino que a maioria das pessoas não sentiu que suas vidas mudaram significativamente para melhor.

Buscar as coisas que este mundo valoriza — poder político e riqueza — é garantia de trazer vazio. Este é o padrão de Satanás — ele sempre promete demais e cumpre de menos.

Foi isso que ele tentou com Jesus: “All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:8). Tudo o que Satanás ofereceu, nada se compara à glória que Jesus recebeu ao seguir o caminho que levou à cruz.

Da mesma forma, Satanás gostaria de distrair os cristãos de buscar as coisas que são valiosas e que trarão esperança. Satanás diz aos cristãos que a política não só mudará o mundo para melhor, como é um caminho mais fácil para mudar o mundo.

A Bíblia é clara que construímos esperança ao nutrir nosso relacionamento com Deus e, depois, trabalhar para ajudar nossos irmãos e irmãs a edificarem esse mesmo relacionamento em suas vidas. A razão pela qual podemos ter esperança não é porque as pessoas sejam maravilhosas — não precisamos viver muito para perceber que não são. A razão pela qual esperamos é porque servimos a um Deus tremendo e fiel que caminha conosco através das piores provações.

Lembre-se de que Temos Esperança Imerecida

As mensagens de Jesus sobre perdão deixam claro que uma das principais razões para perdoarmos os outros em nossas vidas é que nós mesmos recebemos grande e imerecido perdão. O mesmo vale para a esperança.

Cada um de nós era sem esperança e sem razão para esperar receber esperança, e ainda assim nos foi dada uma réstia de luz em meio à nossa escuridão. Talvez parte da razão pela qual temos tanta dificuldade em esperar coisas boas para as pessoas ao nosso redor seja que não lembramos o quão desesperados éramos antes de encontrarmos a graça.

Se Jesus pôde trazer esperança à nossa existência sem esperança, certamente Ele pode fazer coisas maravilhosas nos corações e nas vidas de outros ao nosso redor. As únicas pessoas de que deveríamos desistir são aquelas de quem nosso Salvador também desistiu.

Pequenos Esforços Fazem Diferença

Lembro-me de uma conversa com um jovem que planejava entrar na medicina e tinha um projeto de ir a um país estrangeiro para servir o povo lá. Enquanto conversávamos, um homem mais velho entrou no diálogo e compartilhou que via pouca esperança de mudança em países em desenvolvimento.

As pessoas nesses países simplesmente não estavam interessadas em melhorar e não faziam o mínimo necessário para evitar problemas como vermes e parasitas. Médicos e enfermeiros não podiam fazer diferença num ambiente assim.

Percebi o ânimo do jovem murchando enquanto o homem mais velho falava. Ele tinha experiência e havia perdido a esperança. O triste é que também roubava a esperança de alguém que ainda desejava servir.

Quando eu estava em treinamento, um cirurgião me disse que os médicos de família não faziam muita coisa. Eles simplesmente mantinham seus pacientes vivos até a próxima consulta, enquanto os cirurgiões realmente “consertavam” as pessoas — removendo a parte ofensora do corpo.

No fim das contas, pequenos esforços fazem diferença. Eu não faço neurocirurgia, mas ainda posso impactar a vida de alguém — talvez apenas passando um tempo para ouvir e orar. Isso vale para todos nós.

Além disso, percebemos que fazer esse esforço muda nossas próprias vidas para melhor. Jesus disse às ovelhas que, ao ministrarem “the least of these my brethren,” estavam ministrando a Ele.

Mesmo que a vida de ninguém melhore, nosso Salvador conhece nossos desejos, sente nossos esforços e os recompensará algum dia.

Algumas Coisas para Lembrar

Quando enfrentamos fracassos, tendemos a seguir uma de duas direções. Aqueles de nós que são otimistas tendem a acreditar que o episódio foi isolado e que o futuro ainda é promissor. Por outro lado, os pessimistas acreditam que os fracassos são permanentes, pessoais e abrangentes.

Os pessimistas crêem que seus fracassos resultam de defeitos intrínsecos de caráter que possuem e que essas coisas afetam toda a sua vida e são improváveis de mudar. Ao contrário do homem justo que cai para se levantar novamente, essas pessoas caem e ficam onde caíram, derrotadas desde o início.

Ao lidarmos com outras pessoas, precisamos dar a elas a mesma graça que deveríamos dar a nós mesmos. Elas também estão crescendo e, se falham hoje, farão melhor amanhã. Talvez falhem novamente, mas ao menos “falharão melhor.”

Conclusão

O cinismo está entranhado em nosso mundo. Muitos desistiram da esperança de um futuro melhor, e isso é compreensível para aqueles que investiram sua esperança nas instituições deste mundo. Não há esperança real no governo, nos exércitos ou na burocracia.

A canção diz: “Oh to have no hope in Jesus, how dark this world must be!” Pois Jesus é quem traz luz à nossa escuridão e nos permite prosseguir, mesmo quando outros nos desapontam.

Deus é quem nos redime. Ele é quem enviou os profetas, mesmo que suas mensagens fossem ignoradas e os profetas perseguidos. Ele é quem continua a ter esperança por nós, mesmo quando O temos desapontado tantas vezes no passado.

Ele é a razão pela qual seguimos adiante. Ele é a razão pela qual temos esperança, não apenas para nós mesmos, mas também para nossos irmãos.

The urgency of the last minute is something that many homemakers deal with regularly. No matter how organized we are, sometimes we put off tasks because we dislike them or wait until we are under pressure.

Habitual procrastination potentially leads to higher levels of stress. Maybe I’m odd, but it is hard for me to stay calm and collected when the pressure is mounting. By the time the last minute things are completed I’m too exhausted to enjoy the planned event.

Toothaches and Road Trips

It is a mystery to me why a family member ends up in a dentist chair a day or two before we leave on a trip. Maybe it hasn’t happened as often as I think, but the frustration of an unplanned trip to the dentist at an inopportune time is riveted in my mind. Now I schedule an imaginary appointment before a trip. If it is not a dental emergency, some other issue is bound to fill that time slot.

Deadlines are a normal part of life. Without them we would be unmotivated, and our days would lack purpose. Interruptions are also a normal part of life. They constantly give an unpredictable twist to our days and weeks. If we let too many tasks wait until the last minute, interruptions and deadlines collide, and chaos reigns.

Change the Last-Minute Scenario

Deadlines and interruptions cannot be eliminated but we can limit last-minute tasks. Sometimes it takes some honest looking back to figure out what caused our stress. Often, we blame it on interruptions and fail to realize that poor planning or procrastination might have been the culprit.

For example, if guests are coming and we plan to wash windows and make a dessert along with a dozen more tasks on the day of their arrival, there is no room for disruptions. From experience, we know interruptions will come. So, isn’t it better to “plan” for a bee sting and a stubbed toe?

Why not schedule window washing and dessert another day? That might mean some fingerprints on the windows and a simpler dessert, but isn’t that better than a great deal of stress at the last minute?

Do some tasks ahead of time

Deciding early in the day what to make for supper and packing the diaper bag in advance are little things that can make a big difference at the last minute. When our children were young, I started packing suitcases a day before a trip versus the day of leaving. I was better able to cope with the last-minute rush if that job was out of the way.

Do the most important tasks first

This approach gives freedom to skip jobs of lesser importance when up against a time crunch.

Sometimes not everything on the task list is of equal value. Dropping a task is difficult for a perfectionist, but it is possible to develop new habits.

Break work into smaller bits

Sometimes the enormity of a task makes it seem too huge to start. Break down the large task into smaller components. Completing a smaller task is much more manageable. Deep cleaning my kitchen is a task that I do not enjoy. If my planner says, “deep-clean kitchen,” it’s easy to ignore.

But if my planner says, “clean appliances, wipe out cupboards, and wash windows,” it seems more doable.

There are so many joyful events in life; why be hassled by procrastination? Give yourself the liberty to live life differently. A few minor changes can make the biggest difference between a blessed or stressed last minute.

L'urgence de la dernière minute est une réalité à laquelle de nombreuses femmes au foyer sont régulièrement confrontées. Peu importe notre organisation, il nous arrive parfois de remettre des tâches à plus tard parce qu'elles nous déplaisent ou parce que nous attendons d'être sous pression.

La procrastination habituelle peut entraîner des niveaux de stress plus élevés. Peut-être que je suis étrange, mais il m'est difficile de rester calme et posée quand la pression monte. Quand les choses de dernière minute sont enfin accomplies, je suis trop épuisée pour profiter de l'événement prévu.

Dents qui font mal et voyages en voiture

Je ne comprends pas pourquoi un membre de la famille finit par se retrouver sur le fauteuil du dentiste un jour ou deux avant notre départ en voyage. Peut-être que cela n'arrive pas aussi souvent que je le pense, mais la frustration d'un rendez-vous imprévu chez le dentiste à un moment inopportun est gravée dans ma mémoire. À présent, je planifie mentalement un rendez-vous imaginaire avant un voyage. Si ce n'est pas une urgence dentaire, un autre problème est sûr de remplir ce créneau.

Les échéances font partie normale de la vie. Sans elles, nous manquerions de motivation et nos journées n'auraient pas de but. Les interruptions sont aussi une partie normale de la vie. Elles donnent constamment une tournure imprévisible à nos journées et semaines. Si nous laissons trop de tâches en attente jusqu'à la dernière minute, interruptions et échéances se heurtent, et le chaos s'installe.

Changer le scénario de la dernière minute

On ne peut pas éliminer les échéances et les interruptions, mais nous pouvons limiter les tâches de dernière minute. Parfois, il faut regarder honnêtement en arrière pour comprendre ce qui a causé notre stress. Souvent, nous en attribuons la cause aux interruptions et ne réalisons pas que la mauvaise planification ou la procrastination ont pu être les coupables.

Par exemple, si des invités arrivent et que nous prévoyons de laver les fenêtres et de préparer un dessert, ainsi qu'une douzaine d'autres tâches le jour même de leur arrivée, il n'y a pas de place pour les imprévus. Par expérience, nous savons que des interruptions se produiront. Alors, ne vaut-il pas mieux « prévoir » une piqûre d'abeille et un orteil heurté ?

Pourquoi ne pas programmer le lavage des fenêtres et la préparation du dessert un autre jour ? Cela pourrait signifier quelques empreintes sur les vitres et un dessert plus simple, mais n'est-ce pas préférable à une grande dose de stress à la dernière minute ?

Faites certaines tâches à l'avance

Décider tôt dans la journée de ce que l'on va préparer pour le souper et préparer le sac à couches à l'avance sont de petites choses qui peuvent faire une grande différence à la dernière minute. Quand nos enfants étaient petits, j'ai commencé à faire les valises la veille d'un voyage plutôt que le jour du départ. J'étais mieux à même de faire face à la précipitation de dernière minute si cette tâche était déjà accomplie.

Faites d'abord les tâches les plus importantes

Cette approche donne la liberté de laisser de côté les tâches moins importantes lorsqu'on est pressé par le temps.

Parfois, tout ce qui figure sur la liste des choses à faire n'a pas la même valeur. Abandonner une tâche est difficile pour une personne perfectionniste, mais il est possible de développer de nouvelles habitudes.

Divisez le travail en petites parties

Parfois, l'énormité d'une tâche la rend trop difficile à commencer. Fractionnez la grande tâche en composants plus petits. Accomplir une petite tâche est bien plus gérable. Le nettoyage en profondeur de ma cuisine est une tâche que je n'apprécie pas. Si mon agenda indique « nettoyer en profondeur la cuisine », il est facile de l'ignorer.

Mais si mon agenda dit « nettoyer les appareils, essuyer les placards et laver les fenêtres », cela paraît plus faisable.

Il y a tant d'événements joyeux dans la vie ; pourquoi se laisser importuner par la procrastination ? Donnez-vous la liberté de vivre autrement. Quelques changements mineurs peuvent faire toute la différence entre une dernière minute bénie ou stressante.

I can still smell the tantalizing cacophony of odors as I clutched my father’s strong hand, weaving our way through the masses of tourists that crowded the building. The vendors at the Green Dragon Farmer’s Market in Ephrata, PA, were trying their best to entice buyers with their rows of fresh fish over ice, cheeses of every variety, deli meat and sandwiches, and piles of fresh fruit. And, oh, the candy! My young preschool mind had never seen so many delectable sweets in one place at one time.

The past two days for me were like the boy at the candy store. I had the privilege of attending Christian Aid Ministries’ first Annual Writers’ Conference. I brushed shoulders with well-known authors such as Katrina Hoover Lee, Johnny Miller, and Ruthann Stelfox. I chatted with aspiring writers and seasoned school teachers. I had the opportunity to sit under hours of inspirational and educational workshops on how to write to communicate, using realistic dialog, descriptive writing, and much more. We all had one common goal in mind. Together, we share and learn how to effectively communicate what is in our hearts, and through the power of the written word, transmit those thoughts to your hearts.

The Heartbeat of the Remnant is a means to communicate inspirational thoughts to eager readers scattered across the globe. Courageous writers step forward with pen and paper or keyboard and monitor and help spread the Good News of the Word of God with caution, correction, and edification. Yet, we need more such writers. We need young believers who bravely submit their first children’s stories. Seasoned grandfathers who bring words of admonishment to the younger generation. Mothers who share experiences and trials with other mothers who are in the throes of raising little ones. Youth encouraging fellow youth to press toward the mark of the prize of the high calling in Christ Jesus. Fathers who with a concerned eye watch the world pressing in on the Christian homes. Together, these aspiring writers will produce a periodical that will endure on the family coffee table for many years. I encourage you, fellow believers, to give it a try. Nelson Mandela, former president of South Africa wrote, “Failure is a teacher, and at the end of your life, what do you think you’ll feel worst about, failing or never trying?”

In 2017 and 2018, the Berean Voice printed a series of vaccine articles in The Heartbeat of the Remnant magazine. These articles were a sincere effort to examine various aspects of vaccine usage with an unbiased approach. We attempted to present the facts as clearly as possible and let the readers draw their own conclusions.

Since then, we have received numerous requests from our readers to publish all the vaccine articles in a booklet, which we agreed to do. But then along came 2019, bringing coronavirus with it. This monumental event upended the vaccine debate and ushered in a frenzied rush to market COVID-19 remedies, many of which were not properly tested. We put the printing on hold, unsure whether to include information on these new and unproven COVID-19 “vaccines.” As time progressed and the deadly nature of COVID-19 abated, we decided to publish the original vaccine articles in a booklet without any additional articles on the COVID-19 debate. We are pleased that the project is nearing completion and will be announced when it is released.

Blessings to all,

Edward Martin

Ich kann immer noch die verlockende Kakophonie von Gerüchen riechen, während ich die starke Hand meines Vaters hielt und uns durch die Menschenmassen schlängelte, die das Gebäude füllten. Die Verkäufer auf dem Green Dragon Farmer’s Market in Ephrata, PA, versuchten ihr Bestes, Käufer mit Reihen von frischem Fisch auf Eis, Käsesorten jeder Art, Aufschnitt und Sandwiches sowie Haufen frischer Früchte zu locken. Und ach, das Konfekt! Mein junges Vorschulkind-Gedächtnis hatte noch nie so viele köstliche Süßigkeiten an einem Ort zu einer Zeit gesehen.

Die vergangenen zwei Tage für mich waren wie der Junge im Süßwarenladen. Ich hatte das Privileg, an Christian Aid Ministries’ erstem jährlichen Schriftstellerkonferenz teilzunehmen. Ich stieß mit bekannten Autoren wie Katrina Hoover Lee, Johnny Miller und Ruthann Stelfox zusammen. Ich unterhielt mich mit angehenden Schriftstellern und erfahrenen Lehrkräften. Ich hatte die Gelegenheit, an stundenlangen inspirierenden und lehrreichen Workshops teilzunehmen über das Schreiben, um zu kommunizieren, über die Verwendung realistischer Dialoge, beschreibendes Schreiben und vieles mehr. Wir alle hatten ein gemeinsames Ziel vor Augen. Gemeinsam teilen wir und lernen, wie wir das, was in unseren Herzen ist, wirkungsvoll kommunizieren und durch die Kraft des geschriebenen Wortes diese Gedanken in eure Herzen übertragen.

The Heartbeat of the Remnant ist ein Mittel, um inspirierende Gedanken an eifrige Leser auf der ganzen Welt zu übermitteln. Mutige Schreiber treten vor mit Stift und Papier oder Tastatur und Monitor und helfen, die frohe Botschaft des Wortes Gottes mit Vorsicht, Korrektur und Erbauung zu verbreiten. Dennoch brauchen wir mehr solcher Schreiber. Wir brauchen junge Gläubige, die mutig ihre ersten Kinder­geschichten einreichen. Erfahrene Großväter, die dem jüngeren Generation mahnende Worte bringen. Mütter, die Erfahrungen und Prüfungen mit anderen Müttern teilen, die mitten in der Erziehung kleiner Kinder stehen. Jugendliche, die andere Jugendliche ermutigen, auf das Ziel des Siegespreises der hohen Berufung in Christus Jesus hinzuarbeiten. Väter, die mit besorgtem Blick die Welt beobachten, wie sie auf christliche Häuser drängt. Gemeinsam werden diese angehenden Schriftsteller eine Zeitschrift produzieren, die viele Jahre auf dem Familientisch bestehen wird. Ich ermutige euch, liebe Gläubige, es zu versuchen. Nelson Mandela, ehemaliger Präsident Südafrikas, schrieb: „Failure is a teacher, and at the end of your life, what do you think you’ll feel worst about, failing or never trying?“

The Berean Voice hat sich zum Ziel gesetzt, gedrucktes Material bereitzustellen, das den Lesern hilft, durch die verschiedenen und schwierigen Jahreszeiten des Lebens zu navigieren. All unser Material ist kostenlos verfügbar, doch sind wir auf die Spenden unserer Unterstützer angewiesen. Hier ist eine Liste der Bücher, die wir anbieten:

The Power of the Love of Truth
Christian Counseling- Counterfeit?
The Heart of God
Free Indeed!
Pilgrims and Politics
Cup & Cross
The High Cost of Holistic Healing
Secrets of Successful Writing
The Catholic Connection
Psychiatry and Mood altering Medications
The Mennonite Church and Modernism

In den Jahren 2017 und 2018 druckte The Berean Voice eine Reihe von Impfstoffartikeln in der Zeitschrift The Heartbeat of the Remnant. Diese Artikel waren ein ernsthafter Versuch, verschiedene Aspekte der Impfstoffverwendung unvoreingenommen zu untersuchen. Wir bemühten uns, die Fakten so klar wie möglich darzustellen und den Lesern die Möglichkeit zu geben, ihre eigenen Schlussfolgerungen zu ziehen.

Seitdem haben wir zahlreiche Anfragen unserer Leser erhalten, alle Impfstoffartikel in einer Broschüre zu veröffentlichen, was wir zu tun zustimmten. Doch dann kam 2019 und brachte das Coronavirus mit sich. Dieses monumentale Ereignis stellte die Impfstoffdebatte auf den Kopf und leitete einen fieberhaften Wettlauf zur Markteinführung von COVID-19-Mitteln ein, von denen viele nicht ordnungsgemäß getestet wurden. Wir stellten den Druck zurück und waren uns unschlüssig, ob Informationen über diese neuen und unbelegten COVID-19-„Impfstoffe“ aufgenommen werden sollten. Mit der Zeit und als die tödliche Natur von COVID-19 nachließ, entschieden wir uns, die ursprünglichen Impfstoffartikel in einer Broschüre ohne zusätzliche Artikel zur COVID-19-Debatte zu veröffentlichen. Wir freuen uns, dass das Projekt kurz vor dem Abschluss steht und bei Veröffentlichung bekannt gegeben wird.

Segen für alle,

Edward Martin

Do you believe in miracles? Do you believe in the supernatural? What about divine intervention? Or a better question might be, have you seen God working in your life? Do others see God working in your life?

My brother was working in the greenhouse when a customer walked in and marveled at the beauty of all the plants. He then exclaimed how impressed he was at all our hard work. My brother responded with, “Some plant, some water, but God gives the increase.” To which the customer responded with, “No, no, don’t give the credit to God. You came out here and did all this work. You planted, watered, and fertilized all these plants, and you all deserve the credit, not God!” The reason the man felt this way is because he was a humanist.

What is Humanism?

The dictionary defines humanism like this; an outlook or system of thought attaching prime importance to human rather than divine or supernatural matters. Humanist beliefs stress the potential value and goodness of human beings, emphasize common human needs, and seek solely rational ways of solving human problems.

If God does exist, then we will have to recognize this fact and answer to Him. Humanists attempt to prove that God does not exist, so they can freely live their lives as they please. According to humanism, there is no God. If so, then we, the human race, are superior to God. Everything is for us and our ultimate happiness. This is the definition of humanism.

Two Types of Humanism

There are two types of humanistic beliefs, and we will look at both. The first belief is the theory that there is no God. In reality, this seems to be the only rational way to be a humanist. Everything is created by man and for man. There are no other factors or supernatural involvement. Everything happens by reason and common sense. There is a logical explanation for everything that happens. Of course, some things do not make sense, but humanists brush those aside and look only at the things that can be explained. Like the plants in the greenhouse, they look at all that man does and ignore the supernatural part of a plant springing forth with new life. Scientists around the world are working diligently to put human reasoning into everything that has ever happened, even the creation of the world. Scientists, with all their learning and wisdom, attempt to give logical explanations for why natural disasters and global crises happen. If they can explain everything, then they can rule out God and His existence. This allows the human race to do as it pleases without eternal consequences. This, in turn leads to a great sense of false peace.

The humanists, with all their reasoning, mock the very existence of God. If you go to most colleges in America and talk to people about Christianity, they laugh at you and mock the fact that Christians actually believe in God.

The second type of humanistic belief is a theory of humanism that acknowledges the existence of God. One anthropologist argued that humanism is a project of modernity and a secularized continuation of Western Christian theology. But if you ask people what they think humanism means, you will likely get different responses, and it becomes very confusing. But why the confusion? Because people are trying to be Christian humanists. Christian Humanism has frequently been criticized for its vagueness and difficulty to define. The reason it has become so confusing is that people want to believe in God but also believe in themselves and that the world revolves around them.

In Romans, we read, “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them” (Romans 1:18-32).

So how can one be a humanist and believe in God? This is where we hit a little closer to home. This type of humanist believes God wants him to be happy. He believes in a Creator God but does not believe he has to serve Him In reality. He doesn’t believe in the true God but, in his mind, created a fictitious god that does not exist. This allows him to live for himself and his own happiness. This type of person will talk about God, go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, he will look only to man for all his needs. If he is sick, he calls a doctor. If he needs money, he goes to the banker. If the need is a break from reality, he takes a vacation or retreat. He lives life for his own happiness and then thanks God though he did not look to God for his needs. These people are dependent on themselves. They have confidence in themselves.

Here is an example: A Christian plants a garden and takes care of it each day. He waters and fertilizes weeds and prunes. Finally, his plants all begin to bear fruit, nice fruit. He thanks God for the plentiful harvest. His neighbor, an atheistic humanist, also planted a garden. He, too, went out each day and watered, pruned, weeded, and fertilized. He also received a bountiful harvest. This man, however, boasted of all that he had accomplished. Both men did the same things and had similar results. One gave God the credit, and one credited himself. He will say he accomplished the same thing without God that his neighbor did with God. Christians know that he is wrong and that he actually did need God to grow his garden.

When something happens that requires supernatural intervention, the Christian humanist prays and asks others to pray. However, he does not believe God will answer their prayers and instantly gets to work to solve his problem, with only human reasoning. Then, if the problem is resolved, he thanks God for it. This type of humanism has confused the modern world. It has caused unbelievers to mock the Christian faith and to call it a false religion with no power.

The Christian does not believe in human reasoning. The Christian believes that the God of heaven is the reason for everything. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him” (Colossians 1:16). We are nothing without Him, and without Him, we can do nothing. Christianity is the opposite of humanism. When the Christian does something supernatural, something the humanist or atheist cannot do, then we have something that will confound the wise.

When the neighbor sees the Christian loving his enemies, forgiving someone who wronged him, and doing things that he cannot do, he then begins to wonder where the power to do these things came from. This then leads him to the Father. When there is nothing supernatural that we are doing, he is confused.

What About Us?

I fear that we are falling into this trap of ‘Christian Humanism.’ We talk the talk; we say we believe in God. We go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, from outward appearances, we trust in ourselves. Because we have centered our lives around ourselves and our well-being, the God of heaven does not hear us. Our prayers are not answered, and the time on our knees is a struggle at best. We go through the motions because that is how we’ve been taught, but our faith lies in human reasoning.

It can be extremely difficult to seek the Lord while living in a humanistic society. A society that has perfected the pursuit of liberty and happiness. Slowly, the church is caving to the ways of this world.

A minister from China was visiting the churches in America. Before departing back to China, he was asked what impressed him most about the churches in America. He replied, “I am amazed at what all they have accomplished without God.”

We would do well to simplify the modern definition of humanism. The humanist proudly denies that there is a God when he boasts of his own strength and abilities. He proclaims the great accomplishments of man and mocks the humble Christian.

The Christian denies himself, picks up his cross, and follows his Master. The Christian thinks nothing of himself or the ability of man, confidently admitting that he is merely dust and back to that dust he will quickly go. The Christian looks for the good in others and trusts God for all his daily needs and cares.

Christians believe they are merely servants to their master. They are hated by the world and despised by most, rejected. “If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. (John 15:18)” To them, this life is not the pursuit of happiness. The things of this world do not even interest them. Their joy and peace comes solely from serving their master, from pleasing their Heavenly Father. To the world, they are strange. Fools. To God, they are His dear children.

God is still looking for people today who will put their trust in Him. He is looking over all the earth for someone, somewhere, who will put aside human reasoning and common sense and obey the voice from heaven. God wants men with faith who will step out into the supernatural, like Abraham, Moses, David, and the thousands of believers that followed. Someone who will deny himself and this world and follow the Savior.

When this life is over, the humanists, whether they say they believe in God or not, will perish. And the Christians will go on to live forever in glory.

Humanist? Christian? Christian Humanist? Which one are you?

Tror du på mirakler? Tror du på det overnaturlige? Hva med guddommelig inngripen? Eller et bedre spørsmål kan være: har du sett Gud virke i ditt liv? Ser andre Gud virke i ditt liv?

Broren min arbeidet i drivhuset da en kunde kom inn og beundret skjønnheten i alle plantene. Han utbrøt hvor imponert han var over alt arbeidet vårt. Broren min svarte: «Noen plantet, noen vannet, men Gud gir veksten.» Kunden svarte: «Nei, nei, ikke gi æren til Gud. Dere kom hit og gjorde alt dette arbeidet. Dere plantet, vannet og gjødslet alle disse plantene, og dere fortjener æren, ikke Gud!» Grunnen til at mannen følte det slik var at han var humanist.

Hva er humanisme?

Ordboken definerer humanisme slik; et syn eller tankesystem som tilligger menneskelige fremfor guddommelige eller overnaturlige spørsmål størst betydning. Humanistiske overbevisninger legger vekt på menneskenes potensielle verdi og godhet, understreker felles menneskelige behov, og søker utelukkende rasjonelle måter å løse menneskelige problemer på.

Hvis Gud eksisterer, må vi anerkjenne dette faktum og stå til rette for Ham. Humanister prøver å bevise at Gud ikke eksisterer, så de fritt kan leve sine liv som de vil. Ifølge humanismen finnes det ingen Gud. Hvis det er tilfelle, er vi, menneskeslekten, overlegen Gud. Alt er for oss og vår ultimate lykke. Dette er definisjonen av humanisme.

To typer humanisme

Det finnes to typer humanistiske overbevisninger, og vi skal se på begge. Den første oppfatningen er teorien om at det ikke finnes noen Gud. I realiteten virker dette som den eneste rasjonelle måten å være humanist på. Alt er skapt av mennesket og for mennesket. Det finnes ingen andre faktorer eller overnaturlig innblanding. Alt skjer ved fornuft og sunn fornuft. Det finnes en logisk forklaring på alt som skjer. Selvfølgelig gir ikke alt mening, men humanister skyver disse tingene til side og ser bare på det som kan forklares. Som plantene i drivhuset ser de på alt mennesket gjør og ignorerer den overnaturlige delen av at en plante springer frem med nytt liv. Forskere verden over arbeider flittig for å legge menneskelig resonnering inn i alt som noen gang har skjedd, til og med skapelsen av verden. Forskere, med all sin lærdom og visdom, forsøker å gi logiske forklaringer på hvorfor naturkatastrofer og globale kriser skjer. Hvis de kan forklare alt, kan de utelukke Gud og Hans eksistens. Dette gjør det mulig for menneskeslekten å gjøre som den vil uten evige konsekvenser. Dette fører igjen til en stor følelse av falsk fred.

Humanistene, med all sin resonnering, gjør narr av selve Guds eksistens. Hvis du går på de fleste høyskoler i Amerika og snakker med folk om kristendom, ler de av deg og håner det at kristne faktisk tror på Gud.

Den andre typen humanistisk overbevisning er en teori om humanisme som anerkjenner Guds eksistens. En antropolog hevdet at humanisme er et prosjekt av moderniteten og en sekularisert fortsettelse av vestlig kristen teologi. Men hvis du spør folk hva de mener humanisme betyr, vil du sannsynligvis få forskjellige svar, og det blir veldig forvirrende. Men hvorfor forvirringen? Fordi folk prøver å være kristne humanister. Kristen humanisme har ofte blitt kritisert for vaghet og for at den er vanskelig å definere. Grunnen til at det har blitt så forvirrende er at folk vil tro på Gud, men også tro på seg selv og at verden dreier seg rundt dem.

I Romerne leser vi, “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them” (Romans 1:18-32).

Så hvordan kan man være humanist og tro på Gud? Her treffer vi litt nærmere hjemme. Denne typen humanist tror at Gud vil at han skal være lykkelig. Han tror på en Skaper-Gud, men tror ikke at han i virkeligheten må tjene Ham. Han tror ikke på den sanne Gud, men i sitt sinn har han skapt en fiktiv gud som ikke eksisterer. Dette gjør at han kan leve for seg selv og sin egen lykke. Denne typen person vil snakke om Gud, gå i kirken, synge salmer og si bønner. Likevel vil han bare se til mennesker for alle sine behov. Hvis han er syk, ringer han en lege. Hvis han trenger penger, går han til bankmannen. Hvis behovet er et avbrekk fra virkeligheten, tar han en ferie eller et retrett. Han lever livet for sin egen lykke og takker så Gud selv om han ikke så til Gud for sine behov. Disse menneskene er avhengige av seg selv. De har tillit til seg selv.

Her er et eksempel: En kristen planter en hage og tar seg av den hver dag. Han vanner, gjødsler, fjerner ugress og beskjærer. Endelig begynner plantene hans å bære frukt, fin frukt. Han takker Gud for den rikelige høsten. Hans nabo, en ateistisk humanist, plantet også en hage. Han gikk også ut hver dag og vannet, beskar, luktet ut ugress og gjødslet. Han fikk også en rik høst. Denne mannen skrytet imidlertid av alt han hadde oppnådd. Begge menn gjorde de samme tingene og fikk liknende resultater. Den ene ga Gud æren, og den ene gav seg selv æren. Han vil si at han oppnådde det samme uten Gud som naboen gjorde med Gud. Kristne vet at han tar feil og at han faktisk trengte Gud for å få hagen til å vokse.

Når noe skjer som krever overnaturlig inngripen, ber den kristne humanisten og ber andre om å be. Men han tror ikke at Gud vil svare på bønnene, og går straks i gang med å løse problemet med bare menneskelig resonnering. Så, hvis problemet blir løst, takker han Gud for det. Denne typen humanisme har forvirret den moderne verden. Den har fått vantroende til å håne den kristne tro og kalle den en falsk religion uten kraft.

Den kristne tror ikke på menneskelig resonnering. Den kristne tror at himmelens Gud er årsaken til alt. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him” (Colossians 1:16). Vi er ingenting uten Ham, og uten Ham kan vi ingenting gjøre. Kristen tro er motsatsen til humanisme. Når den kristne gjør noe overnaturlig, noe humanisten eller ateisten ikke kan gjøre, da har vi noe som vil forvirre de vise.

Når naboen ser den kristne elske sine fiender, tilgi noen som har gjort ham urett, og gjøre ting han ikke kan gjøre, begynner han å undre hvor kraften til å gjøre disse tingene kom fra. Dette fører ham så til Faderen. Når det ikke er noe overnaturlig vi gjør, er han forvirret.

Hva med oss?

Jeg frykter at vi er i ferd med å falle i denne fellen med «kristen humanisme». Vi snakker fint; vi sier at vi tror på Gud. Vi går i kirken, synger salmer og ber bønner. Men utad stoler vi på oss selv. Fordi vi har sentrert våre liv rundt oss selv og vårt velvære, hører ikke himmelens Gud oss. Våre bønner blir ikke besvart, og tiden på knærne er på det meste en kamp. Vi går gjennom bevegelsene fordi det er slik vi har blitt lært, men vår tro ligger i menneskelig resonnering.

Det kan være ekstremt vanskelig å søke Herren mens man lever i et humanistisk samfunn. Et samfunn som har perfeksjonert jakten på frihet og lykke. Sakte gir kirken etter for dette verdens måter.

En minister fra Kina besøkte kirkene i Amerika. Før han dro tilbake til Kina, ble han spurt hva som imponerte ham mest med kirkene i Amerika. Han svarte: «Jeg er forbløffet over hva de alle har oppnådd uten Gud.»

Vi ville gjøre klokt i å forenkle den moderne definisjonen av humanisme. Humanisten benekter stolt at det finnes en Gud når han skryter av sin egen styrke og evner. Han kunngjør menneskets store prestasjoner og gjør narr av den ydmyke kristne.

Den kristne fornekter seg selv, tar opp sitt kors og følger sin Mester. Den kristne tenker ikke på seg selv eller menneskets evne, og innrømmer trygt at han bare er støv og at han raskt skal vende tilbake til det støvet. Den kristne søker det gode i andre og stoler på Gud for alle sine daglige behov og bekymringer.

Kristne tror de bare er tjenere for sin Herre. De blir hatet av verden og foraktet av de fleste, forkastet. «If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. (John 15:18)» For dem er ikke dette livet jakten på lykke. Verdslige ting interesserer dem ikke engang. Deres glede og fred kommer utelukkende fra å tjene sin Herre, fra å behage sin Himmelske Far. For verden er de merkelige. Tullinger. For Gud er de Hans kjære barn.

Gud leter fortsatt etter mennesker i dag som vil sette sin lit til Ham. Han ser over hele jorden etter noen, et sted, som vil legge til side menneskelig resonnering og sunn fornuft og adlyde stemmen fra himmelen. Gud ønsker mennesker med tro som vil tre inn i det overnaturlige, som Abraham, Moses, David og de tusenvis av troende som fulgte. Noen som vil fornekte seg selv og denne verden og følge Frelseren.

Når dette livet er over, vil humanistene, enten de sier de tror på Gud eller ikke, gå til grunne. Og de kristne skal vandre videre for å leve evig i herlighet.

Humanist? Kristen? Kristen humanist? Hvem er du?
