Я до сих пор чувствую манящую какофонию запахов, когда крепко держал отцовскую сильную руку и пробирался сквозь толпы туристов, заполнивших здание. Торговцы на фермерском рынке Green Dragon в Эфрате, штат Пенсильвания, изо всех сил старались привлечь покупателей рядами свежей рыбы на льду, сырами всех видов, мясными деликатесами и сэндвичами, горами свежих фруктов. И, о боже, конфеты! Мой юный дошкольный ум никогда не видел столько вкусных сладостей в одном месте одновременно.

Для меня прошедшие двое суток были похожи на мальчика в кондитерской. Мне выпала привилегия присутствовать на первой ежегодной конференции писателей Christian Aid Ministries. Я обменивался рукопожатиями с известными авторами, такими как Katrina Hoover Lee, Johnny Miller и Ruthann Stelfox. Я общался с начинающими писателями и опытными школьными учителями. У меня была возможность послушать часы вдохновляющих и обучающих семинаров о том, как писать для общения, используя реалистичные диалоги, описательное письмо и многое другое. У всех нас была одна общая цель. Вместе мы делимся и учимся эффективно передавать то, что у нас на сердце, и через силу письменного слова транслировать эти мысли к вашим сердцам.

The Heartbeat of the Remnant — это средство для передачи вдохновляющих мыслей жаждущим читателям, разбросанным по всему миру. Смелые писатели выходят вперед с пером и бумагой или с клавиатурой и монитором и помогают распространять Благую Весть Слова Божьего с осторожностью, исправлением и наставлением. Однако нам нужно больше таких авторов. Нам нужны молодые верующие, которые смело представят свои первые детские истории. Закалённые деды, которые принесут слова увещевания молодому поколению. Матери, которые поделятся опытом и испытаниями с другими матерями, находящимися в гуще воспитания малышей. Молодёжь, ободряющая ровесников стремиться к награде высокого звания во Христе Иисусе. Отцы, которые с озабоченным взором наблюдают, как мир давит на христианские дома. Вместе эти начинающие писатели создадут периодическое издание, которое будет долго стоять на семейном журнальном столике. Я призываю вас, братья и сестры во Христе, попробовать. Нельсон Мандела, бывший президент Южно-Африканской Республики, написал: «Неудача — учитель, и в конце вашей жизни о чём, как вы думаете, будете жалеть больше: о провале или о том, что вы никогда не попробовали?»

Цель The Berean Voice — предоставлять печатные материалы, которые помогут читателям ориентироваться в разных и трудных сезонах жизни. Все наши материалы доступны бесплатно, но мы зависим от пожертвований наших сторонников. Вот список книг, которые у нас есть:

Сила любви к истине
Христианское консультирование — подделка?
Сердце Бога
Поистине свободны!
Пилигримы и политика
Чаша и Крест
Высокая цена холистического исцеления
Секреты успешного письма
Католическая связь
Психиатрия и препараты, изменяющие настроение
Меннонитская церковь и модернизм

В 2017 и 2018 годах The Berean Voice публиковал серию статей о вакцинах в журнале The Heartbeat of the Remnant. Эти статьи были искренней попыткой изучить различные аспекты применения вакцин беспристрастно. Мы стремились представить факты как можно яснее и позволить читателям сделать собственные выводы.

С тех пор мы получили многочисленные просьбы от наших читателей опубликовать все статьи о вакцинах в брошюре, с чем мы согласились. Но затем пришёл 2019 год и принес с собой коронавирус. Это монументальное событие перевернуло дебаты о вакцинах и вызвало бешеную гонку по выводу на рынок средств от COVID-19, многие из которых не были должным образом протестированы. Мы приостановили печать, не будучи уверенными, включать ли информацию о этих новых и непроверенных «вакцинах» от COVID-19. По мере того как время шло и смертельная угроза COVID-19 уменьшилась, мы решили опубликовать первоначальные статьи о вакцинах в брошюре без каких-либо дополнительных материалов по дебатам о COVID-19. Мы рады, что проект близок к завершению и будет анонсирован при выходе.

Благословений всем,

Edward Martin

A Christ-centered Courtship is a series of messages on godly courtship preached by Paul Hershberger. He preached these messages several times at different locations over the last ten years. Recently, we had them transcribed and abridged for reading clarity. After printing all six articles in The Heartbeat of the Remnant, we will publish them in a booklet. This is the first article of six.

Introduction

My wife and I had the privilege of having a courtship without regrets or guilt. We were blessed with parents who guided us in the right way and gave us opportunities that they didn’t have.

If you don’t have that testimony or memory, please don’t go on a guilt trip. But my prayer for you is that you get a burning burden and vision in your heart to have it for your children. That can be your reward.

A Christ-centered courtship is a period of time between a single life and a married life. The decisions you make in this period will affect you for the rest of your lives. With God’s blessing on your life, you can end up with no regrets or guilt.

Five goals for this Christ-Centered Courtship series.

Goal #1. To turn the hearts of the fathers to their children.

Goal #2. To turn the hearts of the children to their fathers.

Goal #3. That parents would get a burden to lead each one of their children into the perfect will of God for their lives.

Goal #4. That young people would get a burden to seek after God, find fulfillment and purpose in walking with God, and you would seek maturity in your manners and in your character.

Goal #5. That young men and young women would rise up to be godly fathers and godly mothers with a vision to raise up another godly generation, and the Gospel of Jesus Christ can go on.

God’s Plan for Male and Female

Ecclesiastes 12:1 says, “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them.” My desire is that each one of you, remember your Creator in the days of your youth. Turn your heart, your focus, and your life to pursue after your Creator, Almighty God, in heaven.

What does he mean, “while the evil days come not” and “the years draw nigh”? It means to seek the Lord when you’re young. Take the energy of your youth and seek after God. Young people, you’re young and full of ideas, visions, plans, and dreams. I doubt there are any of you who just enjoy sitting down in an easy chair, putting your feet up, and just dreaming about how terrible and horrible life is going to be. We don’t do that, do we? But if we don’t walk with God and follow God’s plan, hard things will come upon us. When hard things come in life, we have no place to turn to. We dream that life will turn out well. The decisions and actions in our youth affect us for the rest of our lives. The good news is they can affect us in a good way. The bad news is they can affect us in a bad way. It depends on what decisions and choices we make. But young people, you’re young, and you have the opportunity to choose.

Let’s go to the beginning of Genesis.

“And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him. And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field, and every fowl of the air; and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them: and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof. And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him. And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man. And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:18-24).

“And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth” (Genesis 1:26-28).

“And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him” (Genesis 2:18). “I’ll make him an help that is meet for him.” God said He would do that.

“So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them” (Genesis 1:27). God made. God created us male and female. It takes a lot of blind faith to believe that we evolved perfectly as male and female. The creation of male and female is God’s plan. It is one of the living proofs of Creation. God made. God created. It’s God’s plan. God is the Author. And God’s plan brings blessing.

I’d like to look at ten different aspects of this blessing of God’s plan.

1) God brings Eve to Adam.

“And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man. And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man” (Genesis 2:22-23).

God caused Adam to fall into a deep sleep. Then God created Eve and brought her to Adam. Adam awoke and realized, “This one is for me!” He had seen all the animals go by when he named them. Now God brings him someone that is for him. He also realized, “She was taken out of my side.” She’s close to his heart. “This is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh.” It’s not a dog; it’s not a giraffe, or a monkey, or an ape. This one that God brought to him is like him. God’s plan has a blessing.

Adam and Eve had never had a companion before. Adam and Eve had never let the emotions of their heart go before. Something happened in Adam and Eve’s hearts. Adam was a “one-woman man,” and Eve was a “one-man woman.” They never gave their heart passions to anybody else. God has that plan for us, too. God’s plan brings blessings.

2) Leaving and cleaving in unity for life.

“Therefore Bshall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:24).

This verse says, “Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother,” but Adam and Eve did not have a father and mother. What God is saying it doesn’t work for there to be cleaving unless there’s leaving. Also, in Mark 10:7, we read, “For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife.” This is God’s plan, and God’s plan brings blessing.

Leaving means to leave behind, to abandon. “For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother” is to leave parents leave behind. Let’s consider a young man who has a really good home life. He’s blessed and has everything he needs. Yet once God brings his Eve into his life, something rises up inside him, and he says, “I’m leaving!” But this is God’s plan. And God’s plan brings blessing.

It’s not just leaving his father and mother; he also cleaves to his wife. Cleave means “to glue to, to adhere.” We are very familiar with glued wood panels. All kinds of solid furniture are made out of panels glued together. And if they’re glued together right, they will not come apart at the joints. If you tear them apart, you’re going to have to tear the wood apart. God’s glue is the same way, where it glues two people together. The only way to tear them apart is by splintering and ripping and God does not bless that. But leaving and cleaving, staying together and being glued together, that’s God’s plan and it brings blessing.

3) They shall be one flesh.

“Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:24). Two single people who become one married couple, become one unit before God, and become one family before God. They become one flesh, where God sees them as together as one.

“And they twain shall be one flesh: so then they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder” (Mark 10:8-9). God’s plan for male and female is that He brings Eve to Adam. Then the leaving and cleaving to take place. He causes them to become one flesh. Pulling apart is no blessing at all but bringsagony,pain,travail, and hurt. There is no blessing in separation. But God’s plan brings blessing.

4) Not an unequal yoke.

“Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness” (2 Corinthians 6:14-15). “The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband liveth; but if her husband be dead, she is at liberty to be married to whom she will; only in the Lord” (1 Corinthians 7:39).

God’s plan is that marriage is an equal yoke. God will not bring an Eve to an Adam in a marriage that is an unequal yoke.Let’s think about leaving and cleaving, getting glued together, and two becoming one. In marriage, those two are now one before God. Imagine being in a bad marriage relationship like this—a family like this trying to function together. There will be no blessing.

But an equal yoke brings blessing! God desires that we be joined together in one flesh, one heart, and one mind. He wants to see us joined in heart, mind, and fleashthe whole being, being one. God’s plan brings blessing.

5) God planned for us to have children.

“And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth” (Genesis 1:28). Think of the joy and miracle every time another child is born into a Christian home. God planned it this way. And if God brought Adam his Eve, and they leave and cleave, they become one flesh, one heart, one mind. If they are equally yoked and God blesses them with children, it becomes a joyful haven where God can dwell. “And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth” (Genesis 9:1). “And you, be ye fruitful, and multiply; bring forth abundantly in the earth, and multiply therein” (Genesis 9:7). God’s plan brings blessing.

6) Headship order.

“But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God” (1 Corinthians 11:3). It is God, and then Christ, the man, and the woman. God established a headship order, and this headship order is a blessing. It’s God’s plan, and it’s a blessing.

“Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honor thy father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise; That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth” (Ephesians 6:1-3). . Children, obey your parents in the Lord is a part of the headship order. This not difficult to understand, is it? A home following the plan of God is just a blessed situation. Young people learn to be under authority. Make that your high priority. The sooner you learn to be under authority, the better you will be prepared for the responsibilities in life.

I remember looking at married life and having aspirations about teaching children and raising a godly family. I listened to the “Godly Home” series and thought I was ready to go. But then the day came when it was my turn and my responsibility, and all of a sudden, my heart wanted to wither. Responsibility doesn’t feel the same as dreaming about it does. YOU need to do something! YOU are responsible. YOU need to make it happen. And, by the way, not just make it happen; you need to make it happen in a Christlike way. You need to make it happen in a way that the anointing of the Spirit of God can come down on your family. The better we learn how to be under authority, the better we’ll be prepared for those responsibilities. The more we realize we need God, the better off we are. Let’s make a high priority out of learning to be under authority as children and as young people. “My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments: For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee” (Proverbs 3:1-2).

God will add his blessing if we stay in this headship order. The more you learn how to be under authority, the more you will be blessed when you establish your home. God’s plan has blessings.

7) A godly marriage.

Ephesians 5:21,22,24 says, “Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God. Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. . . Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.”

First of all look at verse 21, “submitting yourselves one to another.” There’s a blending together that needs to happen in a godly home. This blending together should happen in the fear of God. If we’re submitting one to another in the fear of God, we’re going to obey God because we want His blessings.

Ephesians 5: 22, 24 “Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. . . Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.” Young ladies, you can count on it: submission to Dad equals submission to a husband. You can practice while you are single. This will help build character in your life. Being a rebellious and froward woman is not going to bring the blessing of God.

It goes on and says, in Ephesians 5:25,28,29. “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it . . . So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church.” Young men, this says that husbands should love their wives. So who do you think God put in your life to prepare you to love your wife? Your mother! Do you want to learn how to love your wife? Learn how to get along with your mom, love your mom, and care about her. Do you want to practice to love your future wife? Go ahead and love your mom.

Verse 33, “Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.” God’s plan brings blessings.

8) Being heirs together of the grace of life.

1 Peter 3:7 “Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honor unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.” As husbands, we give honor to the wife. She is the weaker vessel and the one that born the children! She’s gone through a lot of traumatic changes in her life. She’s the one that gets worn out and tires sooner.

And he says, “Husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge.”

Young men, learn to understand your mom and your sisters. It will help you after you get married. Don’t conclude that—ah, that’s just women. No, you want the blessing of God. Learn to know and understand them.

“Being heirs together of the grace of life.” God wants us to be heirs together of the grace of life. If we’re not heirs together of the grace of life, can we be heirs separated of the grace of life? I don’t think so. He says we should be heirs together so that our prayers are not hindered. So if we’re heirs separated, could we say our prayers will be hindered? Yes, our prayers will be hindered. Let’s give honor unto the wife as unto the weaker vessel. Every ounce you can gain in this area will only bless you later. It’s worth it. God’s plan brings blessing.

9) A blessed and secure home.

This comes partly out of 1 Peter 3:7, but also from Psalm 144:12 “That our sons may be as plants grown up in their youth; that our daughters may be as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace.” The grace of God is on a secure home where there is unity. Where Dad is understanding Mom, where Dad cares about Mom. Dad is ministering and is there to help and guide. He’s there to give direction with a heart of compassion. God’s plan for male and female—God’s plan brings blessings.

10) As Christ and the church.

“Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing. Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish. So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church” (Ephesians 5:24-29).

“Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave Himself for it.” God is looking for men who are willing to give their lives. Single young men, who are willing to answer the call and give their life. This is a high calling of God. It’s the plan of God.

Young men, are you willing to lay down your life, your agenda, and those independent things you like to do? Are you willing to be patient, gentle, and understanding? Are you willing to lose sleep and keep going even when you’re tired? Are you willing to stay calm and not react in stressful circumstances? Are you willing to lead and guide a wife and children, eternal souls, through this life?

But my plea is that you would volunteer and say, “I’m willing to apply myself to the Word of God, the will of God, the plan of God, and I’ll give my life. I’m willing to lay it on the altar.” Jesus gave His life for us, and He’s comparing the marriage with the church and Him.

There’s also a need for mothers who are submissive and yielded to authority. Mothers who do not follow the women’s lib of our day but are rather content to be keepers at home.

Young ladies, are you willing to enlist? Will you give your heart to be guided and led? Are you willing to follow and to cheerfully submit to your authority? Are you willing to serve and be spent for your family? Are you willing to serve and be spent for YOUR family? If you get married someday, it will be YOUR family that you’ll be serving and being spent for. Are you willing to bear pain and discomfort? Are you willing to be a helpmeet, giving yourself for his burden and vision?

But as we look at God’s plan and blessings, you want God’s blessing, young people! But that means you need to make choices accordingly. Rise up and make decisions that will lead to maturity. Maturity comes with the process of seeking after God. Make a commitment in your heart to open yourself to God’s blessings and principles. I encourage you to walk with God, to have a relationship with Jesus Christ, and to do so in humility.

Seek after Christlike character, and do it on purpose. It is so easy for us to just live life however it happens. But if we make decisions on purpose, it will take us somewhere! Those decisions matter. Do things according to God’s plan.

God has a plan for male and female and he has a plan for you.

《以基督为中心的恋爱》是保罗·赫什伯格所讲的一系列关于敬虔恋爱的信息。在过去十年间，他曾在不同地方多次宣讲这些信息。最近，我们将这些信息转录成文字，并加以删节，使阅读更为清晰。待这六篇文章全部在《余民的心声》刊登后，我们将把它们出版成小册子。这是六篇中的第一篇。

引言

我和妻子有幸经历了一段没有遗憾或愧疚的恋爱。我们蒙福，父母引导我们走正确的道路，也给了我们他们自己未曾有过的机会。

如果你没有这样的见证或回忆，请不要陷入自责。但我为你祷告，愿你心中生出迫切的负担和异象，让你的儿女能够拥有这样的经历。这可以成为你的奖赏。

以基督为中心的恋爱，是介于单身生活与婚姻生活之间的一段时期。你们在这段时期所作的决定，会影响你们的一生。有神赐福你们的生命，你们最终可以没有遗憾或愧疚。

《以基督为中心的恋爱》系列的五个目标。

目标一：使父亲的心转向儿女。

目标二：使儿女的心转向父亲。

目标三：使父母心中有负担，引导每一个儿女进入神对他们人生的完美旨意之中。

目标四：使年轻人心中有负担去寻求神，在与神同行中找到满足和人生目的，并在举止和品格上追求成熟。

目标五：使青年男女兴起，成为敬虔的父亲和母亲，怀着培育下一代敬虔之人的异象，使耶稣基督的福音得以继续传扬。

神对男女的计划

传道书12:1说：“趁着你年幼，衰败的日子尚未来到，那些使你说‘我在其中毫无乐趣’的年岁尚未临近，现在就当记念你的创造主。”我盼望你们每一个人都在年幼的时候记念自己的创造主。将你的心、你的关注和你的生命转向你在天上的创造主——全能的神，去追求祂。

“衰败的日子尚未来到”和“年岁尚未临近”是什么意思呢？意思就是要在年轻的时候寻求主。用你青春的精力去寻求神。年轻人，你们正值青春，满有想法、异象、计划和梦想。我想你们中间大概没有谁喜欢坐在安乐椅上，翘起双脚，只管想象将来的生活会多么糟糕、多么可怕。我们不会这样，对吗？但如果我们不与神同行，不遵循神的计划，艰难的事就会临到我们。当人生的艰难来到时，我们就无处求助。我们梦想人生会有美好的结局。我们年轻时的决定和行动，会影响我们的一生。好消息是，它们可以给我们带来好的影响。坏消息是，它们也可以给我们带来坏的影响。这取决于我们作出什么决定和选择。但年轻人，你们还年轻，你们有选择的机会。

让我们来看创世记的开头。

“耶和华神说：‘那人独居不好；我要为他造一个与他相配的帮手。’耶和华神用地上的土造了田野的各样走兽和天空的各样飞鸟，把它们带到亚当面前，看他怎样称呼它们；亚当怎样称呼各样活物，那就是它们的名字。亚当给一切牲畜、天空的飞鸟和田野的各样走兽都起了名字，但没有找到与亚当相配的帮手。耶和华神使亚当沉睡，他就睡着了；神取下他的一根肋骨，又使那处的肉合起来。耶和华神用从那人身上取下的肋骨造了一个女人，把她带到那人面前。亚当说：‘这一次，她是我骨中的骨，肉中的肉；她要称为女人，因为她是从男人身上取出来的。’因此，人要离开父亲和母亲，与妻子紧紧联合，二人成为一体”（创世记2:18-24）。

“神说：‘我们要照着我们的形象，按着我们的样式造人，让他们管理海里的鱼、天空的鸟、牲畜、全地，以及地上爬行的各样爬物。’神就照着自己的形象造人，照着神的形象造了他；祂造了他们，有男有女。神赐福给他们，神对他们说：‘要生养众多，遍满全地，治理这地；要管理海里的鱼、天空的鸟，以及地上活动的各样活物’”（创世记1:26-28）。

“耶和华神说：‘那人独居不好；我要为他造一个与他相配的帮手’”（创世记2:18）。“我要为他造一个适合他的帮手。”神说祂会这样做。

“神就照着自己的形象造人，照着神的形象造了他；祂造了他们，有男有女”（创世记1:27）。是神造的。神创造了我们，有男有女。要相信我们完美地进化成了男性和女性，需要很大的盲目信念。创造男女是神的计划。这是创造的一个活生生的证据。神造了我们。神创造了我们。这是神的计划。神是创始者。而神的计划带来祝福。

我想从十个不同的方面，来看看神的计划所带来的祝福。

1）神将夏娃带到亚当面前。

“耶和华神用从那人身上取下的肋骨造了一个女人，把她带到那人面前。亚当说：‘这一次，她是我骨中的骨，肉中的肉；她要称为女人，因为她是从男人身上取出来的’”（创世记2:22-23）。

神使亚当沉睡。然后神创造了夏娃，把她带到亚当面前。亚当醒来，明白了：“这一位是为我预备的！”他给动物起名字时，曾看着所有动物从面前经过。现在，神带给他一位为他预备的人。他也明白：“她是从我的肋旁取出来的。”她贴近他的心。“这是我骨中的骨，肉中的肉。”她不是狗，不是长颈鹿，也不是猴子或猿。神带给他的这一位，与他相似。神的计划中有祝福。

亚当和夏娃从前都没有过伴侣。亚当和夏娃从前都未曾释放过心中的情感。如今，他们心中发生了变化。亚当是一个“只爱一个女人的男人”，夏娃是一个“只爱一个男人的女人”。他们从未将心中的爱恋给过别人。神对我们也有这样的计划。神的计划带来祝福。

2）离开与联合，终身合一。

“因此，人要离开父亲和母亲，与妻子紧紧联合，二人成为一体”（创世记2:24）。

这节经文说：“因此，人要离开父亲和母亲”，但亚当和夏娃并没有父亲和母亲。神的意思是，若没有离开，就无法联合。我们在马可福音10:7也读到：“为这缘故，人要离开父亲和母亲，与妻子紧紧联合。”这是神的计划，而神的计划带来祝福。

离开的意思是留在身后、放下。“为这缘故，人要离开父亲和母亲”，就是离开父母，将他们留在身后。让我们想想一个家庭生活十分美好的年轻人。他蒙了祝福，所需的一切都有。然而，一旦神把属于他的夏娃带进他的生命，他心里就涌起一种念头，说：“我要离开了！”但这正是神的计划。而神的计划带来祝福。

他不只是离开父亲和母亲，也要与妻子紧紧联合。联合的意思是“粘合、紧贴”。我们很熟悉胶合木板。各种实木家具都是用粘合在一起的木板制成的。如果粘合得当，它们就不会从接缝处裂开。若要把它们拆开，就必须把木头撕裂。神的胶也是如此，将两个人粘合在一起。要把他们拆开，只有劈裂和撕扯，而神不会赐福这种事。但离开与联合，长相厮守、粘合在一起，这才是神的计划，并且带来祝福。

3）二人成为一体。

“因此，人要离开父亲和母亲，与妻子紧紧联合，二人成为一体”（创世记2:24）。两个单身的人结为夫妻，在神面前成为一个整体，在神面前成为一个家庭。他们成为一体，神看他们是合而为一的。

“二人要成为一体；这样，他们不再是两个人，而是一体了。所以，神所配合的，人不可分开”（马可福音10:8-9）。神对男女的计划，是祂将夏娃带到亚当面前。然后发生离开与联合。祂使他们成为一体。拆散他们毫无祝福可言，只会带来煎熬、痛苦、苦楚和伤害。分离之中没有祝福。但神的计划带来祝福。

4）不可不相配地负轭。

“不要与不信的人不相配地同负一轭，因为义与不义有什么相交呢”（哥林多后书6:14-15）。“丈夫活着的时候，妻子受律法约束；丈夫若死了，她就可以自由地嫁给自己愿意嫁的人，只是要在主里”（哥林多前书7:39）。

神的计划是，婚姻应当是相配地同负一轭。神不会把一个夏娃带给一个亚当，让他们进入不相配地同负一轭的婚姻。让我们想想离开与联合、粘合在一起，以及二人成为一体。在婚姻里，这两个人如今在神面前成为一体。想象处在这样一种不好的婚姻关系中——这样的家庭还要尝试共同生活。那里面不会有祝福。

但相配地同负一轭会带来祝福！神愿我们联合，成为一体、一心、一意。祂愿看到我们在心思、意念和身体上联合，整个人合而为一。神的计划带来祝福。

5）神计划让我们生养儿女。

“神赐福给他们，神对他们说：‘要生养众多，遍满全地，治理这地；要管理海里的鱼、天空的鸟，以及地上活动的各样活物’”（创世记1:28）。想想每当一个基督徒家庭又有一个孩子出生时，那份喜乐和奇迹。神就是这样计划的。如果神把亚当的夏娃带给他，他们离开并联合，就成为一体、一心、一意。如果他们相配地同负一轭，神又赐给他们儿女，这个家就成为神可以居住的喜乐避风港。“神赐福给挪亚和他的儿子们，对他们说：‘要生养众多，遍满全地’”（创世记9:1）。“至于你们，要生养众多，在地上繁衍，在其中增多”（创世记9:7）。神的计划带来祝福。

6）作头的次序。

“但我愿你们知道，每一个男人的头是基督，女人的头是男人，基督的头是神”（哥林多前书11:3）。首先是神，然后是基督、男人和女人。神设立了作头的次序，而这个次序是祝福。这是神的计划，也是祝福。

“你们作儿女的，要在主里听从父母，因为这是理所当然的。要孝敬父亲和母亲；这是第一条带有应许的诫命，使你得福，在地上长寿”（以弗所书6:1-3）。儿女在主里听从父母，是作头次序的一部分。这不难理解，对吗？一个遵循神计划的家庭，就是蒙福的家庭。年轻人，要学习顺服权柄。把这件事放在优先的位置。你越早学会顺服权柄，就越能预备好承担人生的责任。

我记得自己曾展望婚姻生活，向往教导孩子、建立敬虔的家庭。我听了“敬虔的家庭”系列信息，以为自己已经准备好了。但后来，轮到我承担责任的那一天来到了，我的心却突然想要退缩。真正承担责任，与梦想承担责任，感受并不一样。你自己需要采取行动！你自己要负责。你自己需要把事情做成。而且，不只是把事情做成，还要以像基督的方式去做。你做事的方式，必须使神的灵的膏抹能够临到你的家庭。我们越懂得如何顺服权柄，就越能预备好承担这些责任。我们越认识到自己需要神，就越有益处。让我们在作孩子和年轻人的时候，就把学习顺服权柄放在优先的位置。“我儿，不要忘记我的教训，你的心要谨守我的诫命，因为它们必给你增添长久的年日、长寿和平安”（箴言3:1-2）。

如果我们持守这个作头的次序，神就会加添祂的祝福。你越学会顺服权柄，将来建立家庭时就越蒙福。神的计划中有祝福。

7）敬虔的婚姻。

以弗所书5:21,22,24说：“要存敬畏神的心彼此顺服。你们作妻子的，要顺服自己的丈夫，如同顺服主……因此，教会怎样顺服基督，妻子也要怎样凡事顺服自己的丈夫。”

首先来看第21节：“要彼此顺服。”敬虔的家庭需要有一种彼此融合。这种融合应当在敬畏神的心中实现。如果我们存敬畏神的心彼此顺服，我们就会顺服神，因为我们盼望得到祂的祝福。

以弗所书5:22,24：“你们作妻子的，要顺服自己的丈夫，如同顺服主……因此，教会怎样顺服基督，妻子也要怎样凡事顺服自己的丈夫。”年轻的姊妹们，你们可以确信：顺服父亲，也就是学习顺服丈夫。你们可以在单身时操练。这有助于塑造你们生命中的品格。作一个悖逆、乖僻的女人，不会带来神的祝福。

接下来，以弗所书5:25,28,29说：“你们作丈夫的，要爱自己的妻子，正如基督爱教会，为教会舍了自己……丈夫也当这样爱妻子，如同爱自己的身体；爱妻子的，就是爱自己。从来没有人恨恶自己的身体，总是养育、珍爱它，正如主对教会一样。”年轻的弟兄们，这里说丈夫应当爱自己的妻子。那么，你们认为神把谁放在你们的生命中，预备你们去爱妻子呢？你们的母亲！你想学习怎样爱妻子吗？要学习如何与母亲相处，爱她、关心她。你想操练爱未来的妻子吗？那就去爱你的母亲。

第33节：“然而，你们各人都要爱自己的妻子，如同爱自己；妻子也要敬重丈夫。”神的计划带来祝福。

8）一同承受生命之恩。

彼得前书3:7：“同样，你们作丈夫的，要按着对妻子的了解与她们同住，尊重妻子，因她是较软弱的器皿，又与你们一同承受生命之恩，使你们的祷告不受阻碍。”作为丈夫，我们要尊重妻子。她是较软弱的器皿，也是生育孩子的那个人！她在生命中经历了许多剧烈的变化。她是那个容易耗尽精力、更快疲倦的人。

他又说：“丈夫们，要按着对妻子的了解与她们同住。”

年轻的弟兄们，要学习理解你们的母亲和姊妹。这会在你们结婚后帮助你们。不要断定说：“啊，女人就是这样。”不，你要的是神的祝福。要学习认识并理解她们。

“一同承受生命之恩。”神愿我们一同承受生命之恩。如果我们不是一同承受生命之恩，难道可以分开承受生命之恩吗？我不这样认为。他说，我们应当一同承受，使我们的祷告不受阻碍。那么，如果我们分开承受，是否可以说，我们的祷告就会受阻碍呢？是的，我们的祷告会受阻碍。让我们尊重妻子，因她是较软弱的器皿。你在这方面每多学会一点，将来都会使你蒙福。这是值得的。神的计划带来祝福。

9）蒙福而安稳的家庭。

这一点部分来自彼得前书3:7，也来自诗篇144:12：“愿我们的儿子在年幼时如同长成的树木；愿我们的女儿如同房角石，按宫殿的样式雕琢。”在一个安稳、合一的家庭里，有神的恩典。父亲理解母亲，父亲关心母亲。父亲服事家人，在那里帮助和引导。他在那里，以怜悯的心指明方向。神对男女的计划——神的计划带来祝福。

10）如同基督与教会。

“因此，教会怎样顺服基督，妻子也要怎样凡事顺服自己的丈夫。你们作丈夫的，要爱自己的妻子，正如基督爱教会，为教会舍了自己，要借着道用水洗净教会，使她成圣，好把教会呈献给自己，成为荣耀的教会，没有斑点、皱纹或任何这样的缺陷，而是圣洁、没有瑕疵。丈夫也当这样爱妻子，如同爱自己的身体；爱妻子的，就是爱自己。从来没有人恨恶自己的身体，总是养育、珍爱它，正如主对教会一样”（以弗所书5:24-29）。

“你们作丈夫的，要爱自己的妻子，正如基督爱教会，为教会舍了自己。”神正在寻找愿意献出生命的男人，寻找愿意回应呼召、献出生命的单身青年男子。这是神崇高的呼召。这是神的计划。

年轻的弟兄们，你们愿意放下自己的生命、自己的安排，以及那些喜欢独自去做的事吗？你们愿意耐心、温柔、体谅人吗？你们愿意少睡一些，即使疲倦也继续尽责吗？你们愿意在压力之下保持平静，不作冲动的反应吗？你们愿意带领和引导妻子、儿女——这些永恒的灵魂——走过今生吗？

我恳求你们自愿回应，说：“我愿意努力遵行神的话语、神的旨意、神的计划，我愿献出自己的生命。我愿把它放在祭坛上。”耶稣为我们舍了生命，祂将婚姻比作教会与祂的关系。

同样，也需要顺服、甘愿降服于权柄的母亲。这样的母亲不随从当今的妇女解放运动，而是甘心持家。

年轻的姊妹们，你们愿意加入这个行列吗？你们愿意献上自己的心，接受引导和带领吗？你们愿意跟随，并且喜乐地顺服在你们之上的权柄吗？你们愿意为家庭服事、耗尽自己吗？你们愿意为你们自己的家庭服事、耗尽自己吗？如果有一天你结婚了，你所服事、为之耗尽自己的，将是你自己的家庭。你愿意承受疼痛和不适吗？你愿意作一个相配的帮手，为他的负担和异象献上自己吗？

当我们看神的计划和祝福时，年轻人，你们是想要神的祝福的！但这意味着你们需要作出相应的选择。要兴起，作出引向成熟的决定。成熟是在寻求神的过程中形成的。要在心中立志，敞开自己，接受神的祝福和原则。我鼓励你们与神同行，与耶稣基督建立关系，并且谦卑地这样做。

要追求像基督的品格，并且有意识地去追求。我们很容易随波逐流地过日子。但如果我们有意识地作决定，这些决定就会把我们带向一个方向！这些决定很重要。要照着神的计划行事。

神对男女有一个计划，对你也有一个计划。

Our Father’s world is a world unspoiled by human invention and intervention. While sin and technology have warped and stolen many lovely things from the human race, there abide still a few that remain unmarred by civilization. Little children in the fresh innocence of their unsoiled morning top the ranks as a bit of heaven on earth and call all observers heavenward. Another is the fowl of the air as prescribed in Genesis. Paul pleaded with the Corinthian church, “Doth not nature itself teach you?” We are exhorted to consider the lilies, the ravens, and the grass of the field. Each of these bears a significant dimension of the eternal God in their existence and gives us definition to their Creator. Perhaps all of nature can give us snapshots into heavenly places if we had the time and eyes to observe it.

Birds hold a unique place in God’s creation, for their sphere is in the heavens. Man may mount on the wings of a plane and evade the lower earth for a few hours, but the heavens will never be a place of his common dominion. The birds are a picture of a heavenly race, for they are at home there. They are a natural representation of the saints and angels of God and so we do well to give them due attention. While there may be dozens of lessons to be drawn from these vessels of grace and beauty, one of the most prominent and outstanding virtues will be observed in the song that they raise. Many animals dwelling on the earth are virtually mute. Of the ones that do speak, it is often to threaten or express complaint. “Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?” (Job 6:5). When they are happy and content, they have no message to convey. The dog barks at an intruder to drive him away, while the cat mews for attention. They speak when they are threatened or dissatisfied, in fear or in pain. Similarly, the earthly human shares its nature with the mammals of the field.

Birds are diverse. They exercise their joyous vocals so much that they are the epitome of happiness. The expression “happy as a lark” is so common a term that it is used by people who have never even ventured to the meadow to see or hear a lark. While some may inform us that these songs are mere mating calls and have little to do with their feelings, we cannot escape the inner conviction that, whether mating or not, these birds delight in bearing a jubilant expression of joy and we do well to let them teach us. “Is any merry? Let him sing psalms” (James 5:13). The birds do this incessantly and it seems impossible to draw any other conclusion but that they are happy while doing so. Wander near the nest of a swallow and you will find that they have ways of expressing depreciation as well. The killdeer also has no qualms with expressing rash disfavor to those who intrude their domain, but these are not to be mistaken as songs. The singing birds are a beautiful painted picture of the saints and angels of God.

How little knowledge of heaven is committed to our understanding. The scenes of heavens described and laid out before us in Revelations can hardly bring our finite minds into its infinite realm. One dimension that we can connect with is that it is a place filled with singing. Little wonder, for it is the culminating end of the contented and joy-filled saints of God, and there they will sing a new song. Nearly every scene at the throne in Revelations is marked by some dimension of praise. “And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God” (Ps 40:3). On 22 occasions, the Scriptures reiterate the phrase, I will sing.

It is the nature of the birds to sing. It is their waking thought as morning guilds the sky, and it flows from within them like a fountain. Not all of their songs are alike. Some are elaborate in their duration, meter, and pitch, while others are plain. Some merely chirp with a merry heart. The robin opens up the choir in early spring, but his song is soon surpassed in beauty by the song sparrow and again by the rose-breasted grosbeak. The song of the wren trumps them all for longevity and vibrancy. The canary sings in a cage, while the nightingale sings in the dark. The robins sing in the rain. The buntings fill in the heat of the day when other birds are silent. As diverse as their song may be, they all commonly burst forth in exuberant happiness. It is here that they shall instruct us.

“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord” (Eph 5:19). The advent of Christ was marked by the angelic host announcing peace and goodwill toward men. All those who will bear His name must deliver the same tidings. In John 4, we happen upon the scene at Jacob’s well, where Christ asks the woman for a drink. Her reply seems to bear a tinge of bitterness. “Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” Though she esteemed herself as a spiritual person and willingly followed Him into religious discourse, she had no song. Like the well that they speak over, her water was buried deep below the surface and how laborious the effort to bring it forth. Christ offers another alternative. “But the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

The well of Christ is an artesian well. One needs neither pitcher nor labor to draw it out, for it spews forth abundantly on its own accord. While Christ is probably speaking of the Spirit as in John 7:38, surely this may be just as applicable to a joy-laden heart. What is a more apt outpouring to flow from a Christ-inspired wellspring than the rapture of a song? “Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart” (Is 65:14). Now this should all seem plain enough to understand and easy enough to do but, alas, we find we have a constant and persistent adversary who seeks to thwart our song. We are not unaware of his devices...

Sin. Not all birds sing. There are some whose visage is black as sin. These only seem to screech and scream and are no example for the saints of God to emulate. The babbling noise we hear emanating from many passing vehicles certainly parallels the songs of such foul fowl. “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird” (Rev 18:2). These abundant creatures are the fallen spirits, the fowls waiting to devour the seed sown by the wayside. Of such are the worthless blackbirds, starlings, and grackles. The crows show themselves also at the roadside, feeding on rotting carcasses. Often you will find them in large numbers feeding themselves on the corn the farmer painstakingly planted for himself. So transgresses the selfish soul in his pursuit of happiness, feeding gleefully on the calamity of another and exploiting their sin. He bears no song, for his day is constantly clouded by the misdeeds of others who cross his path.

Neglect. The cowbird is also black (the female is brown/gray). She will be found sitting on a high vantage, shamelessly calling to her lovers by her shrill screeching. She then has the audacity to lay her egg in another bird’s nest, forcing them to raise her offspring. This is certainly a fitting emblem for a good number of females in our day. Though justified by circumstances, these women care not for their own, but are products of neglect. They have no lullaby to share with their young, for they have escorted them to the nest of another while her mind is preoccupied with work and business. “But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts” (Ps 22:9). No doubt that the singing mother can implant copious songs in her infant and set the stage for a happy and hope-filled life. While we may show mercy to a woman in dire circumstances, the major song of modern women bears chords that are but dissident and melancholy. These are stopped-up wells like unto the wells that Isaac found upon his return to Gerar. The Philistines “had filled them with earth” (Gen 26:15). So run the spiritually neglected homes of many families today, who pack their schedules so full of earthly commitments that they have no time to spend an hour in song together. If the birds stopped singing, would they even notice?

Ingratitude. Find a soul bathed in unthankfulness, and you will find a soul without a song. If the canary were to refuse to sing in captivity, few of us would ever have heard his rollicking melody. “We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD’S song in a strange land?” (Ps 137:2-4). God’s people had been instructed by Jeremiah to build houses, plant gardens, and raise families. “… And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace” (Jer. 29:5-7). But they could see no worth in it. With their eyes fixed upon the dismal scene around them, they lost their song. Israel had within its history a rich tradition of song. Their singing erupted at the passage of the Red Sea in the days of Jehoshaphat and had been known to defeat armies. Earthly discomfort is no excuse to withhold gratitude, for our God reigns, and we are His children. Such were the conditions of the Philippian prison where two jailbirds, Paul and Silas, opened the concert at midnight and rocked the corridors with their joyful singing.

When we open our mouths and stretch our vocals in praise, we enact the grace of God. We join the faithful choir alongside Miriam, Deborah, and Hannah, and blend harmoniously with Moses, David, Paul, and Barnabas. At evening, we sing with our Lord and His disciples after supper, and with legions of angels “giving glory to God in the highest.” If that isn’t enough, perhaps we should consider rising at early dawn and singing with the innumerable hosts of our feathered friends who are thankful for God’s loving providence. “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord … And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men” (Col 3:16, 23).

Vår himmelske Faders verden er en verden urørt av menneskelig oppfinnsomhet og inngripen. Mens synd og teknologi har forvridd og stjålet mange vakre ting fra menneskeslekten, finnes det likevel noen få som forblir uskadde av sivilisasjonen. Små barn i den friske uskylden av sin uplettede morgen troner øverst som et lite stykke himmel på jord og kaller alle tilskuere mot himmelen. En annen er himmelens fugl slik den er foreskrevet i Første Mosebok. Paulus anmodet menigheten i Korint: “Doth not nature itself teach you?” Vi blir formant å overveie liljene, ravnene og markens gress. Hver av disse bærer en betydningsfull dimensjon av den evige Gud i sin eksistens og gir oss en definisjon av deres Skaper. Kanskje kan hele naturen gi oss glimt inn i himmelske steder hvis vi hadde tid og øyne til å iaktta den.

Fugler har en unik plass i Guds skapelse, for deres sfære er i himmelen. Mennesket kan stige på vingene til et fly og unnslippe den lavere jord noen timer, men himmelen vil aldri bli et sted for hans vanlige herredømme. Fuglene er et bilde på et himmelsk folk, for de hører hjemme der. De er en naturlig fremstilling av de hellige og Guds engler, og vi gjør klokt i å gi dem behørig oppmerksomhet. Mens det kan finnes dusinvis av lærepenge å hente fra disse kar av nåde og skjønnhet, vil en av de mest fremtredende og utmerkede dyder observeres i den sang de løfter. Mange dyr som lever på jorden er praktisk talt stumme. Av dem som taler, er det ofte for å true eller uttrykke klage. “Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?” (Job 6:5). Når de er glade og fornøyde, har de ingen beskjed å formidle. Hunden bjeffer på en inntrenger for å jage ham bort, mens katten mjauer for oppmerksomhet. De taler når de blir truet eller misfornøyde, i frykt eller i smerte. På samme måte deler det jordiske mennesket sin natur med felts pattedyrene.

Fugler er mangfoldige. De bruker sine glade vokaler så ofte at de er selve epitomet på lykke. Uttrykket “happy as a lark” er så vanlig at det brukes av folk som aldri engang har våget seg ut på enga for å se eller høre en lerk. Mens noen kan informere oss om at disse sangene bare er paringsrop og har lite å gjøre med deres følelser, kan vi ikke rømme fra den indre overbevisningen om at, enten de paret eller ikke, gleder disse fuglene seg ved å bære et jublende uttrykk av fryd, og vi gjør klokt i å la dem lære oss. “Is any merry? Let him sing psalms” (James 5:13). Fuglene gjør dette ustanselig og det synes umulig å trekke noen annen konklusjon enn at de er glade mens de gjør det. Vandrer du nær sprintens rede, vil du finne at de også har måter å uttrykke forakt på. Killdeeren (killdeer) nøler heller ikke med å uttrykke overilt misnøye overfor dem som trår inn i deres domene, men disse skal ikke forveksles med sanger. De sangende fuglene er et vakkert maleri av Guds hellige og hans engler.

Hvor lite kunnskap om himmelen ligger til vår forståelse. Scenene av himlene som beskrives og settes fram for oss i Revelations kan knapt bringe våre endelige sinn inn i dets uendelige rike. Én dimensjon vi kan knytte oss til er at det er et sted fylt av sang. Liten under, for det er det krystallinske endemålet for de fornøyde og gledefylte Guds hellige, og der skal de synge en ny sang. Nesten hver scene ved tronen i Revelations kjennetegnes av en eller annen dimensjon av prisning. “And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God” (Ps 40:3). På 22 anledninger gjentar Skriften uttrykket, I will sing.

Det er fuglenes natur å synge. Det er deres våkne tanke når morgenen farger himmelen, og det flyter fra dem som en kilde. Ikke alle deres sanger er like. Noen er utsøkte i varighet, takt og tonehøyde, mens andre er enkle. Noen kvitrer bare med et lyst hjerte. Rødhaken åpner koret tidlig om våren, men hans sang blir snart overgått i skjønnhet av sangspurven og igjen av rosebrystet grosbeak. Skrikens sang overgår dem alle i varighet og livfullhet. Kanarifuglen synger i et bur, mens nattergalen synger i mørket. Rødhakene synger i regnet. Buntings fyller inn den varme delen av dagen når andre fugler tier. Så mangfoldig som deres sang kan være, bryter de alle felles ut i overstrømmende glede. Det er her de skal lære oss.

“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord” (Eph 5:19). Kristi komme ble markert av den englehjærens kunngjøring om fred og velvilje mot menneskene. Alle som bærer Hans navn må bringe det samme budskap. I Johannes 4 treffer vi scenen ved Jacobs brønn, hvor Kristus ber kvinnen om å gi ham å drikke. Hennes svar synes å bære et skjær av bitterhet. “Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” Selv om hun anså seg som en from person og villig fulgte ham inn i religiøs samtale, hadde hun ingen sang. Som brønnen de taler om, var vannet hennes begravd dypt under overflaten, og hvor arbeidskrevende var ikke forsøket på å bringe det fram. Kristus tilbyr et annet alternativ. “But the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

Kristi brønn er en artesisk kilde. Man trenger verken krukke eller arbeid for å hente den, for den spruter fram rikelig av seg selv. Mens Kristus sannsynligvis taler om Ånden som i John 7:38, kan dette like gjerne gjelde et glede-fylt hjerte. Hva er en mer passende utstrømming å flyte fra en Kristus-inspirert kilde enn geisten av en sang? “Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart” (Is 65:14). Nå burde alt dette forekomme både forståelig og lett å gjøre, men akk, vi finner at vi har en konstant og vedvarende motstander som søker å hindre vår sang. Vi er ikke ukjent med hans knep...

Synd. Ikke alle fugler synger. Det finnes noen hvis skikkelse er svart som synd. Disse synes bare å skrike og hyle og er intet forbilde for Guds hellige å etterligne. Den plaprende støyen vi hører fra mange forbipasserende kjøretøyer paralleller ganske sikkert sangene til slike fordervede fugler. “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird” (Rev 18:2). Disse overflodsdyr er de falne ånder, fuglene som venter på å sluke frøet sådd ved veien. Av slike er de verdiløse svartfuglene, stjernene og gracklene. Kråkene viser seg også ved veikanten og eter råtnende lik. Ofte finner du dem i stort antall og eter seg på kornet bonden omhyggelig plantet for seg selv. Så gjør den egoistiske sjelen i sitt jag etter lykke, eter seg frydefullt på en annens ulykke og utnytter deres synd. Han bærer ingen sang, for hans dag er stadig skyggelagt av de andres misgjerninger som krysser hans vei.

Forsømmelse. Cowbird er også svart (hunnen er brun/grå). Hun vil bli funnet sittende på et høyt utkikkspunkt, skamløst kalle på sine elskere med sin skarpe skriking. Så har hun frimodigheten til å legge sitt egg i en annen fugls rede, og tvinger dem til å oppfostre hennes avkom. Dette er utvilsomt et treffende emblem for et godt antall kvinner i vår tid. Selv om de er rettferdiggjort av omstendighetene, bryr disse kvinnene seg ikke om sine egne, men er produkter av forsømmelse. De har ingen vuggesang å dele med sine små, for de har ledsaget dem til en annens rede mens tankene deres er opptatt av arbeid og gjøremål. “But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts” (Ps 22:9). Det er ingen tvil om at den syngende mor kan innprente rikelige sanger i sin spedbarn og legge grunnlaget for et lykkelig og håpsfylt liv. Mens vi kan vise barmhjertighet mot en kvinne i nød, bærer den moderne kvinnes store sang akkorder som kun er dissonante og melankolske. Dette er tette brønner lik de brønnene Isak fant ved sin tilbakekomst til Gerar. Filisterne “had filled them with earth” (Gen 26:15). Slik går det i de åndelig forsømmede hjem hos mange familier i dag, som fyller timeplanene sine så fulle av jordiske forpliktelser at de ikke har tid til å tilbringe en time i sang sammen. Hvis fuglene sluttet å synge, ville de engang merke det?

Ungratitude. Finn en sjel badet i utakknemlighet, og du vil finne en sjel uten sang. Hvis kanarifuglen skulle nekte å synge i fangenskap, ville få av oss noen gang ha hørt hans muntre melodi. “We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD’S song in a strange land?” (Ps 137:2-4). Guds folk var blitt instruert av Jeremiah å bygge hus, plante hager og oppdra familier. “… And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace” (Jer. 29:5-7). Men de kunne ikke se verdien i det. Med deres øyne festet ved den dystre scenen rundt dem, mistet de sin sang. Israel hadde i sin historie en rik tradisjon av sang. Deres sang brøt ut ved overgangen av Rødehavet i Jehosjafats dager og hadde vært kjent for å beseire hærer. Jordisk ubehag er ingen unnskyldning for å holde tilbake takknemlighet, for vår Gud rår, og vi er Hans barn. Slik var forholdene i filipperfangeskapet hvor to fangefugler, Paulus og Silas, åpnet konserten ved midnatt og rystet korridorene med sin frydefulle sang.

Når vi åpner munnene våre og strekker våre vokaler i pris, utøver vi Guds nåde. Vi slutter oss til det trofaste koret ved siden av Mirjam, Debora og Hanna, og blander oss harmonisk med Moses, David, Paulus og Barnabas. Om kvelden synger vi med vår Herre og Hans disipler etter måltidet, og med hærer av engler “giving glory to God in the highest.” Hvis ikke det er nok, bør vi kanskje vurdere å stå opp i tidlig gry og synge med de utallige skarer av våre fjærkledde venner som er takknemlige for Guds kjærlige forsyn. “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord … And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men” (Col 3:16, 23).

Our Father’s world is a world unspoiled by human invention and intervention. While sin and technology have warped and stolen many lovely things from the human race, there abide still a few that remain unmarred by civilization. Little children in the fresh innocence of their unsoiled morning top the ranks as a bit of heaven on earth and call all observers heavenward. Another is the fowl of the air as prescribed in Genesis. Paul pleaded with the Corinthian church, “Doth not nature itself teach you?” We are exhorted to consider the lilies, the ravens, and the grass of the field. Each of these bears a significant dimension of the eternal God in their existence and gives us definition to their Creator. Perhaps all of nature can give us snapshots into heavenly places if we had the time and eyes to observe it.

Birds hold a unique place in God’s creation, for their sphere is in the heavens. Man may mount on the wings of a plane and evade the lower earth for a few hours, but the heavens will never be a place of his common dominion. The birds are a picture of a heavenly race, for they are at home there. They are a natural representation of the saints and angels of God and so we do well to give them due attention. While there may be dozens of lessons to be drawn from these vessels of grace and beauty, one of the most prominent and outstanding virtues will be observed in the song that they raise. Many animals dwelling on the earth are virtually mute. Of the ones that do speak, it is often to threaten or express complaint. “Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?” (Job 6:5). When they are happy and content, they have no message to convey. The dog barks at an intruder to drive him away, while the cat mews for attention. They speak when they are threatened or dissatisfied, in fear or in pain. Similarly, the earthly human shares its nature with the mammals of the field.

Birds are diverse. They exercise their joyous vocals so much that they are the epitome of happiness. The expression “happy as a lark” is so common a term that it is used by people who have never even ventured to the meadow to see or hear a lark. While some may inform us that these songs are mere mating calls and have little to do with their feelings, we cannot escape the inner conviction that, whether mating or not, these birds delight in bearing a jubilant expression of joy and we do well to let them teach us. “Is any merry? Let him sing psalms” (James 5:13). The birds do this incessantly and it seems impossible to draw any other conclusion but that they are happy while doing so. Wander near the nest of a swallow and you will find that they have ways of expressing depreciation as well. The killdeer also has no qualms with expressing rash disfavor to those who intrude their domain, but these are not to be mistaken as songs. The singing birds are a beautiful painted picture of the saints and angels of God.

How little knowledge of heaven is committed to our understanding. The scenes of heavens described and laid out before us in Revelations can hardly bring our finite minds into its infinite realm. One dimension that we can connect with is that it is a place filled with singing. Little wonder, for it is the culminating end of the contented and joy-filled saints of God, and there they will sing a new song. Nearly every scene at the throne in Revelations is marked by some dimension of praise. “And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God” (Ps 40:3). On 22 occasions, the Scriptures reiterate the phrase, I will sing.

It is the nature of the birds to sing. It is their waking thought as morning guilds the sky, and it flows from within them like a fountain. Not all of their songs are alike. Some are elaborate in their duration, meter, and pitch, while others are plain. Some merely chirp with a merry heart. The robin opens up the choir in early spring, but his song is soon surpassed in beauty by the song sparrow and again by the rose-breasted grosbeak. The song of the wren trumps them all for longevity and vibrancy. The canary sings in a cage, while the nightingale sings in the dark. The robins sing in the rain. The buntings fill in the heat of the day when other birds are silent. As diverse as their song may be, they all commonly burst forth in exuberant happiness. It is here that they shall instruct us.

“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord” (Eph 5:19). The advent of Christ was marked by the angelic host announcing peace and goodwill toward men. All those who will bear His name must deliver the same tidings. In John 4, we happen upon the scene at Jacob’s well, where Christ asks the woman for a drink. Her reply seems to bear a tinge of bitterness. “Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” Though she esteemed herself as a spiritual person and willingly followed Him into religious discourse, she had no song. Like the well that they speak over, her water was buried deep below the surface and how laborious the effort to bring it forth. Christ offers another alternative. “But the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

The well of Christ is an artesian well. One needs neither pitcher nor labor to draw it out, for it spews forth abundantly on its own accord. While Christ is probably speaking of the Spirit as in John 7:38, surely this may be just as applicable to a joy-laden heart. What is a more apt outpouring to flow from a Christ-inspired wellspring than the rapture of a song? “Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart” (Is 65:14). Now this should all seem plain enough to understand and easy enough to do but, alas, we find we have a constant and persistent adversary who seeks to thwart our song. We are not unaware of his devices...

Sin. Not all birds sing. There are some whose visage is black as sin. These only seem to screech and scream and are no example for the saints of God to emulate. The babbling noise we hear emanating from many passing vehicles certainly parallels the songs of such foul fowl. “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird” (Rev 18:2). These abundant creatures are the fallen spirits, the fowls waiting to devour the seed sown by the wayside. Of such are the worthless blackbirds, starlings, and grackles. The crows show themselves also at the roadside, feeding on rotting carcasses. Often you will find them in large numbers feeding themselves on the corn the farmer painstakingly planted for himself. So transgresses the selfish soul in his pursuit of happiness, feeding gleefully on the calamity of another and exploiting their sin. He bears no song, for his day is constantly clouded by the misdeeds of others who cross his path.

Neglect. The cowbird is also black (the female is brown/gray). She will be found sitting on a high vantage, shamelessly calling to her lovers by her shrill screeching. She then has the audacity to lay her egg in another bird’s nest, forcing them to raise her offspring. This is certainly a fitting emblem for a good number of females in our day. Though justified by circumstances, these women care not for their own, but are products of neglect. They have no lullaby to share with their young, for they have escorted them to the nest of another while her mind is preoccupied with work and business. “But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts” (Ps 22:9). No doubt that the singing mother can implant copious songs in her infant and set the stage for a happy and hope-filled life. While we may show mercy to a woman in dire circumstances, the major song of modern women bears chords that are but dissident and melancholy. These are stopped-up wells like unto the wells that Isaac found upon his return to Gerar. The Philistines “had filled them with earth” (Gen 26:15). So run the spiritually neglected homes of many families today, who pack their schedules so full of earthly commitments that they have no time to spend an hour in song together. If the birds stopped singing, would they even notice?

Ingratitude. Find a soul bathed in unthankfulness, and you will find a soul without a song. If the canary were to refuse to sing in captivity, few of us would ever have heard his rollicking melody. “We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD’S song in a strange land?” (Ps 137:2-4). God’s people had been instructed by Jeremiah to build houses, plant gardens, and raise families. “… And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace” (Jer. 29:5-7). But they could see no worth in it. With their eyes fixed upon the dismal scene around them, they lost their song. Israel had within its history a rich tradition of song. Their singing erupted at the passage of the Red Sea in the days of Jehoshaphat and had been known to defeat armies. Earthly discomfort is no excuse to withhold gratitude, for our God reigns, and we are His children. Such were the conditions of the Philippian prison where two jailbirds, Paul and Silas, opened the concert at midnight and rocked the corridors with their joyful singing.

When we open our mouths and stretch our vocals in praise, we enact the grace of God. We join the faithful choir alongside Miriam, Deborah, and Hannah, and blend harmoniously with Moses, David, Paul, and Barnabas. At evening, we sing with our Lord and His disciples after supper, and with legions of angels “giving glory to God in the highest.” If that isn’t enough, perhaps we should consider rising at early dawn and singing with the innumerable hosts of our feathered friends who are thankful for God’s loving providence. “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord … And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men” (Col 3:16, 23).

Onze hemelse Vader’s wereld is een wereld onbescha­digd door menselijke uitvindingen en ingrepen. Terwijl zonde en techniek veel lieflijke dingen van het menselijke ras hebben vervormd en weggenomen, blijven er toch enkelen over die onaangetast door de beschaving gebleven zijn. Kleine kinderen in de frisse onschuld van hun ongevlekte ochtend staan bovenaan als een stukje hemel op aarde en roepen alle toeschouwers hemelwaarts. Een ander zijn de gevleugelde vogels zoals voorgeschreven in Genesis. Paulus smeekte de gemeente te Korinthe: “Doth not nature itself teach you?” Ons wordt aangemoedigd de leliën, de raven en het gras des velds te overwegen. Elk van deze draagt een belangrijke dimensie van de eeuwige God in zijn bestaan en geeft ons een omschrijving van hun Schepper. Misschien kan de hele natuur ons kiekjes geven van hemelse plaatsen als we er tijd en ogen voor hadden om haar te observeren.

Vogels hebben een unieke plaats in Gods schepping, want hun sfeer is in de hemelen. De mens kan op de vleugels van een vliegtuig stijgen en de lagere aarde voor een paar uur ontlopen, maar de hemelen zullen nooit een plaats van zijn gewone heerschappij zijn. De vogels zijn een beeld van een hemels ras, want zij zijn daar thuis. Zij zijn een natuurlijke voorstelling van de heiligen en engelen van God en dus doen wij er goed aan hen de nodige aandacht te geven. Hoewel er tientallen lessen uit deze vaten van genade en schoonheid getrokken kunnen worden, zal een van de meest prominente en opvallende deugd te zien zijn in het lied dat zij opheffen. Veel dieren die op aarde wonen zijn vrijwel muisstil. Van degenen die wel spreken, is het vaak om te dreigen of klacht te uiten. “Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?” (Job 6:5). Wanneer zij blij en tevreden zijn, hebben zij geen boodschap over te brengen. De hond blaft een indringer weg, terwijl de kat miauwt om aandacht. Zij spreken wanneer zij bedreigd of ontevreden zijn, in angst of pijn. Evenzo deelt de aardse mens zijn natuur met de zoogdieren des velds.

Vogels zijn divers. Ze oefenen hun vreugdevolle zang zo vaak dat zij het toonbeeld van geluk zijn. De uitdrukking “happy as a lark” is zo algemeen geworden dat mensen hem gebruiken die nooit de wei zijn binnengestapt om een leeuwerik te zien of te horen. Hoewel sommigen ons kunnen vertellen dat deze liederen louter paringsroepen zijn en weinig met hun gevoelens te maken hebben, kunnen we niet ontsnappen aan de innerlijke overtuiging dat, al is het ook om te paren, deze vogels er genoegen in hebben een juichende uitdrukking van blijdschap te laten horen en dat wij er goed aan doen hen dat te laten onderwijzen. “Is any merry? Let him sing psalms” (James 5:13). De vogels doen dit onophoudelijk en het lijkt onmogelijk een andere conclusie te trekken dan dat zij blij zijn terwijl zij dit doen. Wandel dicht bij het nest van een zwaluw en je zult merken dat zij ook manieren hebben om minachting uit te drukken. De killdeer aarzelt ook niet om rash afkeuring te uiten jegens hen die hun domein binnendringen, maar deze mogen niet verward worden met zang. De zingende vogels zijn een prachtig geschilderd beeld van de heiligen en engelen van God.

Hoe weinig kennis van de hemel is aan ons begrip toevertrouwd. De taferelen van de hemelen beschreven en voor ons uitgespreid in Revelations kunnen onze eindige geest nauwelijks in haar oneindige rijk brengen. Één dimensie waarmee we ons kunnen verbinden is dat het een plaats vol gezang is. Geen wonder, want het is het culminerende einde van de tevreden en vreugdevolle heiligen van God, en daar zullen zij een nieuw lied zingen. Bijna elk tafereel bij de troon in Revelations wordt gemarkeerd door een of andere dimensie van lofprijzing. “And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God” (Ps 40:3). Bij 22 gelegenheden herhaalt de Schrift de frase, I will sing.

Het is de aard van de vogels te zingen. Het is hun ontwakende gedachte als de morgen de lucht kleurt, en het vloeit uit hen als een fontein. Niet al hun liederen zijn hetzelfde. Sommige zijn uitgebreid in duur, maat en toonhoogte, terwijl andere eenvoudig zijn. Sommigen tjirpen slechts met een vrolijk hart. De roodborst opent het koor in het vroege voorjaar, maar zijn lied wordt spoedig overtroffen in schoonheid door de song sparrow en opnieuw door de rose-breasted grosbeak. Het lied van de winterkoning overtreft ze allen in lengte en levendigheid. De kanarie zingt in een kooi, terwijl de nachtegaal in het duister zingt. De roodborsten zingen in de regen. De buntings vullen de warmte van de dag wanneer andere vogels zwijgen. Hoe divers hun zang ook mag zijn, zij barsten allen gemeenlijk naar buiten in uitbundige vrolijkheid. Het is hier dat zij ons zullen onderwijzen.

“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord” (Eph 5:19). De komst van Christus werd gekenmerkt door het engelenleger dat vrede en goede wil jegens de mensen aankondigde. Allen die Zijn naam zullen dragen moeten hetzelfde bericht brengen. In John 4 komen we bij de put van Jacob, waar Christus de vrouw om een drinkwater vraagt. Haar antwoord lijkt een vleugje bitterheid te dragen. “Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” Hoewel zij zichzelf als een geestelijk persoon beschouwde en bereidwillig met Hem in religieuze discussie trad, had zij geen lied. Zoals de put waarover zij spreken, lag haar water diep onder het oppervlak en hoe arbeidsintensief de inspanning om het naar boven te halen. Christus biedt een ander alternatief. “But the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

De put van Christus is een artesische bron. Men heeft noch kruik noch arbeid nodig om haar op te diepen, want zij borrelt overvloedig uit zichzelf voort. Terwijl Christus waarschijnlijk spreekt over de Geest zoals in John 7:38, zou dit zeker even toepasselijk kunnen zijn op een van vreugde gevulde hart. Wat is een meer passende uitstroming om uit een door Christus geïnspireerde bron te vloeien dan de vervoering van een lied? “Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart” (Is 65:14). Dit zou nu allemaal duidelijk genoeg moeten zijn om te begrijpen en gemakkelijk genoeg om te doen maar, helaas, wij vinden dat we een voortdurende en hardnekkige tegenstander hebben die onze zang wil dwarsbomen. Wij zijn ons niet onbekend met zijn listen...

Zonde. Niet alle vogels zingen. Er zijn enkelen wier voorkomen zwart is als zonde. Deze lijken slechts te krijsen en te schreeuwen en zijn geen voorbeeld voor de heiligen van God om na te volgen. Het babbelende geluid dat we horen uit veel passerende voertuigen parallelleert zeker de liederen van zulke vuile vogels. “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird” (Rev 18:2). Deze overvloedige wezens zijn de gevallen geesten, de vogels die klaarstaan om het zaad dat langs de weg gezaaid is te verslinden. Van zulke zijn de waardeloze kauwen, spreeuwen en grackles. De raven tonen zich ook langs de weg, etend van rottende kadavers. Vaak vindt men hen in grote aantallen, zich voedend met het graan dat de boer met pijn en moeite voor zichzelf had geplant. Zo overtreden de egoïstische zielen in hun jacht op geluk, zich vrolijk voedend met het ongeluk van een ander en hun zonde uitbuitend. Zij hebben geen lied, want hun dag is voortdurend verduisterd door de wandaden van anderen die hun pad kruisen.

Verwaarlozing. De koevogel is ook zwart (het vrouwtje is bruin/grijs). Zij zal op een hoog uitkijkpunt zitten, schaamteloos haar geliefden roepend met haar schelle geschreeuw. Daarna heeft zij de brutaliteit haar ei in het nest van een andere vogel te leggen, en hen te dwingen haar jongen groot te brengen. Dit is zeker een passend embleem voor een aanzienlijk aantal vrouwen van onze tijd. Hoewel gerechtvaardigd door omstandigheden, zorgen deze vrouwen niet voor hun eigen kinderen, maar zijn producten van verwaarlozing. Zij hebben geen wiegelied om met hun jong te delen, want zij hebben hen naar het nest van een ander begeleid terwijl haar geest bezet is met werk en zaken. “But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts” (Ps 22:9). Ongetwijfeld kan de zingende moeder overvloedige liederen in haar kind planten en het toneel zetten voor een gelukkig en hoopvol leven. Terwijl we barmhartigheid kunnen tonen aan een vrouw in benarde omstandigheden, draagt het grote lied van moderne vrouwen akkoorden die slechts dissonant en melancholiek zijn. Dit zijn verstopt geraakte bronnen zoals de putten die Isaac vond bij zijn terugkeer naar Gerar. De Filistijnen “had filled them with earth” (Gen 26:15). Zo lopen de geestelijk verwaarloosde huizen van vele gezinnen vandaag, die hun schema’s zo volstoppen met aardse verplichtingen dat zij geen tijd hebben om een uur samen in zang door te brengen. Als de vogels zouden stoppen met zingen, zouden zij het dan zelfs merken?

Ondankbaarheid. Vind een ziel badend in ondankbaarheid, en je vindt een ziel zonder lied. Als de kanarie weigerde te zingen in gevangenschap, zouden we weinigen van ons ooit zijn uitbundige melodie hebben gehoord. “We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD’S song in a strange land?” (Ps 137:2-4). Gods volk was door Jeremiah geïnstrueerd huizen te bouwen, tuinen te planten en gezinnen op te voeden. “… And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace” (Jer. 29:5-7). Maar zij zagen er geen waarde in. Met hun ogen gericht op het sombere tafereel om hen heen, verloren zij hun lied. Israël had binnen zijn geschiedenis een rijke traditie van gezang. Hun gezang barstte los bij de doortocht van de Rode Zee in de dagen van Jehoshaphat en had bekendheid om legers te verslaan. Aardse ongemakken zijn geen excuus om dankbaarheid achter te houden, want onze God regeert, en wij zijn Zijn kinderen. Zo waren de omstandigheden in de gevangenis van Filippi waar twee gevangenen, Paulus en Silas, het concert om middernacht openden en de gangen deed daveren met hun vreugdevolle gezang.

Wanneer wij onze monden openen en onze stemmen strekken in lof, voeren wij de genade van God uit. Wij voegen ons bij het getrouwe koor naast Mirjam, Debora en Hanna, en mengen ons harmonieus met Mozes, David, Paulus en Barnabas. Des avonds zingen wij met onze Heer en Zijn discipelen na het avondmaal, en met legers engelen die “giving glory to God in the highest.” Als dat nog niet genoeg is, zouden we misschien overwegen bij het vroege dageraad op te staan en te zingen met de ontelbare scharen van onze gevleugelde vrienden die dankbaar zijn voor Gods liefdevolle voorzienigheid. “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord … And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men” (Col 3:16, 23).
